1	# Two env files (split in #209 so app Settings can run extra="forbid"):
2	#   .env      — infra/compose only: POSTGRES_* (+ VITE_* for the frontend). This is
3	#               the file compose auto-substitutes ${...} from. setup.sh creates it
4	#               from .env.example. NOT loaded into the api/worker containers.
5	#   .env.app  — app config (DATABASE_URL, AZURE_*, AUTH_DEV_BYPASS, SECRET_STORE, …):
6	#               only keys the app's Settings recognizes. Loaded into api/worker/
7	#               migrate via env_file below; created from .env.app.example.
8	# DATABASE_URL is identical across migrate/api/worker. Postgres user/password/db
9	# carry NO embedded defaults — they come from .env or the shell. The `:?` on the
10	# canonical postgres block below makes compose fail fast if any is unset, rather
11	# than baking credentials into the file.
12	x-database-url: &database-url "REDACTED"
13	
14	services:
15	  postgres:
16	    image: postgres:16-alpine
17	    restart: unless-stopped
18	    environment:
19	      POSTGRES_USER: "${POSTGRES_USER:?set POSTGRES_USER in .env}"
20	      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}"
21	      POSTGRES_DB: "${POSTGRES_DB:?set POSTGRES_DB in .env}"
22	    ports:
23	      - "5432:5432"
24	    volumes:
25	      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
26	    healthcheck:
27	      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U ${POSTGRES_USER}"]
28	      interval: 5s
29	      timeout: 3s
30	      retries: 10
31	
32	  redis:
33	    image: redis:7-alpine
34	    restart: unless-stopped
35	    ports:
36	      - "6379:6379"
37	    healthcheck:
38	      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
39	      interval: 5s
40	      timeout: 3s
41	      retries: 10
42	
43	  # One-shot: applies Alembic migrations then exits 0. api/worker wait on it via
44	  # service_completed_successfully so `docker compose up` never serves an
45	  # un-migrated schema (#156). Mirrors setup.sh's `cd backend && alembic ...`
46	  # because alembic.ini's script_location is relative to backend/.
47	  migrate:
48	    build:
49	      context: .
50	      dockerfile: backend/Dockerfile
51	    restart: "no"
52	    command: sh -c "cd backend && alembic upgrade head"
53	    env_file:
54	      - path: .env.app
55	        required: false
56	    environment:
57	      DATABASE_URL: *database-url
58	    volumes:
59	      - ./backend:/workspace/backend
60	    depends_on:
61	      postgres:
62	        condition: service_healthy
63	
64	  # FastAPI + Celery share one image (backend/Dockerfile, conda env `dataq`).
65	  # DATABASE_URL / REDIS_URL are overridden here to the in-network service
66	  # hostnames (the .env defaults point at localhost for host-side dev).
67	  api:
68	    build:
69	      context: .
70	      dockerfile: backend/Dockerfile
71	    restart: unless-stopped
72	    command: uvicorn backend.app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --reload
73	    ports:
74	      - "8000:8000"
75	    env_file:
76	      - path: .env.app
77	        required: false
78	    environment:
79	      DATABASE_URL: *database-url
80	      REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379/0
81	      # Shared across api + worker so a credential the API writes at runtime is
82	      # readable by connection-driven worker runs (#86). Dev only — plaintext in
83	      # Redis. NOTE: in redis mode KV_SECRET_* env vars are NOT consulted (that's
84	      # `env` mode); set SECRET_STORE=env if you rely on env-provided creds.
85	      SECRET_STORE: ${SECRET_STORE:-redis}
86	    volumes:
87	      # Bind-mount source for hot reload; the conda env in the image is untouched.
88	      - ./backend:/workspace/backend
89	    depends_on:
90	      postgres:
91	        condition: service_healthy
92	      redis:
93	        condition: service_healthy
94	      migrate:
95	        condition: service_completed_successfully
96	
97	  worker:
98	    build:
99	      context: .
100	      dockerfile: backend/Dockerfile
101	    restart: unless-stopped
102	    # -B runs celery-beat embedded in the worker (the #171 orchestration polling
103	    # schedule). Fine for the single-worker dev stack; prod runs a separate beat.
104	    command: celery -A backend.app.worker.celery_app worker -B --loglevel=INFO
105	    env_file:
106	      - path: .env.app
107	        required: false
108	    environment:
109	      DATABASE_URL: *database-url
110	      REDIS_URL: redis://redis:6379/0
111	      # Must match the api service so secrets the API writes are visible here (#86).
112	      SECRET_STORE: ${SECRET_STORE:-redis}
113	    volumes:
114	      - ./backend:/workspace/backend
115	    depends_on:
116	      postgres:
117	        condition: service_healthy
118	      redis:
119	        condition: service_healthy
120	      migrate:
121	        condition: service_completed_successfully
122	
123	  # React/Vite dev server. corepack pins pnpm from package.json's packageManager.
124	  # node_modules is an anonymous volume so the host's (possibly macOS-built) copy
125	  # doesn't clobber the container's. pnpm's ~300MB content-addressable store is
126	  # relocated to /pnpm-store (OUTSIDE the ./frontend bind) and held in its own
127	  # volume — so nothing leaks into, or creates an empty mountpoint under, the host
128	  # working tree. The browser loads from localhost:3000 and the Vite proxy forwards
129	  # /api + /mcp to the api service over the compose network.
130	  frontend:
131	    image: node:24-alpine
132	    restart: unless-stopped
133	    working_dir: /app
134	    command: sh -c "corepack enable && pnpm config set store-dir /pnpm-store && pnpm install && pnpm dev --host"
135	    environment:
136	      VITE_API_PROXY_TARGET: http://api:8000
137	      # Pass the client-side auth vars into the Vite dev server. Only VITE_*
138	      # vars are forwarded (DB/secret env stays out of the node container).
139	      # Substituted from the project .env; dev-bypass defaults on for local dev.
140	      VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS: ${VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS:-true}
141	      VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID: ${VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID:-}
142	      VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID: ${VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID:-}
143	      VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID: ${VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID:-}
144	      VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE: ${VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE:-user_impersonation}
145	    ports:
146	      - "3000:3000"
147	    volumes:
148	      - ./frontend:/app
149	      - /app/node_modules
150	      - pnpm-store:/pnpm-store
151	    depends_on:
152	      - api
153

156	  pnpm-store:

Here's the current Docker state, and there's a meaningful split I want to confirm before deleting anything:

**Clearly DataQ compose stack** (safe to remove — rebuildable from the repo):
- Containers: `dataq-{frontend,worker,api,migrate,postgres,redis}-1`
- Images: `dataq-api`, `dataq-worker`, `dataq-migrate`
- Volumes: `dataq_postgres_data` (dev seed data), `dataq_pnpm-store`
- Network: `dataq_default`

**DataQ-harness demo images** (the ADR 0021 live demo env — large, rebuilt via the harness, not this repo):
- `dataqacr3erlgd.azurecr.io/airflow-dataq` (10 tags, ~443MB–2.18GB each), `.../mockdata`, plus local `airflow-dataq:latest`, `mockdata:latest`

**NOT DataQ — must not touch:**
- `jellyfin` container + image (your media server)
- `docs_default` network (some other project)
- 14 anonymous hex volumes (unknown ownership — some likely jellyfin's)

So a blanket `docker system prune -a --volumes` is off the table — it'd kill jellyfin and the harness images. Two decisions for you:

1	# DataQ — deployment scaffolding
2	
3	Apply-ready Azure deploy scaffolding (Week 7). **Nothing here deploys on its own**
4	— the workflow ([.github/workflows/deploy.yml](../.github/workflows/deploy.yml)) is
5	`workflow_dispatch`-only until the Azure resources exist and the secrets/vars
6	below are set. This documents what to provision and how the pieces fit.
7	
8	Azure is **one** deploy target behind the app's seams (ADR 0010/0013) — the
9	manifests here are infra config, not business logic. No Azure resource names are
10	hardcoded in app code; they live only as workflow `vars`/`secrets`.
11	
12	## Topology
13	
14	```
15	Browser ─► Azure Static Web App (frontend/dist)
16	              │  /api/* proxied to the linked backend (same-origin → no CORS)
17	              ▼
18	        Azure Container Apps
19	          • dataq-api     (FastAPI image, external ingress :8000)
20	          • dataq-worker  (same image, `celery -A ... worker` + beat)
21	          • dataq-migrate (Container Apps Job: `alembic upgrade head`)
22	              │
23	              ├─► Azure Database for PostgreSQL (DATABASE_URL)
24	              ├─► Azure Cache for Redis        (REDIS_URL)
25	              ├─► Azure Key Vault              (SECRET_STORE=azure_key_vault, managed identity)
26	              └─► Application Insights         (APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING)
27	        Azure Container Registry (ACR) — holds the backend image
28	```
29	
30	Both api + worker run the **same** image ([backend/Dockerfile](../backend/Dockerfile),
31	build context = repo root). The frontend is built and uploaded to SWA by the
32	workflow (the [frontend/Dockerfile](../frontend/Dockerfile) is the container
33	alternative — only needed if you run the UI on Container Apps instead of SWA).
34	
35	## One-time provisioning
36	
37	The datasource + compute infra is stood up by the external Terraform harness
38	(ADR 0021) — see `HARNESS_TODO.md`. Beyond that, this app needs:
39	
40	1. **ACR** + an **ACA environment** + the three apps/job above. The api/worker run
41	   `uvicorn …` / `celery …`; the migrate **job** runs `alembic upgrade head`.
42	2. **Managed identity** on the api + worker apps with **Key Vault Secrets User**
43	   on the vault (so `DefaultAzureCredential` resolves `SECRET_STORE=azure_key_vault`).
44	3. **App env**: set the keys in [deploy/.env.app.prod.example](.env.app.prod.example)
45	   on the api + worker apps. Secret values (DB/Redis URL, App Insights) are Key
46	   Vault-backed Container Apps secrets — never literals.
47	4. **SWA linked backend**: link the `dataq-api` Container App as the SWA backend so
48	   `/api/*` is proxied same-origin (then `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS` can stay empty). If
49	   instead the SPA calls the API cross-origin, set `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS` to the SWA
50	   origin (the FastAPI CORS middleware turns on only when it's non-empty).
51	5. **Azure Monitor → ADF webhook** alert rule (Week-7 task) — needs the deployed
52	   API URL; configure after the first deploy.
53	
54	## GitHub config the workflow reads
55	
56	Set under repo **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**, and add a
57	federated credential for OIDC login (subject = this repo's `production`
58	environment).
59	
60	**Secrets:** `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID`
61	(OIDC app registration), `AZURE_STATIC_WEB_APPS_API_TOKEN`.
62	
63	**Variables:** `ACR_NAME`, `ACR_LOGIN_SERVER`, `AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP`,
64	`API_APP_NAME`, `WORKER_APP_NAME`, `MIGRATE_JOB_NAME`, and the non-secret
65	`VITE_AZURE_*` build values.
66	
67	## Going live
68	
69	1. Provision the resources + set the secrets/vars above.
70	2. Run the **Deploy** workflow manually (`workflow_dispatch`) to validate end-to-end.
71	3. To deploy on every merge, uncomment the `push: branches: [main]` trigger in
72	   the workflow.
73	
74	Migrations are additive/backward-compatible (CLAUDE.md), so the workflow runs
75	`alembic upgrade head` **before** rolling the apps — the running old code
76	tolerates the new schema. (This is exactly the dev-DB step that, when skipped,
77	500s the checks endpoint after a schema-adding deploy.)
78

1	name: Deploy
2	
3	# Manual-only for now (workflow_dispatch): apply-ready scaffolding that never
4	# fires on its own until the Azure resources exist + secrets/vars are set. Once
5	# the infra is provisioned (see deploy/README.md), flip on the push trigger:
6	#   push:
7	#     branches: [main]
8	on:
9	  workflow_dispatch:
10	    inputs:
11	      image_tag:
12	        description: "Image tag to build + deploy"
13	        default: "latest"
14	
15	concurrency:
16	  group: deploy-production
17	  cancel-in-progress: false
18	
19	# OIDC federated login to Azure (no stored client secret). The federated cred +
20	# the listed vars/secrets must be configured first — see deploy/README.md.
21	permissions:
22	  id-token: write
23	  contents: read
24	
25	env:
26	  IMAGE: ${{ vars.ACR_LOGIN_SERVER }}/dataq-backend:${{ inputs.image_tag }}
27	
28	jobs:
29	  backend:
30	    name: Backend — build, migrate, deploy (API + worker)
31	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
32	    environment: production
33	    steps:
34	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
35	
36	      - name: Azure login (OIDC)
37	        uses: azure/login@v2
38	        with:
39	          client-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
40	          tenant-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
41	          subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
42	
43	      - name: Build + push backend image to ACR
44	        run: |
45	          az acr login --name "${{ vars.ACR_NAME }}"
46	          docker build -f backend/Dockerfile -t "$IMAGE" .
47	          docker push "$IMAGE"
48	
49	      # Migrate BEFORE rolling the app: migrations are additive/backward-compatible
50	      # (CLAUDE.md), so the running old code tolerates the new schema. Runs the
51	      # one-off migrate Container Apps Job (provisioned per deploy/README.md).
52	      # `az containerapp job start` only *starts* the execution and returns, so we
53	      # capture the execution name and poll it to a terminal state — the rollout
54	      # below must not begin until the migration has actually SUCCEEDED, and a
55	      # failed migration must abort the deploy (fail-closed) rather than roll the
56	      # apps onto an un-migrated schema.
57	      - name: Run DB migrations (alembic upgrade head) and wait for success
58	        run: |
59	          set -euo pipefail
60	          exec_name=$(az containerapp job start \
61	            --name "${{ vars.MIGRATE_JOB_NAME }}" \
62	            --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
63	            --image "$IMAGE" \
64	            --query name -o tsv)
65	          echo "Started migration execution: $exec_name"
66	          deadline=$(( SECONDS + 900 ))  # 15-minute cap
67	          while (( SECONDS < deadline )); do
68	            status=$(az containerapp job execution list \
69	              --name "${{ vars.MIGRATE_JOB_NAME }}" \
70	              --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
71	              --query "[?name=='$exec_name'].properties.status | [0]" -o tsv)
72	            echo "migration status: ${status:-<pending>}"
73	            case "$status" in
74	              Succeeded) echo "Migration succeeded."; exit 0 ;;
75	              Failed|Degraded|Stopped) echo "::error::Migration $status — aborting before app rollout."; exit 1 ;;
76	            esac
77	            sleep 10
78	          done
79	          echo "::error::Timed out waiting for migration to complete."; exit 1
80	
81	      - name: Deploy API
82	        run: |
83	          az containerapp update \
84	            --name "${{ vars.API_APP_NAME }}" \
85	            --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
86	            --image "$IMAGE"
87	
88	      - name: Deploy worker
89	        run: |
90	          az containerapp update \
91	            --name "${{ vars.WORKER_APP_NAME }}" \
92	            --resource-group "${{ vars.AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
93	            --image "$IMAGE"
94	
95	  frontend:
96	    name: Frontend — build + deploy to Static Web App
97	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
98	    environment: production
99	    steps:
100	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
101	      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
102	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
103	        with:
104	          node-version: "22"
105	          cache: pnpm
106	          cache-dependency-path: frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml
107	
108	      - name: Build
109	        working-directory: frontend
110	        # VITE_* are inlined at build time. Non-secret azure client/tenant ids
111	        # come from repo vars; never the SPA secret (there is none — MSAL is public).
112	        env:
113	          VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
114	          VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID }}
115	          VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID }}
116	          VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE: ${{ vars.VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE }}
117	          VITE_AUTH_DEV_BYPASS: "false"
118	        run: |
119	          pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
120	          pnpm build
121	
122	      - name: Deploy to Azure Static Web Apps
123	        uses: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy@v1
124	        with:
125	          azure_static_web_apps_api_token: ${{ secrets.AZURE_STATIC_WEB_APPS_API_TOKEN }}
126	          action: upload
127	          app_location: frontend/dist
128	          skip_app_build: true
129

The deploy scaffolding is stale vs. ADR 0023.** The most recent commit (1959b8d) accepted **GHCR** as the registry and explicitly *"supersedes the #379 ACR deploy scaffolding"* — but [deploy.yml](.github/workflows/deploy.yml) and [deploy/README.md](deploy/README.md) still build/push to **ACR** (`az acr login`, `ACR_LOGIN_SERVER`, `ACR_NAME`). That reconciliation is an in-repo task, costs nothing, and should land before we wire up real infra.

| Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL | ✅ Registered | Postgres |
| **Microsoft.Web** | ❌ NotRegistered | Static Web App |
| **Microsoft.KeyVault** | ❌ NotRegistered | secrets |
| **Microsoft.Insights** | ❌ NotRegistered | App Insights |
| **Microsoft.Cache** | ❌ NotRegistered | Redis |

========== versions.tf ==========
# DataQ harness — Terraform / provider version pins.
# Disposable demo env (ADR 0021). Local state backend — state is gitignored,
# never committed (it contains secrets). Pin providers; do not float to latest.

terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.9"

  backend "local" {
    path = "terraform.tfstate"
  }

  required_providers {
    azurerm = {
      source  = "hashicorp/azurerm"
      version = "~> 4.0"
    }
    snowflake = {
      source  = "snowflakedb/snowflake"
      version = "~> 1.0"
    }
    databricks = {
      source  = "databricks/databricks"
      version = "~> 1.50"
    }
    random = {
      source  = "hashicorp/random"
      version = "~> 3.6"
    }
  }
}
========== providers.tf ==========
# Provider blocks. No credentials live in these files — every provider reads
# its secrets from the environment exported by `source ../secrets.sh`:
#   azurerm    -> ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID / ARM_TENANT_ID / ARM_CLIENT_ID / ARM_CLIENT_SECRET
#   snowflake  -> SNOWFLAKE_USER / SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD / SNOWFLAKE_ROLE
#   databricks -> DATABRICKS_HOST / DATABRICKS_TOKEN
# Only non-secret identifiers (org/account name) are passed as variables.

provider "azurerm" {
  features {}
  # subscription_id / tenant_id / client_id / client_secret come from ARM_* env vars.
  #
  # The Terraform SP is Contributor on dataq-rg ONLY — it has no rights at the
  # subscription scope, so it cannot auto-register resource providers. Skip that;
  # the required RPs (Microsoft.Storage, Microsoft.DataFactory) must already be
  # registered on the subscription by an owner (see README).
  resource_provider_registrations = "none"
}

provider "snowflake" {
  # user / password / role come from SNOWFLAKE_* env vars.
  organization_name = var.snowflake_organization_name
  account_name      = var.snowflake_account_name
  # snowflake_table is still a preview resource in the provider.
  preview_features_enabled = ["snowflake_table_resource"]
}

provider "databricks" {
  # host / token come from DATABRICKS_HOST / DATABRICKS_TOKEN env vars.
  # Pin PAT auth explicitly — the ARM_* env vars (for azurerm) would otherwise be
  # picked up as a second, conflicting auth method (Azure SP).
  auth_type = "pat"
}

provider "random" {}
========== main.tf ==========
# Shared data sources + locals.

# The RG already exists (§0); the SP has Contributor on it. Reference, don't create.
data "azurerm_resource_group" "dataq" {
  name = var.azure_resource_group
}

# Random suffix to make the storage-account name globally unique.
resource "random_string" "suffix" {
  length  = 6
  lower   = true
  upper   = false
  numeric = true
  special = false
}

locals {
  common_tags = {
    project = var.project_tag
    managed = "terraform"
    purpose = "dataq-harness"
  }

  # 3-24 lowercase alphanumerics; prefix + 6-char suffix.
  storage_account_name = substr("${var.storage_account_prefix}${random_string.suffix.result}", 0, 24)
}

# Non-secret configuration. Defaults match the §0 prerequisites in HARNESS_TODO.md.
# Override in terraform.tfvars (also gitignored) if you stand up a second env.

variable "project_tag" {
  description = "Tag applied to all cloud resources (secrets.sh convention: project=dataq)."

  default     = "dataq"
}

# ---- Azure ----------------------------------------------------------------

variable "azure_resource_group" {
  description = "Existing RG the Terraform SP has Contributor on (created in §0)."

}

variable "azure_location" {
  description = "Azure region for harness resources."
  type        = string
  default     = "West US 2"
}

variable "postgres_location" {
  description = "Region for the Airflow metadata Postgres. Separate from azure_location because Postgres Flexible Server is offer-restricted in West US 2 for this subscription. Use westus3 (adjacent to West US 2 — low latency the Airflow scheduler needs; centralus's ~30-40ms cross-region latency starved the scheduler's executor loop)."
  type        = string
  default     = "westus3"
}

variable "storage_account_prefix" {
  description = "ADLS Gen2 account name prefix (a random suffix is appended for global uniqueness; 3-24 lowercase alphanumerics total)."
  type        = string

}

# ---- Snowflake ------------------------------------------------------------

========== container_apps.tf ==========
# Container Apps platform — shared host for Airflow (airflow.tf) + the mockdata
# cron Jobs (mockdata_job.tf). Decision 2026-06-26: Airflow on Container Apps
# (not local Docker; ADF Managed Airflow was retired for new instances 2026-01-01).
# Needs subscription RPs: Microsoft.App, Microsoft.OperationalInsights,
# Microsoft.ContainerRegistry (registered by an Owner — see README).

resource "azurerm_log_analytics_workspace" "harness" {
  name                = "dataq-harness-logs"
  location            = var.azure_location
  resource_group_name = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name
  sku                 = "PerGB2018"
  retention_in_days   = var.log_retention_days
  tags                = local.common_tags
}

resource "azurerm_container_app_environment" "harness" {
  name                       = "dataq-harness-cae"
  location                   = var.azure_location
  resource_group_name        = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name
  log_analytics_workspace_id = azurerm_log_analytics_workspace.harness.id
  tags                       = local.common_tags
}

# Holds the mockdata image (+ a custom Airflow image once §3 bakes DAGs in).
# admin_enabled = true so the Job pulls with registry creds — avoids an AcrPull
# role assignment (the Terraform SP is Contributor-only and can't grant roles).
resource "azurerm_container_registry" "harness" {
  name                = "${var.acr_prefix}${random_string.suffix.result}"
  resource_group_name = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name
  location            = var.azure_location
  sku                 = "Basic"
  admin_enabled       = true
  tags                = local.common_tags
}
========== redis.tf ==========
# Redis broker for Airflow CeleryExecutor (§3 / execution scaling).
# Self-hosted Redis container (not Azure Cache for Redis) — cheapest + fastest for a
# disposable harness; the broker is transient (no persistence needed). Internal-only
# TCP ingress so only the Airflow scheduler + workers in this environment reach it.
resource "azurerm_container_app" "redis" {
  name                         = "dataq-harness-redis"
  container_app_environment_id = azurerm_container_app_environment.harness.id
  resource_group_name          = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name
  revision_mode                = "Single"

  ingress {
    external_enabled = false # only reachable within the Container Apps environment
    transport        = "tcp"
    target_port      = 6379
    exposed_port     = 6379
    traffic_weight {
      latest_revision = true
      percentage      = 100
    }
  }

  template {
    min_replicas = 1
    max_replicas = 1
    container {
      name   = "redis"
      image  = "redis:7-alpine" # public image — no registry auth needed
      cpu    = 0.5
      memory = "1Gi"
      # default redis-server entrypoint is fine for a transient broker (RDB snapshots
      # are harmless here; azurerm can't serialize an empty-string arg for --save "").
    }
  }

  tags = local.common_tags
}
========== postgres.tf ==========
# Airflow metadata database — Postgres Flexible Server (Burstable B1ms, cheapest).
# Public access + "allow Azure services" so the Container Apps Environment reaches it
# without VNet integration (fine for a disposable harness). Password generated locally
# (random_password) — never committed; state is gitignored.

resource "random_password" "pg" {
  length  = 24
  special = false # keep the SQLAlchemy URL clean (no %-encoding)
}

resource "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server" "airflow" {
  # "-wus3" (westus3) marker: westus2 is offer-restricted (left a hidden 409 name
  # reservation); centralus worked but its cross-region latency starved the Airflow
  # scheduler. westus3 is adjacent to westus2 → low latency. New marker avoids the
  # centralus server's name on teardown.
  name                          = "dataq-airflow-pg-wus3-${random_string.suffix.result}"
  resource_group_name           = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name
  # Postgres Flexible Server is offer-restricted in West US 2 for this subscription
  # (LocationIsOfferRestricted at apply); centralus is unrestricted. Cross-region from
  # the Container Apps env is fine — public access + allow-Azure-services firewall.
  location                      = var.postgres_location
  version                       = "16"
  administrator_login           = var.postgres_admin_login
  administrator_password        = random_password.pg.result
  sku_name                      = var.postgres_sku
  storage_mb                    = 32768
  auto_grow_enabled             = true
  public_network_access_enabled = true
  zone                          = "1"
  tags                          = local.common_tags
}

resource "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_database" "airflow" {
  name      = "airflow"
  server_id = azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.airflow.id
  collation = "en_US.utf8"
  charset   = "utf8"
}

# start=end=0.0.0.0 is Azure's special "allow access from Azure services" rule.
resource "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_firewall_rule" "azure_services" {
  name             = "allow-azure-services"
  server_id        = azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.airflow.id
  start_ip_address = "0.0.0.0"
  end_ip_address   = "0.0.0.0"
}
========== outputs.tf ==========
# Connection coordinates DataQ's connection editor needs. After `terraform apply`,
# copy these into the harness env / secrets.sh blanks (SNOWFLAKE_*, ADF_FACTORY_NAME).
# None of these are secrets (no passwords/keys/tokens are output).

output "adls_storage_account" {
  description = "ADLS Gen2 account name (DataQ flat-file connection host)."
  value       = azurerm_storage_account.landing.name
}

output "adls_dfs_endpoint" {
  description = "ADLS Gen2 DFS endpoint."
  value       = azurerm_storage_account.landing.primary_dfs_endpoint
}

output "adls_filesystems" {
  description = "Landing-zone filesystems (containers)."
  value       = [for fs in azurerm_storage_data_lake_gen2_filesystem.zones : fs.name]
}

output "adf_factory_name" {
  description = "ADF factory name -> fill ADF_FACTORY_NAME in secrets.sh."
  value       = azurerm_data_factory.dataq.name
}

output "snowflake_database" {
  description = "-> fill SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE in secrets.sh."
  value       = snowflake_database.dataq.name
}

output "snowflake_warehouse" {
  description = "-> fill SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE in secrets.sh."
  value       = snowflake_warehouse.dataq.name
}

output "snowflake_reader_role" {
  description = "Least-privilege role -> switch SNOWFLAKE_ROLE in secrets.sh once tables are loaded."
  value       = snowflake_account_role.reader.name
}

output "snowflake_schemas" {
  description = "Schemas created in the DataQ database."
  value       = [for s in snowflake_schema.schemas : s.name]
}

output "uc_catalog" {
  description = "Unity Catalog catalog name (DataQ UC connection)."
  value       = databricks_catalog.dataq.name
}

output "uc_schemas" {
  description = "UC schemas (medallion + reference)."
  value       = [for s in databricks_schema.schemas : s.name]
}

# ---- Container Apps platform ----------------------------------------------

output "container_app_environment" {
  description = "Shared Container Apps Environment (Airflow + mockdata Jobs)."
  value       = azurerm_container_app_environment.harness.name
}

output "acr_login_server" {
  description = "Registry login server — build+push the mockdata image here before the first Job run."
  value       = azurerm_container_registry.harness.login_server
}

output "airflow_url" {
  description = "Airflow web UI."
  value       = "https://${azurerm_container_app.airflow.ingress[0].fqdn}"
}

output "airflow_admin_user" {
  description = "Airflow web admin username."
  value       = var.airflow_admin_user
}

output "airflow_admin_password" {
  description = "Airflow web admin password (generated)."
  value       = random_password.airflow_admin.result
  sensitive   = true
}

output "postgres_fqdn" {
  description = "Airflow metadata Postgres host."
  value       = azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.airflow.fqdn
}

output "mockdata_jobs" {
  description = "Cron Jobs created (feed -> schedule)."
  value       = { for k, j in azurerm_container_app_job.mockdata : k => var.feed_crons[k] }
}

## Approved Plan (edited by user):
# Week 7 — Go to cloud: DataQ app infra (Terraform) + GHCR deploy reconciliation

## Context

Week 6 is closed (27/27); we're entering **Week 7 — deployment, hardening & docs**.
The exit gate is *production-ready v1 deployed to Azure, CI/CD live*. Deploy
**scaffolding** (#379) exists but is incomplete and stale:

1. **Stale registry.** ADR 0023 (latest commit) made **GHCR** the registry and
   explicitly *supersedes the #379 ACR scaffolding* — but `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`
   + `deploy/README.md` still build/push to **ACR** (`az acr login`, `ACR_*`). The
   ACA apps should pull `ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:<tag>` anonymously
   (public package → no registry credential, per ADR 0023).
2. **No app infra-as-code.** There is no Terraform for the *app's own* production
   resources. The harness Terraform (`~/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/terraform/`,
   ADR 0021) stands up *datasources + demo env* only and must stay separate.

**Decisions (locked with the user):**
- Scope this round = author + reconcile + **apply** (provision billable infra now).
- New Terraform lives **in-repo** at `deploy/terraform/`; state gitignored.
- Redis = **self-hosted `redis:7-alpine` Container App** (internal, transient broker).
- GitHub Actions → Azure auth = **AAD app registration + OIDC** (federated cred).
- Reuse **subscription + RG `dataq-rg` only**; everything else is fresh `dataq-app-*`.
- Account is **Owner at subscription scope** → can register RPs + assign roles
  (the old "blocked on Owner" gate is cleared).

**Outcome:** DataQ v1 running on Azure Container Apps + Static Web App, backed by
managed Postgres, Key Vault, App Insights, and a self-hosted Redis broker — with a
GHCR-based CI deploy path wired for OIDC.

---

## Separation & tagging (hard constraint)

- All new resources: prefix `dataq-app-*`, tags
  `{ project = "dataq", managed = "terraform", purpose = "dataq-app" }`
  (mirrors harness `common_tags`, only `purpose` differs from `dataq-harness`).
- RG `dataq-rg` is **shared** — referenced, never destroyed. Its RG-level tag stays
  `project=dataq` (do not stamp `purpose` on the shared RG).
- The harness uses an `azurerm_resource_provider_registrations = "none"` SP; this
  stack applies as the **Owner user** so it can register RPs + grant roles.

---

## Part A — Reconcile deploy scaffolding to GHCR (ADR 0023)

In-repo edits, no cloud side effects:

- **`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`**
  - Drop the `az acr login` / `docker build`+`push` to ACR. Build + push to
    **GHCR** using `docker/login-action` with `${{ github.actor }}` /
    `${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` (needs `permissions: packages: write`).
  - `env.IMAGE: ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:${{ inputs.image_tag }}`
    (lowercase owner — GHCR requirement).
  - Migrate-job + `containerapp update` steps keep their structure (the
    migrate-before-rollout gate + 15-min poll is correct — keep it).
  - Drop `ACR_NAME` / `ACR_LOGIN_SERVER` vars; keep RG/app-name vars.
- **`deploy/README.md`** — swap the ACR topology line + "GitHub config" section for
  GHCR (public package, anonymous ACA pull, no `AZURE_STATIC_WEB_APPS_API_TOKEN`
  change). Update the var list (remove `ACR_*`).
- **`deploy/.env.app.prod.example`** — already GHCR-agnostic; only fill in the
  vault/url shape notes if needed (no secret values).

---

## Part B — New Terraform at `deploy/terraform/`

Mirror harness conventions (local state, pinned providers, `local.common_tags`,
`random_string` suffix). Files:

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `versions.tf` | `terraform >= 1.9`; pins: `azurerm ~> 4`, `azuread ~> 3`, `random ~> 3.6`; **local backend** (`terraform.tfstate`, gitignored). |
| `providers.tf` | `azurerm { features {} }` (sub/tenant from `az login`/`ARM_*`), `azuread {}`, `random {}`. |
| `main.tf` | **Idempotent RG step** (see below) → `data "azurerm_resource_group"` → `local.common_tags` + `random_string.suffix`. |
| `variables.tf` | rg=`dataq-rg`, location=`West US 2`, `postgres_location=westus3` (wus2 offer-restricted per harness note), SKUs, `github_repo="TheurgicDuke771/DataQ"`, `backend_image` (GHCR), `image_tag`, `workspace_admin_emails`, Azure-AD SSO ids. |
| `rp.tf` | `azurerm_resource_provider_registration` for `Microsoft.Web`, `Microsoft.KeyVault`, `Microsoft.Insights`, `Microsoft.Cache` (the 4 NotRegistered). Declarative + idempotent. |
| `logs.tf` | `azurerm_log_analytics_workspace "dataq-app-logs"` (PerGB2018, 30d). |
| `appinsights.tf` | workspace-based `azurerm_application_insights "dataq-app-ai"`. |
| `identity.tf` | user-assigned `azurerm_user_assigned_identity "dataq-app-id"` for api+worker; `azurerm_role_assignment` → **Key Vault Secrets User** on the vault. |
| `keyvault.tf` | `azurerm_key_vault "dataq-app-kv-<suffix>"` (RBAC auth); secrets: `database-url`, `redis-url`, `appinsights-connection-string`, `adf-webhook-secret`, `airflow-webhook-secret`, (`teams-webhook` optional). Grant the **applier (Owner)** Key Vault Secrets Officer so TF can write secret values; grant the UAMI Secrets User (read). |
| `postgres.tf` | `azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server` (B1ms, v16, `westus3`, public + allow-Azure-services firewall) + `database "dataq"` + `random_password`. Build `DATABASE_URL` (`...?sslmode=require`) → KV secret. |
| `aca.tf` | `azurerm_container_app_environment "dataq-app-cae"` (→ logs workspace). |
| `redis.tf` | self-hosted `azurerm_container_app "dataq-app-redis"` — `redis:7-alpine`, internal TCP `:6379`, 1 replica. `REDIS_URL=redis://dataq-app-redis:6379/0` → KV secret. |
| `containerapps.tf` | `dataq-api` (external ingress :8000, uvicorn), `dataq-worker` (`celery … worker -B`), `dataq-migrate` **job** (`alembic upgrade head`). All: same GHCR image, UAMI attached, `SECRET_STORE=azure_key_vault`, `AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL`, secret refs (DATABASE_URL/REDIS_URL/APPINSIGHTS) as Container Apps secrets sourced from Key Vault via the UAMI, plus the SSO env from vars. |
| `swa.tf` | `azurerm_static_web_app "dataq-app-web"` (**Standard** — linked backends need Standard) + `azurerm_static_web_app_custom...`/linked-backend to `dataq-api` so `/api/*` is same-origin (CORS stays empty, per README §4 / ADR 0018). *Alt: Free + `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS`=SWA origin if cost matters.* |
| `github_oidc.tf` | `azuread_application` + `service_principal` + `azuread_application_federated_identity_credential` (subject `repo:TheurgicDuke771/DataQ:environment:production`) + `azurerm_role_assignment` Contributor on `dataq-rg`. |
| `outputs.tf` | api FQDN, SWA default hostname + **SWA api token** (sensitive), KV url, App Insights conn string (sensitive), and the GitHub config values: `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`/`AZURE_TENANT_ID`/`AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID`, app names, image ref. |

**Idempotent RG step (`main.tf`)** — user-requested:
```hcl
resource "null_resource" "ensure_rg" {
  provisioner "local-exec" {
    command = "az group create -n ${var.azure_resource_group} -l '${var.azure_location}' --tags project=dataq"
  }                       # az group create is idempotent; preserves project=dataq
}
data "azurerm_resource_group" "dataq" {
  name       = var.azure_resource_group
  depends_on = [null_resource.ensure_rg]
}
```

**`.gitignore`** — add `deploy/terraform/.terraform/`, `*.tfstate*`,
`*.tfvars` (keep `*.tfvars.example`), `.terraform.lock.hcl` kept tracked.

---

## Part C — Apply / bring-up sequence

1. **Build + push first backend image to GHCR** (chicken-and-egg: ACA needs an
   image to start). `gh auth token | docker login ghcr.io -u TheurgicDuke771 --password-stdin`;
   `docker build -f backend/Dockerfile -t ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:v1 .`;
   `docker push …`; **make the GHCR package public** (anonymous ACA pull, ADR 0023).
2. `terraform -chdir=deploy/terraform init && … plan` → **review** → `apply`.
   (RP registration first apply may take a few min.)
3. **Post-apply wiring** (mostly `gh` CLI from outputs):
   - Set repo **secrets** `AZURE_CLIENT_ID/TENANT_ID/SUBSCRIPTION_ID`,
     `AZURE_STATIC_WEB_APPS_API_TOKEN`; **vars** `AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP`,
     `API_APP_NAME`, `WORKER_APP_NAME`, `MIGRATE_JOB_NAME`, `VITE_AZURE_*`,
     GHCR image ref. Create the `production` GitHub environment.
   - Build + deploy the **frontend** to SWA (via the Deploy workflow or `swa` CLI).
4. **Verify** (below).
5. **Docs:** new ADR `0024` (app deploy infra: GHCR + ACA + self-hosted redis +
   SWA linked backend + OIDC app-reg); update CLAUDE.md §13 + `docs/progress.md`.

Deferred to later W7 tasks (not this round): Azure Monitor → ADF webhook alert
rule (needs the live API URL — wire after step 4), the FastMCP 8-tool server,
security hardening pass.

---

## Verification (end-to-end)

- `terraform plan` clean before apply; `apply` converges with no drift on re-run
  (idempotency check — run `plan` again, expect "No changes").
- `az resource list -g dataq-rg --query "[?tags.purpose=='dataq-app'].name"` lists
  exactly the new stack; harness `dataq-harness-*` untouched.
- **Migrate job**: `az containerapp job start --name dataq-migrate …` → execution
  `Succeeded`.
- **API health**: `curl https://<dataq-api fqdn>/api/v1/...` (health/openapi) 200;
  Swagger at `/docs`.
- **Secrets**: api/worker resolve `SECRET_STORE=azure_key_vault` via the UAMI (no
  startup auth errors in `az containerapp logs show`).
- **Frontend**: SWA URL loads the SPA; `/api/*` proxies same-origin (no CORS error);
  Azure-AD login works (`AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=false`).
- **CI deploy**: trigger the **Deploy** workflow (`workflow_dispatch`) → OIDC login
  succeeds, builds+pushes GHCR image, migrate gate passes, api+worker roll.

---

## Risks / notes

- **GHCR package must be public** before apply or ACA pulls fail (ADR 0023 model).
- **SWA Standard** (~$9/mo) is required for the linked backend; Free+CORS is the
  cheaper fallback (flip `swa.tf` SKU + set `CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS`).
- **AAD app registration** needs tenant app-reg rights — fine as Default Directory
  Owner; if blocked, fall back to a user-assigned identity + federated cred.
- Postgres in **westus3** (wus2 offer-restricted for this sub, per harness).
- Billing starts at apply: ACA env, Postgres B1ms, SWA Standard, Log Analytics,
  App Insights, KV. Self-hosted redis avoids managed-cache cost.
- Migrations are additive (CLAUDE.md) → migrate-before-rollout is safe.
- One-functionality-per-commit (CONTRIBUTING): land Part A (GHCR reconcile),
  Part B (terraform), and the ADR/docs as **separate commits/PRs**.

=== terraform ===
Terraform v1.15.7
on darwin_arm64
=== backend Dockerfile (entry/cmd) ===
# (which would interfere with signal forwarding to uvicorn/celery).
FROM continuumio/miniconda3:24.11.1-0

WORKDIR /workspace

# Create the conda env first and cache the layer. environment.yml's pip section
# does `-r backend/requirements-dev.txt` (which -r's requirements.txt /
# -typecheck / -tooling), so those must exist before `conda env create`. Copy
# just the requirements files (not all of backend/) so the env-create layer cache
# busts only on a pin change, not on every code edit.
COPY environment.yml ./
COPY backend/requirements*.txt ./backend/
RUN conda env create -f environment.yml && conda clean -afy

ENV PATH=/opt/conda/envs/dataq/bin:$PATH \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

# Application code + tooling config (pyproject is needed to run pytest/mypy in-container).
COPY pyproject.toml ./
COPY backend ./backend

EXPOSE 8000

# Default to the API; the worker service overrides `command` in compose.
CMD ["uvicorn", "backend.app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]

========== airflow.tf ==========
# Airflow on Container Apps — scheduler + webserver (LocalExecutor), backed by the
# Postgres metadata DB. min_replicas = 1 (the scheduler can't scale to zero); HTTPS
# ingress so Event-Grid (file-landing push) and DataQ can reach it. ~$25-75/mo always-on.
#
# Starts on the public airflow image (no DAGs). §3 swaps `airflow_image` for a custom
# registry image (FROM apache/airflow + COPY dags/) that calls the mockdata tick CLI / loads.

resource "random_id" "fernet" {
  byte_length = 32
}

resource "random_password" "airflow_webserver_secret" {
  length  = 32
  special = false
}

resource "random_password" "airflow_admin" {
  length  = 20
  special = false
}

locals {
  # Valid Fernet key = url-safe base64 of 32 bytes (swap +/ for -_, keep padding).
  airflow_fernet_key = replace(replace(random_id.fernet.b64_std, "+", "-"), "/", "_")

  airflow_pg_conn = join("", [
    "postgresql+psycopg2://",
    var.postgres_admin_login, ":", random_password.pg.result,
    "@", azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.airflow.fqdn, ":5432/",
    azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_database.airflow.name, "?sslmode=require",
  ])

  # Custom registry image (apache/airflow + the harness DAGs + client libs).
  airflow_image = "${azurerm_container_registry.harness.login_server}/airflow-dataq:${var.airflow_image_tag}"

  # CeleryExecutor: Redis broker (internal) + Postgres result backend. Workers run in a
  # SEPARATE, horizontally scalable container app (airflow_worker.tf) — that's what lifts
  # the single-executor / 2-vCPU-per-replica ceiling that throttled LocalExecutor.
  # Container Apps internal service-to-service: the short app name resolves over the
  # environment's internal DNS (the full .internal. FQDN did not connect for TCP).
  celery_broker_url = "redis://${azurerm_container_app.redis.name}:6379/0"
  celery_result_backend = join("", [
    "db+postgresql://",
    var.postgres_admin_login, ":", random_password.pg.result,
    "@", azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.airflow.fqdn, ":5432/",
    azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_database.airflow.name, "?sslmode=require",
  ])

  # Shared scheduler + webserver env (DRYed into both containers via dynamic blocks).
  # LocalExecutor runs tasks in the scheduler, so the connection env must live here.
  airflow_env = [
    { name = "AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_CONN", secret_name = "pg-conn" },
    { name = "AIRFLOW__CORE__EXECUTOR", value = "CeleryExecutor" },
    { name = "AIRFLOW__CELERY__BROKER_URL", value = local.celery_broker_url },
    { name = "AIRFLOW__CELERY__RESULT_BACKEND", secret_name = "celery-result-backend" },
    # Tasks per worker replica — each cold-starts a fresh interpreter, so keep it modest
    # vs the worker's 2 vCPU / 4 GiB; horizontal scaling (more replicas) is the lever.
    { name = "AIRFLOW__CELERY__WORKER_CONCURRENCY", value = "3" },
    { name = "AIRFLOW__CORE__FERNET_KEY", secret_name = "fernet-key" },
    { name = "AIRFLOW__WEBSERVER__SECRET_KEY", secret_name = "webserver-secret" },
    { name = "AIRFLOW__CORE__LOAD_EXAMPLES", value = "False" },
    # Enable basic-auth on the REST API so DAG runs can be triggered programmatically.
    { name = "AIRFLOW__API__AUTH_BACKENDS", value = "airflow.api.auth.backend.basic_auth,airflow.api.auth.backend.session" },
    # Run each task in a FRESH interpreter (spawn) instead of forking the scheduler.
    # The scheduler is multi-threaded (Azure SDK / gRPC bg threads); LocalExecutor's
    # fork() of it deadlocks the child → tasks stick in 'scheduled' and never run.
    { name = "AIRFLOW__CORE__EXECUTE_TASKS_NEW_PYTHON_INTERPRETER", value = "True" },

    # ADLS read (key-based connection string).
    { name = "AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING", secret_name = "adls-conn" },
    { name = "ADLS_FILESYSTEM", value = var.adls_filesystems[0] },

    # Snowflake load — write with DATAQ_LOADER (ETL), not the read-only DATAQ_READER.
    { name = "SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT", value = "${var.snowflake_organization_name}-${var.snowflake_account_name}" },
    { name = "SNOWFLAKE_USER", value = var.snowflake_reader_user },
    { name = "SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD", secret_name = "snowflake-password" },
    { name = "SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE", value = var.snowflake_warehouse },
    { name = "SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE", value = var.snowflake_database },
    { name = "SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA", value = var.snowflake_schemas[0] },
    { name = "SNOWFLAKE_ROLE", value = var.snowflake_loader_role },

    # Databricks — UC reference loads (flow_a_uc_reference) + Flow B notebook submit.
    { name = "DATABRICKS_HOST", value = var.databricks_host },
    { name = "DATABRICKS_TOKEN", secret_name = "databricks-token" },
    { name = "DATABRICKS_HTTP_PATH", value = var.databricks_http_path },
    { name = "UC_CATALOG", value = var.uc_catalog },
  ]
}

resource "azurerm_container_app" "airflow" {
  name                         = "dataq-harness-airflow"
  container_app_environment_id = azurerm_container_app_environment.harness.id
  resource_group_name          = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name
  revision_mode                = "Single"

  identity {
    type = "SystemAssigned"
  }

  registry {
    server               = azurerm_container_registry.harness.login_server
    username             = azurerm_container_registry.harness.admin_username
    password_secret_name = "acr-password"
  }

  secret {
    name  = "acr-password"
    value = azurerm_container_registry.harness.admin_password
  }
  secret {
    name  = "adls-conn"
    value = azurerm_storage_account.landing.primary_connection_string
  }
  secret {
    name  = "snowflake-password"
    value = var.snowflake_password
  }
  secret {
    name  = "databricks-token"
    value = var.databricks_token
  }
  secret {
    name  = "celery-result-backend"
    value = local.celery_result_backend
  }
  secret {
    name  = "pg-conn"
    value = local.airflow_pg_conn
  }
  secret {
    name  = "fernet-key"
    value = local.airflow_fernet_key
  }
  secret {
    name  = "webserver-secret"
    value = random_password.airflow_webserver_secret.result
  }
  secret {
    name  = "admin-password"
    value = random_password.airflow_admin.result
  }

  ingress {
    external_enabled = true
    target_port      = 8080
    transport        = "auto"
    traffic_weight {
      latest_revision = true
      percentage      = 100
    }
  }

  template {
    min_replicas = 1
    max_replicas = 1

    # One-shot: migrate the metadata DB + create the admin user before the app starts.
    init_container {
      name    = "airflow-init"
      image   = local.airflow_image
      cpu     = 0.5
      memory  = "1Gi"
      command = ["/bin/bash", "-c"]
      args = [
        "airflow db migrate && airflow users create --username ${var.airflow_admin_user} --password \"$AIRFLOW_ADMIN_PW\" --firstname Demo --lastname Admin --role Admin --email ${var.airflow_admin_user}@example.com || true",
      ]
      env {
        name        = "AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_CONN"
        secret_name = "pg-conn"
      }
      env {
        name        = "AIRFLOW__CORE__FERNET_KEY"
        secret_name = "fernet-key"
      }
      env {
        name        = "AIRFLOW_ADMIN_PW"
        secret_name = "admin-password"
      }
    }

    container {
      name = "scheduler"
      image = local.airflow_image
      # LocalExecutor runs every task as a subprocess of THIS container, and each task
      # cold-starts a fresh interpreter (EXECUTE_TASKS_NEW_PYTHON_INTERPRETER, the
      # fork-deadlock fix) re-importing Airflow + snowflake/azure/databricks libs.
      # 0.5 vCPU bottlenecked that to ~1-2 concurrent tasks. Consumption caps a replica
      # at 2.0 vCPU / 4 GiB TOTAL, so: scheduler 1.5/3Gi + webserver 0.5/1Gi = 2.0/4Gi
      # (the max) — a 3x bump to the task runner.
      cpu    = 1.5
      memory = "3Gi"
      args   = ["scheduler"]
      dynamic "env" {
        for_each = local.airflow_env
        content {
          name        = env.value.name
          value       = lookup(env.value, "value", null)
          secret_name = lookup(env.value, "secret_name", null)
        }
      }
    }

    container {
      name   = "webserver"
      image  = local.airflow_image
      cpu    = 0.5
      memory = "1Gi"
      args   = ["webserver"]
      dynamic "env" {
        for_each = local.airflow_env
        content {
          name        = env.value.name
          value       = lookup(env.value, "value", null)
          secret_name = lookup(env.value, "secret_name", null)
        }
      }
    }
  }

  tags = local.common_tags
}
========== mockdata_job.tf ==========
# mockdata file-creation Jobs (§2a) — one Container Apps Job per feed, each on its
# own cron (var.feed_crons). Runs `python -m mockdata tick --feed <feed>` writing the
# generated batch + state to ADLS. Source-system simulator, upstream of ADF/Airflow.
#
# Auth: ACR pull via registry admin creds; ADLS write via the storage account
# connection string (AdlsStore reads AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING) — both avoid
# role assignments the Contributor-only Terraform SP can't create.
#
# NOTE: build + push the image before the first scheduled run:
#   az acr login -n <registry> && docker build -t <login_server>/mockdata:latest . && docker push ...
# Run `init` once (manually, as a Job execution or locally) to seed state in ADLS.

locals {
  adls_root  = "adls://${azurerm_storage_account.landing.name}/${var.adls_filesystems[0]}"
  adls_state = "${local.adls_root}/state"
}

resource "azurerm_container_app_job" "mockdata" {
  for_each = var.feed_crons

  name                         = "mockdata-${each.key}"
  container_app_environment_id = azurerm_container_app_environment.harness.id
  resource_group_name          = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name
  location                     = var.azure_location

  replica_timeout_in_seconds = 1800
  replica_retry_limit        = 1

  schedule_trigger_config {
    cron_expression          = each.value
    parallelism              = 1
    replica_completion_count = 1
  }

  registry {
    server               = azurerm_container_registry.harness.login_server
    username             = azurerm_container_registry.harness.admin_username
    password_secret_name = "acr-password"
  }

  secret {
    name  = "acr-password"
    value = azurerm_container_registry.harness.admin_password
  }
  secret {
    name  = "storage-conn"
    value = azurerm_storage_account.landing.primary_connection_string
  }

  template {
    container {
      name    = "mockdata"
      image   = "${azurerm_container_registry.harness.login_server}/mockdata:${var.mockdata_image_tag}"
      cpu     = 0.5
      memory  = "1Gi"
      command = ["python", "-m", "mockdata"]
      args = [
        "tick", "--feed", each.key,
        "--out", local.adls_root,
        "--state", local.adls_state,
      ]
      env {
        name        = "AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING"
        secret_name = "storage-conn"
      }
    }
  }

  tags = local.common_tags
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/deploy/terraform/versions.tf",
  "content": "# DataQ APP infra — Terraform / provider pins.\n#\n# This stack provisions the *application's own* production resources (ACA + SWA +\n# Postgres + Key Vault + App Insights + a self-hosted Redis broker) into the\n# EXISTING dataq-rg. It is deliberately SEPARATE from the harness stack\n# (~/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/terraform — ADR 0021), which stands up the\n# datasources + demo env. Only the subscription + resource group are shared.\n#\n# Local state backend — state is gitignored, never committed (it contains the\n# generated Postgres password + secret values). Pin providers; do not float.\n\nterraform {\n  required_version = \">= 1.9\"\n\n  backend \"local\" {\n    path = \"terraform.tfstate\"\n  }\n\n  required_providers {\n    azurerm = {\n      source  = \"hashicorp/azurerm\"\n      version = \"~> 4.0\"\n    }\n    azuread = {\n      source  = \"hashicorp/azuread\"\n      version = \"~> 3.0\"\n    }\n    random = {\n      source  = \"hashicorp/random\"\n      version = \"~> 3.6\"\n    }\n    time = {\n      source  = \"hashicorp/time\"\n      version = \"~> 0.12\"\n    }\n    null = {\n      source  = \"hashicorp/null\"\n      version = \"~> 3.2\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/deploy/terraform/main.tf",
  "content": "# Shared data sources, locals, and the idempotent RG ensure-step.\n\ndata \"azurerm_client_config\" \"current\" {}\n\ndata \"azurerm_subscription\" \"current\" {}\n\n# ── Idempotent RG step ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n# `az group create` is idempotent: it creates dataq-rg if absent and is a no-op\n# (with the same tags) if it already exists. We only ever pass project=dataq so\n# the shared RG's existing tag is preserved and the harness resources in the same\n# RG are unaffected. The data source below then references the (now-guaranteed) RG\n# — we never manage/destroy the shared RG as a Terraform resource.\nresource \"null_resource\" \"ensure_rg\" {\n  triggers = {\n    rg       = var.azure_resource_group\n    location = var.azure_location\n  }\n  provisioner \"local-exec\" {\n    command = \"az group create --name ${var.azure_resource_group} --location '${var.azure_location}' --tags project=dataq --only-show-errors --output none\"\n  }\n}\n\ndata \"azurerm_resource_group\" \"dataq\" {\n  name       = var.azure_resource_group\n  depends_on = [null_resource.ensure_rg]\n}\n\nresource \"random_string\" \"suffix\" {\n  length  = 6\n  lower   = true\n  upper   = false\n  numeric = true\n  special = false\n}\n\nlocals {\n  # All DataQ-APP resources carry purpose=dataq-app so they're trivially\n  # distinguishable from the harness's purpose=dataq-harness resources in the\n  # shared RG (see the verification query in deploy/terraform/README.md).\n  common_tags = {\n    project = var.project_tag\n    managed = \"terraform\"\n    purpose = \"dataq-app\"\n  }\n}\n"
}

  "content": "# Non-secret configuration. Defaults are wired for the single-tenant v1 deploy.\n# Override in terraform.tfvars (gitignored) — see terraform.tfvars.example.\n\nvariable \"project_tag\" {\n  description = \"Tag applied to all resources (matches the harness/RG convention).\"\n  type        = string\n  default     = \"dataq\"\n}\n\n# ── Shared (reused) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nvariable \"azure_resource_group\" {\n  description = \"Existing RG shared with the harness. Reused, never destroyed.\"\n  type        = string\n  default     = \"dataq-rg\"\n}\n\nvariable \"azure_location\" {\n  description = \"Region for the app resources (Container Apps, KV, SWA, logs).\"\n  type        = string\n  default     = \"West US 2\"\n}\n\nvariable \"postgres_location\" {\n  description = \"Region for the app Postgres. westus3 because Postgres Flexible Server is offer-restricted in West US 2 for this subscription (same constraint the harness hit). Adjacent to westus2 -> low latency from the Container Apps env.\"\n  type        = string\n  default     = \"West US 3\"\n}\n\n# ── Backend image (GHCR — ADR 0023) ──────────────────────────────────────────\n\nvariable \"backend_image_repo\" {\n  description = \"GHCR backend image repository (public package, anonymous ACA pull). Lowercase owner per GHCR.\"\n  type        = string\n  default     = \"ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend\"\n}\n\nvariable \"image_tag\" {\n  description = \"Backend image tag to deploy. Use an IMMUTABLE tag in prod (ACA caches 'latest' at the node, so a same-tag rebuild won't be re-pulled on a new revision). Bump per deploy.\"\n  type        = string\n  default     = \"v1\"\n}\n\n# ── Sizing ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nvariable \"postgres_sku\" {\n  description = \"Postgres Flexible Server SKU (Burstable B1ms = cheapest).\"\n  type        = string\n  default     = \"B_Standard_B1ms\"\n}\n\nvariable \"postgres_admin_login\" {\n  description = \"App Postgres admin login (password is generated, stored in state + KV-adjacent container secret).\"\n  type        = string\n  default     = \"dataqadmin\"\n}\n\nvariable \"log_retention_days\" {\n  description = \"Log Analytics retention for the Container Apps environment.\"\n  type        = number\n  default     = 30\n}\n\nvariable \"swa_sku\" {\n  description = \"Static Web App SKU. Standard is required to link a Container Apps backend (same-origin /api proxy). Drop to Free only with the CORS fallback.\"\n  type        = string\n  default     = \"Standard\"\n}\n\n# ── App config (non-secret) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nvariable \"environment\" {\n  description = \"ENVIRONMENT value the backend Settings read.\"\n  type        = string\n  default     = \"prod\"\n}\n\nvariable \"workspace_admin_emails\" {\n  description = \"Comma-separated workspace-admin allowlist (WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS).\"\n  type        = string\n  default     = \"\"\n}\n\n# Azure AD SSO — real auth in prod (AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=false). These are non-secret\n# identifiers (MSAL SPA is a public client; there is no SPA secret).\nvariable \"azure_tenant_id\" {\n  description = \"Azure AD tenant id for SSO. Empty = inherit the deployer's tenant.\"\n  type        = string\n  default     = \"\"\n}\n\nvariable \"azure_api_client_id\" {\n  description = \"App-registration (API) client id for token validation.\"\n  type        = string\n  default     = \"\"\n}\n\nvariable \"azure_spa_client_id\" {\n  description = \"App-registration (SPA) client id (public MSAL client).\"\n  type        = string\n  default     = \"\"\n}\n\nvariable \"azure_api_scope\" {\n  description = \"API scope the SPA requests.\"\n  type        = string\n  default     = \"user_impersonation\"\n}\n\n# ── CI deploy (GitHub OIDC) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nvariable \"github_repo\" {\n  description = \"owner/repo the Deploy workflow runs from (federated-credential subject).\"\n  type        = string\n  default     = \"TheurgicDuke771/DataQ\"\n}\n\nvariable \"github_environment\" {\n  description = \"GitHub environment the federated credential is scoped to.\"\n  type        = string\n  default     = \"production\"\n}\n"

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/deploy/terraform/keyvault.tf",
  "content": "# Key Vault — the app's runtime SecretStore (SECRET_STORE=azure_key_vault). It\n# holds the datasource connection credentials the app writes/reads via the API at\n# runtime, plus the pre-seeded orchestration webhook secrets. RBAC authorization\n# (not access policies): the UAMI gets Secrets User (read); the deployer gets\n# Secrets Officer (write) so Terraform can seed the webhook secrets.\n#\n# NOTE: boot-critical config (DATABASE_URL / REDIS_URL / App Insights) is injected\n# as inline Container App secrets in containerapps.tf, NOT via KV references — that\n# decouples first-revision activation from KV-RBAC propagation delay (the classic\n# \"secret ref fails on the very first apply\" gotcha). The vault is still exercised\n# end-to-end by the UAMI read path + the webhook secrets below.\n\nresource \"azurerm_key_vault\" \"app\" {\n  name                      = \"dataq-app-kv-${random_string.suffix.result}\"\n  location                  = var.azure_location\n  resource_group_name       = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name\n  tenant_id                 = data.azurerm_client_config.current.tenant_id\n  sku_name                  = \"standard\"\n  enable_rbac_authorization = true\n  purge_protection_enabled  = false\n  tags                      = local.common_tags\n\n  depends_on = [azurerm_resource_provider_registration.keyvault]\n}\n\n# Deployer (Owner user running this apply) -> write secrets.\nresource \"azurerm_role_assignment\" \"kv_deployer\" {\n  scope                = azurerm_key_vault.app.id\n  role_definition_name = \"Key Vault Secrets Officer\"\n  principal_id         = data.azurerm_client_config.current.object_id\n}\n\n# App identity -> read secrets at runtime (DefaultAzureCredential).\nresource \"azurerm_role_assignment\" \"kv_app_reader\" {\n  scope                = azurerm_key_vault.app.id\n  role_definition_name = \"Key Vault Secrets User\"\n  principal_id         = azurerm_user_assigned_identity.app.principal_id\n}\n\n# RBAC data-plane role assignments are eventually consistent — wait before the\n# first secret write so Terraform doesn't 403 immediately after the grant.\nresource \"time_sleep\" \"kv_rbac_propagation\" {\n  create_duration = \"60s\"\n  depends_on      = [azurerm_role_assignment.kv_deployer]\n}\n\n# ── Pre-seeded webhook secrets (orchestration event auth) ────────────────────\n# Names match deploy/.env.app.prod.example (ADF_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME etc.). Values\n# are generated; rotate via the provider rotation path (ADR 0006/0007).\n\nresource \"random_password\" \"adf_webhook\" {\n  length  = 40\n  special = false\n}\n\nresource \"random_password\" \"airflow_webhook\" {\n  length  = 40\n  special = false\n}\n\nresource \"azurerm_key_vault_secret\" \"adf_webhook\" {\n  name         = \"adf-webhook-secret\"\n  value        = random_password.adf_webhook.result\n  key_vault_id = azurerm_key_vault.app.id\n  depends_on   = [time_sleep.kv_rbac_propagation]\n}\n\nresource \"azurerm_key_vault_secret\" \"airflow_webhook\" {\n  name         = \"airflow-webhook-secret\"\n  value        = random_password.airflow_webhook.result\n  key_vault_id = azurerm_key_vault.app.id\n  depends_on   = [time_sleep.kv_rbac_propagation]\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/deploy/terraform/postgres.tf",
  "content": "# App database — Postgres Flexible Server (Burstable B1ms). Public access +\n# \"allow Azure services\" so the Container Apps environment reaches it without VNet\n# integration (single-tenant v1). Password generated locally — never committed;\n# state is gitignored. westus3 (see postgres_location) avoids the wus2 offer\n# restriction the harness also hit.\n\nresource \"random_password\" \"pg\" {\n  length  = 28\n  special = false # keep the SQLAlchemy URL clean (no %-encoding)\n}\n\nresource \"azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server\" \"app\" {\n  name                          = \"dataq-app-pg-wus3-${random_string.suffix.result}\"\n  resource_group_name           = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name\n  location                      = var.postgres_location\n  version                       = \"16\"\n  administrator_login           = var.postgres_admin_login\n  administrator_password        = random_password.pg.result\n  sku_name                      = var.postgres_sku\n  storage_mb                    = 32768\n  auto_grow_enabled             = true\n  public_network_access_enabled = true\n  zone                          = \"1\"\n  tags                          = local.common_tags\n}\n\nresource \"azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_database\" \"app\" {\n  name      = \"dataq\"\n  server_id = azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.app.id\n  collation = \"en_US.utf8\"\n  charset   = \"utf8\"\n}\n\n# start=end=0.0.0.0 is Azure's special \"allow access from Azure services\" rule.\nresource \"azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_firewall_rule\" \"azure_services\" {\n  name             = \"allow-azure-services\"\n  server_id        = azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.app.id\n  start_ip_address = \"0.0.0.0\"\n  end_ip_address   = \"0.0.0.0\"\n}\n\nlocals {\n  # psycopg2 URL the backend Settings read as DATABASE_URL. sslmode=require —\n  # Flexible Server enforces TLS.\n  database_url = join(\"\", [\n    \"postgresql+psycopg2://\",\n    var.postgres_admin_login, \":\", random_password.pg.result,\n    \"@\", azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.app.fqdn, \":5432/\",\n    azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_database.app.name, \"?sslmode=require\",\n  ])\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/deploy/terraform/redis.tf",
  "content": "# Self-hosted Redis broker for Celery (decision: self-hosted Container App, not\n# Azure Cache for Redis — cheapest for a transient broker; no persistence needed).\n# Internal-only TCP ingress so only the api + worker in this environment reach it.\n# The api/worker connect over the environment's internal DNS using the short app\n# name: redis://dataq-app-redis:6379/0 (the full .internal FQDN does not connect\n# for raw TCP — same finding as the harness broker).\n\nresource \"azurerm_container_app\" \"redis\" {\n  name                         = \"dataq-app-redis\"\n  container_app_environment_id = azurerm_container_app_environment.app.id\n  resource_group_name          = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name\n  revision_mode                = \"Single\"\n\n  ingress {\n    external_enabled = false\n    transport        = \"tcp\"\n    target_port      = 6379\n    exposed_port     = 6379\n    traffic_weight {\n      latest_revision = true\n      percentage      = 100\n    }\n  }\n\n  template {\n    min_replicas = 1\n    max_replicas = 1\n    container {\n      name   = \"redis\"\n      image  = \"redis:7-alpine\" # public image — no registry auth\n      cpu    = 0.5\n      memory = \"1Gi\"\n    }\n  }\n\n  tags = local.common_tags\n}\n\nlocals {\n  redis_url = \"redis://${azurerm_container_app.redis.name}:6379/0\"\n}\n"
}

  "content": "# The DataQ backend on Container Apps — api (external ingress), worker (Celery +\n# embedded beat), and the migrate Job. All three run the SAME GHCR image\n# (ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:<tag>), pulled anonymously (public\n# package, ADR 0023 — no registry block / credential).\n#\n# Boot-critical secrets (DATABASE_URL, App Insights) are inline Container App\n# secrets, NOT KV references (see keyvault.tf for why). REDIS_URL is non-secret\n# (in-environment, no auth). The app's runtime SecretStore reads datasource creds\n# from Key Vault via the attached user-assigned identity (SECRET_STORE +\n# AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL).\n\nlocals {\n  backend_image   = \"${var.backend_image_repo}:${var.image_tag}\"\n  azure_tenant_id = var.azure_tenant_id != \"\" ? var.azure_tenant_id : data.azurerm_client_config.current.tenant_id\n\n  # Inline secrets shared by api + worker (+ DATABASE_URL also on the migrate job).\n  app_secrets = [\n    { name = \"database-url\", value = local.database_url },\n    { name = \"appinsights-conn\", value = azurerm_application_insights.app.connection_string },\n  ]\n\n  # Non-secret env + secret_name references, shared by api + worker.\n  app_env = [\n    { name = \"ENVIRONMENT\", value = var.environment },\n    { name = \"LOG_LEVEL\", value = \"INFO\" },\n    { name = \"DATABASE_URL\", secret_name = \"database-url\" },\n    { name = \"REDIS_URL\", value = local.redis_url },\n    { name = \"APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING\", secret_name = \"appinsights-conn\" },\n    { name = \"SAMPLE_FAILURES_RETENTION_DAYS\", value = \"30\" },\n    # Runtime SecretStore -> Key Vault via the user-assigned identity.\n    { name = \"SECRET_STORE\", value = \"azure_key_vault\" },\n    { name = \"AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL\", value = azurerm_key_vault.app.vault_uri },\n    # Real SSO in prod. The *_CLIENT_ID/TENANT are non-secret; fill via tfvars once\n    # the app registrations exist (empty is fine for the first deploy — health/docs\n    # don't require auth; flip when SSO is wired).\n    { name = \"AUTH_DEV_BYPASS\", value = \"false\" },\n    { name = \"AZURE_TENANT_ID\", value = local.azure_tenant_id },\n    { name = \"AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID\", value = var.azure_api_client_id },\n    { name = \"AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID\", value = var.azure_spa_client_id },\n    { name = \"AZURE_API_SCOPE\", value = var.azure_api_scope },\n    { name = \"WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS\", value = var.workspace_admin_emails },\n    # Empty: the SWA linked backend proxies /api same-origin, so the FastAPI CORS\n    # middleware stays off (README §4 / ADR 0018).\n    { name = \"CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS\", value = \"\" },\n    # Webhook secret KEY names (values live in Key Vault — keyvault.tf).\n    { name = \"ADF_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME\", value = \"adf-webhook-secret\" },\n    { name = \"AIRFLOW_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME\", value = \"airflow-webhook-secret\" },\n  ]\n}\n\n# ── API (FastAPI, external ingress) ──────────────────────────────────────────\nresource \"azurerm_container_app\" \"api\" {\n  name                         = \"dataq-api\"\n  container_app_environment_id = azurerm_container_app_environment.app.id\n  resource_group_name          = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name\n  revision_mode                = \"Single\"\n\n  identity {\n    type         = \"UserAssigned\"\n    identity_ids = [azurerm_user_assigned_identity.app.id]\n  }\n\n  dynamic \"secret\" {\n    for_each = local.app_secrets\n    content {\n      name  = secret.value.name\n      value = secret.value.value\n    }\n  }\n\n  ingress {\n    external_enabled = true\n    target_port      = 8000\n    transport        = \"auto\"\n    traffic_weight {\n      latest_revision = true\n      percentage      = 100\n    }\n  }\n\n  template {\n    min_replicas = 1\n    max_replicas = 3\n    container {\n      name   = \"api\"\n      image  = local.backend_image\n      cpu    = 0.5\n      memory = \"1Gi\"\n      # Image CMD already runs `uvicorn backend.app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0\n      # --port 8000` (no --reload in the image), so no command override.\n      dynamic \"env\" {\n        for_each = local.app_env\n        content {\n          name        = env.value.name\n          value       = lookup(env.value, \"value\", null)\n          secret_name = lookup(env.value, \"secret_name\", null)\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  tags       = local.common_tags\n  depends_on = [azurerm_role_assignment.kv_app_reader]\n}\n\n# ── Worker (Celery worker + embedded beat) ───────────────────────────────────\nresource \"azurerm_container_app\" \"worker\" {\n  name                         = \"dataq-worker\"\n  container_app_environment_id = azurerm_container_app_environment.app.id\n  resource_group_name          = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name\n  revision_mode                = \"Single\"\n\n  identity {\n    type         = \"UserAssigned\"\n    identity_ids = [azurerm_user_assigned_identity.app.id]\n  }\n\n  dynamic \"secret\" {\n    for_each = local.app_secrets\n    content {\n      name  = secret.value.name\n      value = secret.value.value\n    }\n  }\n\n  template {\n    # min_replicas = 1: the worker also runs celery-beat (-B) for the schedule\n    # dispatcher + orchestration polling, so it can't scale to zero.\n    min_replicas = 1\n    max_replicas = 1\n    container {\n      name    = \"worker\"\n      image   = local.backend_image\n      cpu     = 1.0\n      memory  = \"2Gi\"\n      command = [\"celery\", \"-A\", \"backend.app.worker.celery_app\", \"worker\", \"-B\", \"--loglevel=INFO\"]\n      dynamic \"env\" {\n        for_each = local.app_env\n        content {\n          name        = env.value.name\n          value       = lookup(env.value, \"value\", null)\n          secret_name = lookup(env.value, \"secret_name\", null)\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  tags       = local.common_tags\n  depends_on = [azurerm_role_assignment.kv_app_reader]\n}\n\n# ── Migrate Job (alembic upgrade head) ───────────────────────────────────────\n# Manual-trigger job the Deploy workflow runs BEFORE rolling the apps (additive,\n# backward-compatible migrations — CLAUDE.md). alembic.ini's script_location is\n# relative to backend/, so cd there first (mirrors docker-compose's migrate svc).\nresource \"azurerm_container_app_job\" \"migrate\" {\n  name                         = \"dataq-migrate\"\n  container_app_environment_id = azurerm_container_app_environment.app.id\n  resource_group_name          = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name\n  location                     = var.azure_location\n\n  replica_timeout_in_seconds = 900\n  replica_retry_limit        = 1\n\n  manual_trigger_config {\n    parallelism              = 1\n    replica_completion_count = 1\n  }\n\n  secret {\n    name  = \"database-url\"\n    value = local.database_url\n  }\n\n  template {\n    container {\n      name    = \"migrate\"\n      image   = local.backend_image\n      cpu     = 0.5\n      memory  = \"1Gi\"\n      command = [\"sh\", \"-c\", \"cd backend && alembic upgrade head\"]\n      env {\n        name        = \"DATABASE_URL\"\n        secret_name = \"database-url\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  tags = local.common_tags\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/deploy/terraform/swa.tf",
  "content": "# Static Web App — hosts the React/Vite build. Standard SKU so the api Container\n# App can be linked as a backend: SWA then proxies /api/* to it same-origin, which\n# is exactly what frontend/staticwebapp.config.json + the relative axios baseURL\n# ('/api/v1') expect (no CORS). The SPA content is uploaded by the Deploy workflow\n# (Azure/static-web-apps-deploy) using the api token output below.\n\nresource \"azurerm_static_web_app\" \"app\" {\n  name                = \"dataq-app-web\"\n  resource_group_name = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name\n  location            = var.azure_location\n  sku_tier            = var.swa_sku\n  sku_size            = var.swa_sku\n  tags                = local.common_tags\n\n  depends_on = [azurerm_resource_provider_registration.web]\n}\n\n# Link the api Container App as the SWA backend. No azurerm resource covers\n# arbitrary linked backends (only the Functions registration), so use the CLI.\n# `backends link` errors if a backend is already linked, so tolerate that on\n# re-apply; re-run after changing the api by tainting this resource.\nresource \"null_resource\" \"swa_linked_backend\" {\n  triggers = {\n    swa_id = azurerm_static_web_app.app.id\n    api_id = azurerm_container_app.api.id\n  }\n  provisioner \"local-exec\" {\n    command = <<-CMD\n      az staticwebapp backends link \\\n        --name ${azurerm_static_web_app.app.name} \\\n        --resource-group ${data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name} \\\n        --backend-resource-id ${azurerm_container_app.api.id} \\\n        --backend-region ${var.azure_location} \\\n        --only-show-errors --output none || echo \"backend already linked (or link pending) — continuing\"\n    CMD\n  }\n  depends_on = [azurerm_static_web_app.app, azurerm_container_app.api]\n}\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/deploy/terraform/github_oidc.tf",
  "content": "# GitHub Actions -> Azure auth for the Deploy workflow (.github/workflows/deploy.yml)\n# via OIDC federated credentials — no stored client secret. The workflow's\n# azure/login uses the client/tenant/subscription ids output by this stack; the SP\n# gets Contributor on dataq-rg so it can run `az containerapp update` / `job start`\n# (the GHCR image push uses the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN, not this SP).\n\nresource \"azuread_application\" \"github_deploy\" {\n  display_name = \"dataq-github-deploy\"\n}\n\nresource \"azuread_service_principal\" \"github_deploy\" {\n  client_id = azuread_application.github_deploy.client_id\n}\n\nresource \"azuread_application_federated_identity_credential\" \"github_deploy\" {\n  application_id = azuread_application.github_deploy.id\n  display_name   = \"github-actions-${var.github_environment}\"\n  description    = \"GitHub Actions OIDC for the ${var.github_environment} environment deploy\"\n  audiences      = [\"api://AzureADTokenExchange\"]\n  issuer         = \"https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com\"\n  # Must match the workflow's `environment: production` job scoping.\n  subject = \"repo:${var.github_repo}:environment:${var.github_environment}\"\n}\n\nresource \"azurerm_role_assignment\" \"github_deploy_contributor\" {\n  scope                = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.id\n  role_definition_name = \"Contributor\"\n  principal_id         = azuread_service_principal.github_deploy.object_id\n}\n"
}
