{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/deploy/terraform/README.md",
  "content": "# DataQ — app infra (Terraform)\n\nProvisions the DataQ **application's own** production resources into the existing\n`dataq-rg`. Deliberately **separate** from the harness stack\n(`~/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/terraform`, ADR 0021) — only the subscription +\nRG are shared. All resources here are prefixed `dataq-app-*` and tagged\n`purpose=dataq-app`; the harness's `dataq-harness-*` / `purpose=dataq-harness`\nresources are never touched.\n\n## What it creates\n\n| Resource | Name |\n|---|---|\n| Log Analytics workspace | `dataq-app-logs` |\n| Application Insights | `dataq-app-ai` |\n| User-assigned identity | `dataq-app-id` (api/worker → Key Vault) |\n| Key Vault (RBAC) | `dataq-app-kv-<suffix>` (SecretStore + webhook secrets) |\n| Postgres Flexible Server | `dataq-app-pg-wus3-<suffix>` (westus3, B1ms) |\n| Container Apps environment | `dataq-app-cae` |\n| Redis broker (Container App) | `dataq-app-redis` (internal TCP) |\n| API / worker / migrate | `dataq-api` · `dataq-worker` · `dataq-migrate` (job) |\n| Static Web App (Standard) | `dataq-app-web` (+ linked api backend) |\n| GitHub-deploy app registration | `dataq-github-deploy` (OIDC federated cred) |\n\nBackend image: `ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:<image_tag>` (GHCR, public —\nACA pulls anonymously, ADR 0023). It must exist + be **public** before apply.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n- `az login` as a subscription **Owner** (this stack registers RPs + creates role\n  assignments + an AAD app registration).\n- The GHCR backend image pushed + public (see repo root `deploy/README.md` /\n  the Week-7 bring-up steps).\n- State is **local + gitignored** — do not commit `terraform.tfstate`.\n\n## Apply\n\n```bash\ncd deploy/terraform\ncp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars   # optional; defaults work\nterraform init\nterraform plan      # review\nterraform apply\n```\n\n## After apply — wire the Deploy workflow\n\n`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` reads these. Push them with `gh` from the outputs:\n\n```bash\ngh secret  set AZURE_CLIENT_ID       -b \"$(terraform output -raw github_actions_client_id)\"\ngh secret  set AZURE_TENANT_ID       -b \"$(terraform output -raw azure_tenant_id)\"\ngh secret  set AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID -b \"$(terraform output -raw azure_subscription_id)\"\ngh secret  set AZURE_STATIC_WEB_APPS_API_TOKEN -b \"$(terraform output -raw swa_api_token)\"\ngh variable set AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP -b \"$(terraform output -raw resource_group)\"\ngh variable set API_APP_NAME         -b \"$(terraform output -raw api_app_name)\"\ngh variable set WORKER_APP_NAME      -b \"$(terraform output -raw worker_app_name)\"\ngh variable set MIGRATE_JOB_NAME     -b \"$(terraform output -raw migrate_job_name)\"\n# Plus the non-secret VITE_AZURE_* build vars (tenant/spa/api client ids + scope).\n```\n\nCreate the `production` GitHub environment (the federated credential subject is\n`repo:<owner>/<repo>:environment:production`).\n\n## Verify\n\n```bash\n# Exactly the app stack — harness untouched:\naz resource list -g dataq-rg --query \"[?tags.purpose=='dataq-app'].name\" -o tsv\n\n# Re-plan is clean (idempotent):\nterraform plan      # expect: No changes\n\n# API health + Swagger:\ncurl -fsS \"$(terraform output -raw api_url)/docs\" >/dev/null && echo OK\n```\n"
}

On your **Slack question** first:

For DataQ's alerting (which today is the `ResultPublisher` → Teams adaptive-card path with a webhook secret in Key Vault), adding Slack is a near-mirror. What's needed depends on which mechanism:

- **Slack Incoming Webhook (recommended, matches the Teams pattern):** just **one webhook URL** — `https://hooks.slack.com/services/T…/B…/…`. You create a Slack app, enable *Incoming Webhooks*, and add it to a channel; the channel is bound into the URL. We'd store it as a Key Vault secret (e.g. `SLACK_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME`, parallel to `TEAMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME`) and POST Block Kit JSON. **No bot token, no channel ID required.**
- **Slack Web API (`chat.postMessage`)** — only if you need threading, message edits, or @-mentions by user ID: a **bot token** (`xoxb-…`), the **`chat:write`** scope, and the **channel ID**.

So for the simplest "fire an alert into a channel," all you need is the **incoming webhook URL**. Tell me which mechanism and whether it's workspace-wide or per-suite (like the #373/#378 per-suite notification config) and I can scope it as a new `ResultPublisher` channel.

  "new_string": "# Defense-in-depth: even though ingress is internal-only (reachable solely from\n# within this Container Apps environment), the broker still requires a password\n# (--requirepass) so a compromised neighbour can't use it unauthenticated.\nresource \"random_password\" \"redis\" {\n  length  = 32\n  special = false\n}\n\nresource \"azurerm_container_app\" \"redis\" {\n  name                         = \"dataq-app-redis\"\n  container_app_environment_id = azurerm_container_app_environment.app.id\n  resource_group_name          = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name\n  revision_mode                = \"Single\"\n\n  secret {\n    name  = \"redis-password\"\n    value = random_password.redis.result\n  }\n\n  ingress {\n    external_enabled = false\n    transport        = \"tcp\"\n    target_port      = 6379\n    exposed_port     = 6379\n    traffic_weight {\n      latest_revision = true\n      percentage      = 100\n    }\n  }\n\n  template {\n    min_replicas = 1\n    max_replicas = 1\n    container {\n      name    = \"redis\"\n      image   = \"redis:7-alpine\" # public image — no registry auth\n      cpu     = 0.5\n      memory  = \"1Gi\"\n      command = [\"sh\", \"-c\", \"exec redis-server --requirepass \\\"$REDIS_PASSWORD\\\"\"]\n      env {\n        name        = \"REDIS_PASSWORD\"\n        secret_name = \"redis-password\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  tags = local.common_tags\n}\n\nlocals {\n  # Password-authenticated broker URL — carries the secret, so it's injected as a\n  # Container App secret (not a plain env) on the api + worker.\n  redis_url = \"REDACTED\"\n}"
}

1	# ADR 0023 — Container image registry: GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) over ACR / Docker Hub
2	
3	- **Status:** Accepted
4	- **Date:** 2026-06-27
5	- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771
6	- **Related:** ADR [0010](0010-provider-agnostic-infrastructure-seams.md) (Azure is one impl behind
7	  each seam — the registry is infra, not business logic), [0013](0013-marketplace-distribution-and-anti-lock-in.md)
8	  (BYOL/marketplace distribution — a neutral registry doubles as the future distribution channel),
9	  [0021](0021-demo-test-data-environment-strategy.md) (deploy/harness context). Supersedes the ACR
10	  choice scaffolded in the Week-7 deploy work (#379); rides the `deploy.yml` SHA-pin (#382).
11	
12	## Context
13	
14	The Week-7 deploy scaffolding (#379) wired `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` to **Azure Container
15	Registry (ACR)**: backend image built in CI, pushed to ACR, pulled by Azure Container Apps (api +
16	worker share one image; a migrate Job runs `alembic upgrade head`). Before the apply, we reconsidered
17	the registry. The DataQ repo is **public**, and a standing project principle (ADR 0010/0013) is that
18	**Azure is one implementation behind each seam** — no Azure-specific assumption should be load-bearing
19	where a neutral option is equivalent. A registry is pure infra; ACR couples the artifact path to Azure
20	for no functional gain.
21	
22	Options weighed: **ACR**, **Docker Hub**, **GHCR**.
23	
24	## Decision
25	
26	**Use GitHub Container Registry (`ghcr.io`) as the container registry for the backend image.**
27	
28	- CI pushes `ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:${{ github.sha }}` (immutable SHA tag, #382),
29	  authenticating with the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` (`permissions: packages: write`) — **no separate
30	  registry account or stored PAT** in CI.
31	- The package is published **public** (the repo is already public and the image bakes in no secrets —
32	  credentials are injected at runtime via Key Vault / Container Apps secrets per the working
33	  agreement), so **Azure Container Apps pulls anonymously — no registry credential stored on the
34	  apps**. This preserves the "no literals / no long-lived registry secret" posture that ACR's managed
35	  identity gave us, without the Azure coupling.
36	- The migrate Job, api, and worker all pull the **same** SHA-pinned image.
37	
38	## Consequences
39	
40	**Positive**
41	- **Vendor-neutral** — the artifact path no longer assumes Azure (ADR 0010/0013). If DataQ moves off
42	  Azure, the registry doesn't move with it.
43	- **Free** for public images; **no Docker Hub pull-rate throttling** on our own GHCR images (matters
44	  under ACA autoscaling + worker + migrate Job all pulling).
45	- **No extra credential** — CI uses `GITHUB_TOKEN`; ACA pulls a public package anonymously. One fewer
46	  secret to rotate than Docker Hub (PAT) and parity with ACR's MI on the "no literals" goal.
47	- **Doubles as the BYOL/marketplace distribution registry** (ADR 0013) — a neutral public registry is
48	  the natural home for a customer-pullable image post-v1.
49	- Same GitHub surface as the source + Actions — one fewer system to provision/manage than ACR.
50	
51	**Negative / watch**
52	- Loses ACR's in-region **co-location** with ACA → pulls cross the internet (added cold-start/scale-out
53	  latency) and loses **Defender for Cloud** registry vulnerability scanning inside the Azure trust
54	  boundary. Mitigation: image scanning can run in CI (e.g. Trivy/Scout) independent of the registry;
55	  the security cadence (CLAUDE.md §6) already covers SAST/deps.
56	- If the image ever needs to be **private** (e.g. a closed BYOL build), GHCR pull from ACA requires a
57	  GitHub PAT as a Container Apps registry secret — re-introducing a stored credential. Revisit then.
58	- Relies on GHCR availability for deploys/scale-out (as any external registry would).
59	
60	## Alternatives considered
61	
62	- **Azure Container Registry (ACR).** Best purely *in-Azure*: managed-identity pull (no secret),
63	  region co-location, Defender scanning. Rejected as the default because it couples the artifact path
64	  to Azure (against ADR 0010/0013) and carries a small standing cost, for benefits that are latency/
65	  scanning niceties rather than correctness. Remains a valid swap if a fully-in-Azure trust boundary is
66	  later required — the registry is config, not code.
67	- **Docker Hub.** Vendor-neutral and free for public images, but **pull-rate limits** (anon/free tiers)
68	  are a real risk under ACA scale-out, and it needs a **separate account + PAT** stored as an ACA
69	  registry credential. Strictly worse than GHCR here (GHCR has neither problem and reuses GitHub auth).
70	  Better reserved as an optional *additional* public distribution mirror if ever wanted.
71	
```

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/docs/adr/0024-app-deployment-infrastructure.md",
  "content": "# ADR 0024 — App deployment infrastructure: Terraform (ACA + SWA + KV + self-hosted Redis), separate from the harness\n\n- **Status:** Accepted\n- **Date:** 2026-06-27\n- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771\n- **Related:** ADR [0010](0010-provider-agnostic-infrastructure-seams.md) (Azure = one impl behind each\n  seam), [0013](0013-marketplace-distribution-and-anti-lock-in.md) (BYOL distribution), [0018](0018-results-surface-and-grafana-deferral.md)\n  (in-app surface → same-origin SPA), [0021](0021-demo-test-data-environment-strategy.md) (the harness\n  infra is out-of-repo and separate), [0023](0023-container-image-registry-ghcr.md) (GHCR registry).\n  Realizes the Week-7 deploy and supersedes the #379 scaffolding's ACR assumption.\n\n## Context\n\nWeek 7 is \"go to cloud.\" The #379 scaffolding documented a topology but had **no infra-as-code** for the\napp's own resources, and still assumed ACR (superseded by ADR 0023). Separately, the demo/datasource\ninfra already lives in an **out-of-repo** Terraform harness (ADR 0021) in the shared `dataq-rg`. We had\nto decide: where the app's production IaC lives, how it stays isolated from the harness, and the\nconcrete service choices (registry pull, Redis, secrets, frontend↔API wiring, CI auth).\n\n## Decision\n\n**Provision the app's production resources with a dedicated, in-repo Terraform stack at\n`deploy/terraform/`, reusing only the subscription + `dataq-rg`, and isolated from the harness.**\n\n- **In-repo IaC, local gitignored state.** Unlike the harness (out-of-repo, ADR 0021), this is the\n  *app's own* deploy config and belongs with the code; state is gitignored (it holds the generated\n  Postgres/Redis passwords). The provider lock is tracked.\n- **Strict separation in the shared RG.** All resources are `dataq-app-*` and tagged\n  `purpose=dataq-app` (harness = `dataq-harness-*` / `purpose=dataq-harness`). The RG is **referenced,\n  never managed** — an **idempotent `az group create` step** (preserving the existing `project=dataq`\n  tag) guarantees it exists without Terraform owning/destroying the shared RG.\n- **Compute = Azure Container Apps.** `dataq-api` (external ingress), `dataq-worker` (Celery + embedded\n  beat), `dataq-migrate` (manual Job: `alembic upgrade head`). All run the **same GHCR image** (ADR\n  0023), pulled **anonymously** (public package — no registry block/credential).\n- **Redis = self-hosted `redis:7-alpine` Container App** (internal TCP), not Azure Cache for Redis. The\n  Celery broker is transient (no persistence SLA needed); self-hosting is materially cheaper for v1. It\n  still requires a password (`--requirepass`) as defense-in-depth atop internal-only ingress.\n- **Secrets.** Key Vault (RBAC) is the app's runtime `SecretStore` (`SECRET_STORE=azure_key_vault`),\n  read via a **user-assigned managed identity** (Key Vault Secrets User). Boot-critical config\n  (`DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL`, App Insights) is injected as **inline Container App secrets**, *not* KV\n  references — decoupling first-revision activation from KV-RBAC propagation delay. Webhook secrets are\n  pre-seeded in KV.\n- **Frontend ↔ API = SWA Standard + linked backend.** The SPA uses a relative `/api/v1` base URL, so\n  the Static Web App links the `dataq-api` Container App as its backend and proxies `/api/*`\n  **same-origin** (CORS middleware stays off — consistent with the existing `staticwebapp.config.json`\n  and ADR 0018's same-origin authz). Linking uses `az staticwebapp backends link` (no azurerm resource\n  covers arbitrary linked backends).\n- **CI auth = AAD app registration + GitHub OIDC.** A `dataq-github-deploy` app registration with a\n  federated credential (`repo:…:environment:production`) — no stored client secret. Its Contributor\n  role is **scoped to the three deploy targets**, not the shared RG (least privilege; the RG holds\n  harness resources).\n- **Hardening toggles.** `postgres_public_network_access` (true for v1 over the allow-Azure-services\n  firewall + TLS; flip to false for the VNet-private path) and `key_vault_purge_protection` (false for\n  bring-up name reuse; true for prod) are explicit variables, not silent defaults.\n\n## Consequences\n\n**Positive**\n- App IaC is reviewable, reproducible, and idempotent (`plan` is clean on re-run); the shared RG and\n  harness resources are provably untouched (`az resource list … purpose=='dataq-app'`).\n- No Azure registry, no stored registry/CI secret (GHCR public + OIDC); cheapest viable Redis.\n- Same-origin SPA↔API needs no CORS and matches the committed SWA config.\n- Least-privilege CI principal can't reach harness resources in the shared RG.\n\n**Negative / watch**\n- **Self-hosted Redis** has no managed HA/persistence; a replica restart drops in-flight broker state\n  (acceptable for a Celery broker — tasks re-dispatch). Revisit Azure Cache if durability is needed.\n- **Postgres public access** (v1) is gated only by the allow-Azure-services rule + TLS + credentials;\n  the VNet-private path is the post-v1 hardening (variable already in place).\n- **Linked-backend via CLI** (`null_resource`) is outside Terraform's graph — re-link by tainting it if\n  the API resource id changes.\n- Cross-internet GHCR pulls add cold-start latency (already noted in ADR 0023).\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n- **Out-of-repo, harness-style (ADR 0021 precedent).** Rejected: that precedent is for *demo/datasource*\n  infra; the app's deploy config belongs with the app (state still gitignored, no secrets in files).\n- **Azure Cache for Redis (managed).** Rejected for v1 on cost; the broker doesn't need a managed SLA.\n- **SWA Free + CORS (absolute API URL).** Rejected: needs a frontend code change (relative `/api/v1`\n  baseURL) and re-introduces CORS; linked backend is the same-origin design already committed.\n- **User-assigned identity + federated cred for CI** (instead of an app registration). Viable and needs\n  no app-reg rights; the app registration was chosen for a cleaner separation of the CI principal.\n"
}
```

> AGENT

This is well worth doing, and the evidence is decisive. Look at what `environment.yml` actually installs:

```yaml
dependencies:
  - python=3.13
  - pip
  - pip:
    - -r backend/requirements-dev.txt   # ← everything
```

**Conda installs nothing from conda channels except the Python interpreter and pip itself.** All ~30 runtime deps come through pip wheels already. So conda's one real advantage — prebuilt binary packages from conda-forge — is **completely unused** here. You're paying conda's cost for none of its benefit.

## Verdict: yes, `python:3.13-slim` + pip is better for the cloud target

**Concrete wins — and they're exactly the pain we just hit:**
- **Image size:** `miniconda3` base (~600 MB) + the env → your **2.84 GB** image. `python:3.13-slim` + these wheels (multi-stage) → roughly **0.8–1.2 GB**. Smaller image = faster ACA cold-start/scale-out and less cross-internet GHCR pull latency — the precise concern ADR 0023 flagged.
- **Build:** simpler and much faster under the amd64 emulation we just fought; a multi-stage build drops the compiler/toolchain from the final layer.
- **No compilation risk:** every heavy dep (pyarrow, pandas, `snowflake-connector-python`, `databricks-sql-connector`, `great-expectations`, `psycopg2-binary`) ships manylinux wheels. (requirements.txt even already notes "swap psycopg2-binary for psycopg2 in the production image.")

## Two scopes — I'd recommend the first now

1. **Slim the production image only (low risk, big win):** convert `backend/Dockerfile` to multi-stage `python:3.13-slim` + `pip install -r requirements.txt`; keep conda for local dev. Image shrinks immediately, dev workflow untouched. Minor cost: a dev(conda)/prod(pip) split.
2. **Full switch to venv+pip everywhere:** retire `environment.yml`, update `setup.sh`/CI/docs, drop the "conda only" rule. Cleaner long-term, bigger blast radius.

## The catch

"Conda only" is a **locked Week-1 decision** (CLAUDE.md §6/§11). Flipping it properly needs an **ADR superseding that lock** (exactly like ADR 0017 superseded the Python-3.11 lock) plus updates to CONTRIBUTING/CLAUDE.md — so I won't change it silently. The only reason to *keep* conda would be a future dep that's genuinely painful via pip (rare in 2026, and not your case today).

**Nice synergy:** I already owe you a rebuild+push of `v1` (to apply the OCI-source label and link the GHCR package). That rebuild could just as easily produce the **slim image** instead — folding the size win into a step we're doing anyway.

Want me to:
- **(A)** make that linkage rebuild a multi-stage slim image now (+ write the ADR), or
- **(B)** keep `v1` as-is to finish the deploy, and do the slim switch as a separate ADR'd PR afterward?

Meanwhile the apply is at ~5 min — the 4 RP registrations are the long pole; dependent resources create once they're `Registered`. I'll continue when it completes.

2	# Build context is the repo ROOT (not backend/) because the app imports as the

7	# pinned environment.yml and its bin dir is put first on PATH so `uvicorn`,
8	# `celery`, `alembic`, and `python` resolve to it without a `conda run` wrapper
9	# (which would interfere with signal forwarding to uvicorn/celery).
10	FROM continuumio/miniconda3:24.11.1-0
11	
12	# Link the GHCR package to this repo (shows under the repo's Packages and lets the
13	# repo's Actions GITHUB_TOKEN push to it — ADR 0023/0024). Without this the package
14	# is user-scoped + unlinked, so CI can't push and ACA-pull access isn't inherited.
15	LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ"
16	LABEL org.opencontainers.image.description="DataQ backend (FastAPI API + Celery worker)"

23	# -typecheck / -tooling), so those must exist before `conda env create`. Copy
24	# just the requirements files (not all of backend/) so the env-create layer cache
25	# busts only on a pin change, not on every code edit.

27	COPY backend/requirements*.txt ./backend/

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/Dockerfile",
  "content": "# DataQ backend image — serves both the FastAPI API and the Celery worker.\n# Build context is the repo ROOT (not backend/) because the app imports as the\n# top-level `backend.app.*` package:\n#   docker build -f backend/Dockerfile .\n#\n# Multi-stage pip build on python:3.13-slim (ADR 0025). The production image uses\n# pip, NOT conda: every dependency already came through pip (environment.yml only\n# `-r`'d the requirements chain — conda installed no conda-channel packages), so\n# the miniconda base added ~1.5-2GB and build friction for no benefit. Conda stays\n# the LOCAL-DEV tool (environment.yml / setup.sh) per CLAUDE.md; only this image\n# changed. RUNTIME deps only (requirements.txt) — tests/tooling run in the dev env\n# (conda locally, pip in CI), never in this image.\n\n# ── Builder: install deps into an isolated venv ──────────────────────────────\nFROM python:3.13-slim AS builder\n\nENV PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1 \\\n    PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1\n\n# build-essential covers any sdist-only transitive dep; it lives ONLY in this\n# stage and never reaches the final image.\nRUN apt-get update \\\n    && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends build-essential \\\n    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*\n\nRUN python -m venv /opt/venv\nENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH\n\n# Copy just the requirements chain first so this layer caches on pin changes\n# only, not on every code edit. requirements.txt is the runtime SINGLE SOURCE OF\n# TRUTH (the dev/typecheck/tooling files are not installed into the image).\nCOPY backend/requirements*.txt ./backend/\nRUN pip install -r backend/requirements.txt\n\n# ── Runtime: slim base + the venv + app code ─────────────────────────────────\nFROM python:3.13-slim AS runtime\n\n# Link the GHCR package to this repo (shows under the repo's Packages and lets the\n# repo's Actions GITHUB_TOKEN push to it — ADR 0023/0024). Without this the package\n# is user-scoped + unlinked, so CI can't push and ACA-pull access isn't inherited.\nLABEL org.opencontainers.image.source=\"https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ\"\nLABEL org.opencontainers.image.description=\"DataQ backend (FastAPI API + Celery worker)\"\nLABEL org.opencontainers.image.licenses=\"MIT\"\n\nENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH \\\n    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \\\n    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1\n\nWORKDIR /workspace\n\n# The fully-built venv from the builder (no compilers / apt lists in this layer).\nCOPY --from=builder /opt/venv /opt/venv\n\n# Application code + tooling config (pyproject is imported for runtime config).\nCOPY pyproject.toml ./\nCOPY backend ./backend\n\nEXPOSE 8000\n\n# Default to the API; the worker overrides `command` (compose / Container App),\n# and the migrate job runs `alembic upgrade head`. psycopg2-binary (a wheel)\n# keeps the image apt-free; the psycopg2-source swap remains a deferred nicety.\nCMD [\"uvicorn\", \"backend.app.main:app\", \"--host\", \"0.0.0.0\", \"--port\", \"8000\"]\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/docs/adr/0025-production-image-pip-slim.md",
  "content": "# ADR 0025 — Production image: pip on `python:3.13-slim` (multi-stage); conda retained for local dev\n\n- **Status:** Accepted\n- **Date:** 2026-06-27\n- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771\n- **Related:** ADR [0017](0017-python-313-runtime-upgrade.md) (Python 3.13 runtime — same pinned\n  interpreter, different packager), [0023](0023-container-image-registry-ghcr.md) (GHCR pulls cross the\n  internet → image size = cold-start/scale-out latency), [0024](0024-app-deployment-infrastructure.md)\n  (ACA deploy this image runs on). Amends — does **not** fully revoke — the Week-1 \"conda only\" tooling\n  lock (CLAUDE.md §6/§11): conda stays for local dev; only the container image changes.\n\n## Context\n\nThe backend image was built on `continuumio/miniconda3` and created the `dataq` conda env at build\ntime. But `environment.yml` installs **nothing from conda channels** except the Python interpreter +\npip — its entire `dependencies:` is `pip: [-r backend/requirements-dev.txt]`. So conda's one real\nadvantage (prebuilt binary packages from conda-forge) was **unused**: all ~30 runtime deps already come\nfrom pip wheels.\n\nMeanwhile the Week-7 cloud move made image size load-bearing: the conda image was **~2.84 GB**, GHCR\npulls cross the internet (ADR 0023), and the amd64 image must be built under emulation locally. We were\npaying conda's full cost (base image + env + build friction) for none of its benefit.\n\n## Decision\n\n**Build the production image with pip on a multi-stage `python:3.13-slim`. Keep conda as the local-dev\ntool unchanged.**\n\n- **Multi-stage** ([backend/Dockerfile](../../backend/Dockerfile)): a `builder` stage (`python:3.13-slim`\n  + `build-essential`, discarded) installs `requirements.txt` into a `/opt/venv`; the `runtime` stage is\n  `python:3.13-slim` + that venv + the app code. No compilers / apt lists in the final layer.\n- **Runtime deps only** — the image installs `requirements.txt`, not the dev/typecheck/tooling chain.\n  Tests + linters run in the dev env (conda locally, `pip install` in CI), **never in the image**. CI\n  already uses `actions/setup-python` + pip directly, so it is unaffected.\n- **Same pinned deps + interpreter** — `requirements.txt` stays the single source of truth and Python\n  stays 3.13 (ADR 0017). Only the packager/base image changed.\n- **Local dev unchanged** — `environment.yml` / `setup.sh` / the conda workflow stay. CLAUDE.md's \"conda\n  only\" now means *local dev*; the production image is pip-on-slim.\n- `psycopg2-binary` (a wheel) is kept so the image stays apt-free; the psycopg2-source swap noted in\n  `requirements.txt` remains a deferred nicety.\n\n## Consequences\n\n**Positive**\n- **Image ~2.84 GB → ~0.8–1.2 GB.** Faster ACA cold-start + scale-out and smaller cross-internet GHCR\n  pulls (the ADR 0023 concern), and a faster local amd64 emulated build.\n- Smaller attack surface (no conda toolchain / build tools / dev+test deps in the runtime image).\n- Standard, portable container idiom (venv + slim) — friendlier for the BYOL/marketplace image (ADR\n  0013) than a conda base.\n\n**Negative / watch**\n- **Dev/prod packager split** (conda locally, pip in the image). Mitigated because deps + versions +\n  interpreter are identical (one requirements source, same 3.13); only the install mechanism differs.\n- In-container `pytest`/`mypy` no longer work (runtime-only image) — intentional; use the dev env.\n- A future conda-only dependency would reopen this; none exists today (all deps ship 3.13 wheels).\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n- **Keep conda in the image.** Rejected: ~2× the image size + slower builds for zero functional gain\n  (no conda-channel packages in use).\n- **Full switch to venv+pip everywhere** (retire conda, drop the §6 rule). Deferred: larger blast radius\n  (setup.sh / dev docs / contributor habits) for little extra benefit beyond this image. Can be a later\n  ADR if the dev/prod split proves annoying.\n- **Distroless / Alpine base.** Rejected for now: distroless complicates the venv + shell-form migrate\n  command; Alpine's musl breaks many manylinux wheels (would force source builds). `slim` (glibc) keeps\n  wheels working with most of the size win.\n"
}

Apply hit two issues:

1. **`MaxNumberOfRegionalEnvironmentsInSubExceeded`** — this subscription allows only **1 Container App Environment per region in West US 2**, and the harness already has `dataq-harness-cae` there. So our `dataq-app-cae` can't go in West US 2.
2. **Postgres `InternalServerError`** (a transient Azure error with a tracking ID) — usually clears on retry.

Fix for #1 with **minimal churn**: put only the ACA environment (and the container apps/redis/migrate job that live inside it) in **West US 3** (no ACA env there; harness Postgres already proves the region works), while the already-created Key Vault / Log Analytics / App Insights / identity stay in West US 2 (referenced cross-region, no replacement). > AGENT

Good question — and for DataQ specifically, App Service has a real downside. Here's the honest comparison:

## App Service (Web App for Containers)

**Benefits**
- **Full separation** — its own App Service Plan, nothing shared with the harness (satisfies "but that's it" cleanly).
- Mature platform niceties: deployment slots (staging→prod swap), easy custom domain/TLS, simple autoscale.
- Managed identity → Key Vault works identically; SWA *can* link an App Service backend, so the same-origin `/api` proxy still works.

**Downsides (these bite DataQ)**
- **The Celery worker doesn't fit.** App Service Linux containers must answer on an HTTP port or the platform's health check marks them unhealthy and restart-loops them. A Celery worker has no HTTP listener → you're forced into hacks (dummy HTTP server, or disabling health checks) or a separate awkward always-on web app. ACA treats a non-HTTP worker as a first-class app; App Service fights it.
- **Redis broker → Azure Cache for Redis.** App Service can't run our self-hosted `redis:7-alpine` sidecar cleanly, so you'd add managed Redis (~$16/mo Basic C0) — exactly the cost we avoided.
- **No native job primitive** for `alembic upgrade head` — migrations become a startup hook or a manual one-off, less clean than the ACA migrate Job.
- **More cost + rework**: App Service Plan + managed Redis, and a meaningful rewrite of the Terraform (diverges from ADR 0024).

## Shared harness ACA env (the recommended option)

**Benefit:** keeps the entire architecture intact — worker, self-hosted redis, and the migrate Job are all first-class; cheapest; immediate.
**Downside:** the compute *environment* is shared with the harness (shared env-level Log Analytics + internal network). The apps/KV/Postgres/identity stay separate and tagged. Notably, the shared internal network is exactly why I already password-protected redis — so that risk is mitigated. App lands in West US 2.

## My take

App Service is excellent for a pure API, but DataQ is **API + long-running Celery worker + a broker** — the two things App Service handles worst. So I'd rank: **share the ACA env > quota increase > App Service**. App Service only makes sense if full separation is non-negotiable *and* you're willing to take on managed Redis + the worker health-check workaround.

Given that, how do you want to proceed?

1	# ADR 0024 — App deployment infrastructure: Terraform (ACA + SWA + KV + self-hosted Redis), separate from the harness
2	
3	- **Status:** Accepted
4	- **Date:** 2026-06-27
5	- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771
6	- **Related:** ADR [0010](0010-provider-agnostic-infrastructure-seams.md) (Azure = one impl behind each
7	  seam), [0013](0013-marketplace-distribution-and-anti-lock-in.md) (BYOL distribution), [0018](0018-results-surface-and-grafana-deferral.md)
8	  (in-app surface → same-origin SPA), [0021](0021-demo-test-data-environment-strategy.md) (the harness
9	  infra is out-of-repo and separate), [0023](0023-container-image-registry-ghcr.md) (GHCR registry).
10	  Realizes the Week-7 deploy and supersedes the #379 scaffolding's ACR assumption.
11	
12	## Context
13	
14	Week 7 is "go to cloud." The #379 scaffolding documented a topology but had **no infra-as-code** for the
15	app's own resources, and still assumed ACR (superseded by ADR 0023). Separately, the demo/datasource
16	infra already lives in an **out-of-repo** Terraform harness (ADR 0021) in the shared `dataq-rg`. We had
17	to decide: where the app's production IaC lives, how it stays isolated from the harness, and the
18	concrete service choices (registry pull, Redis, secrets, frontend↔API wiring, CI auth).
19	
20	## Decision
21	
22	**Provision the app's production resources with a dedicated, in-repo Terraform stack at
23	`deploy/terraform/`, reusing only the subscription + `dataq-rg`, and isolated from the harness.**
24	
25	- **In-repo IaC, local gitignored state.** Unlike the harness (out-of-repo, ADR 0021), this is the
26	  *app's own* deploy config and belongs with the code; state is gitignored (it holds the generated
27	  Postgres/Redis passwords). The provider lock is tracked.
28	- **Strict separation in the shared RG.** All resources are `dataq-app-*` and tagged
29	  `purpose=dataq-app` (harness = `dataq-harness-*` / `purpose=dataq-harness`). The RG is **referenced,
30	  never managed** — an **idempotent `az group create` step** (preserving the existing `project=dataq`
31	  tag) guarantees it exists without Terraform owning/destroying the shared RG.
32	- **Compute = Azure Container Apps.** `dataq-api` (external ingress), `dataq-worker` (Celery + embedded
33	  beat), `dataq-migrate` (manual Job: `alembic upgrade head`). All run the **same GHCR image** (ADR
34	  0023), pulled **anonymously** (public package — no registry block/credential).
35	- **Redis = self-hosted `redis:7-alpine` Container App** (internal TCP), not Azure Cache for Redis. The
36	  Celery broker is transient (no persistence SLA needed); self-hosting is materially cheaper for v1. It
37	  still requires a password (`--requirepass`) as defense-in-depth atop internal-only ingress.
38	- **Secrets.** Key Vault (RBAC) is the app's runtime `SecretStore` (`SECRET_STORE=azure_key_vault`),
39	  read via a **user-assigned managed identity** (Key Vault Secrets User). Boot-critical config
40	  (`DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL`, App Insights) is injected as **inline Container App secrets**, *not* KV
41	  references — decoupling first-revision activation from KV-RBAC propagation delay. Webhook secrets are
42	  pre-seeded in KV.
43	- **Frontend ↔ API = SWA Standard + linked backend.** The SPA uses a relative `/api/v1` base URL, so
44	  the Static Web App links the `dataq-api` Container App as its backend and proxies `/api/*`
45	  **same-origin** (CORS middleware stays off — consistent with the existing `staticwebapp.config.json`
46	  and ADR 0018's same-origin authz). Linking uses `az staticwebapp backends link` (no azurerm resource
47	  covers arbitrary linked backends).
48	- **CI auth = AAD app registration + GitHub OIDC.** A `dataq-github-deploy` app registration with a
49	  federated credential (`repo:…:environment:production`) — no stored client secret. Its Contributor
50	  role is **scoped to the three deploy targets**, not the shared RG (least privilege; the RG holds
51	  harness resources).
52	- **Hardening toggles.** `postgres_public_network_access` (true for v1 over the allow-Azure-services
53	  firewall + TLS; flip to false for the VNet-private path) and `key_vault_purge_protection` (false for
54	  bring-up name reuse; true for prod) are explicit variables, not silent defaults.
55	
56	## Consequences
57	
58	**Positive**
59	- App IaC is reviewable, reproducible, and idempotent (`plan` is clean on re-run); the shared RG and
60	  harness resources are provably untouched (`az resource list … purpose=='dataq-app'`).
61	- No Azure registry, no stored registry/CI secret (GHCR public + OIDC); cheapest viable Redis.
62	- Same-origin SPA↔API needs no CORS and matches the committed SWA config.
63	- Least-privilege CI principal can't reach harness resources in the shared RG.
64	
65	**Negative / watch**
66	- **Self-hosted Redis** has no managed HA/persistence; a replica restart drops in-flight broker state
67	  (acceptable for a Celery broker — tasks re-dispatch). Revisit Azure Cache if durability is needed.
68	- **Postgres public access** (v1) is gated only by the allow-Azure-services rule + TLS + credentials;
69	  the VNet-private path is the post-v1 hardening (variable already in place).
70	- **Linked-backend via CLI** (`null_resource`) is outside Terraform's graph — re-link by tainting it if
71	  the API resource id changes.
72	- Cross-internet GHCR pulls add cold-start latency (already noted in ADR 0023).
73	
74	## Alternatives considered
75	
76	- **Out-of-repo, harness-style (ADR 0021 precedent).** Rejected: that precedent is for *demo/datasource*
77	  infra; the app's deploy config belongs with the app (state still gitignored, no secrets in files).
78	- **Azure Cache for Redis (managed).** Rejected for v1 on cost; the broker doesn't need a managed SLA.
79	- **SWA Free + CORS (absolute API URL).** Rejected: needs a frontend code change (relative `/api/v1`
80	  baseURL) and re-introduces CORS; linked backend is the same-origin design already committed.
81	- **User-assigned identity + federated cred for CI** (instead of an app registration). Viable and needs
82	  no app-reg rights; the app registration was chosen for a cleaner separation of the CI principal.
83	
```

> AGENT

**Answer: yes — ADR 0024 was the one that needed updating, and it's done.** The shared-env pivot made several of its claims stale; I revised:

- **Title + Decision:** "separate from the harness / reuse subscription + RG only" → now reuse the subscription, RG, **and the single Container Apps environment** (everything else stays separate `dataq-app-*`).
- **Context:** documented the `MaxNumberOfGlobalEnvironmentsInSubExceeded` hard cap (1 env/subscription) that forced env-sharing.
- **Naming/tags:** the shared env is the neutral `dataq-cae` / `purpose=dataq-shared`; apps renamed `dataq-app-api/worker/migrate`.
- **Consequences:** added the shared-env coupling (env rebuild from either side recreates both; container stdout co-mingles in `dataq-harness-logs` while app telemetry stays in `dataq-app-ai`; shared network/quota; ties back to why redis is password-protected).

The Postgres failure is **not transient** — it's now failed 3× with the same opaque `InternalServerError`, and this matches a documented gotcha (the harness's own notes describe Postgres Flexible Server leaving a **hidden name reservation** after a failed/dropped create). Our first attempt created then dropped `dataq-app-pg-wus3-aw6laj`, so that exact name is likely poisoned. Redis created fine; the apps depend on Postgres so they didn't proceed.

1	# App database — Postgres Flexible Server (Burstable B1ms). Public access +
2	# "allow Azure services" so the Container Apps environment reaches it without VNet
3	# integration (single-tenant v1). Password generated locally — never committed;
4	# state is gitignored. westus3 (see postgres_location) avoids the wus2 offer
5	# restriction the harness also hit.
6	
7	resource "random_password" "pg" {
8	  length  = 28
9	  special = false # keep the SQLAlchemy URL clean (no %-encoding)
10	}
11	
12	resource "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server" "app" {
13	  name                          = "dataq-app-pg-wus3-${random_string.suffix.result}"
14	  resource_group_name           = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name
15	  location                      = var.postgres_location
16	  version                       = "16"
17	  administrator_login           = var.postgres_admin_login
18	  administrator_password        = random_password.pg.result
19	  sku_name                      = var.postgres_sku
20	  storage_mb                    = 32768
21	  auto_grow_enabled             = true
22	  public_network_access_enabled = var.postgres_public_network_access
23	  zone                          = "1"
24	  tags                          = local.common_tags
25	}
26	
27	resource "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_database" "app" {
28	  name      = "dataq"
29	  server_id = azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.app.id
30	  collation = "en_US.utf8"
31	  charset   = "utf8"
32	}
33	
34	# start=end=0.0.0.0 is Azure's special "allow access from Azure services" rule —
35	# only meaningful while public access is on. Disappears under the VNet-private
36	# hardening path (var.postgres_public_network_access=false).
37	resource "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_firewall_rule" "azure_services" {
38	  count            = var.postgres_public_network_access ? 1 : 0
39	  name             = "allow-azure-services"
40	  server_id        = azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.app.id
41	  start_ip_address = "0.0.0.0"
42	  end_ip_address   = "0.0.0.0"
43	}
44	
45	locals {
46	  # psycopg2 URL the backend Settings read as DATABASE_URL. sslmode=require —
47	  # Flexible Server enforces TLS.
48	  database_url = join("", [
49	    "postgresql+psycopg2://",
50	    var.postgres_admin_login, ":", random_password.pg.result,
51	    "@", azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.app.fqdn, ":5432/",
52	    azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_database.app.name, "?sslmode=require",
53	  ])
54	}
55

> AGENT

The activity log shows no quota substatus — and the smoking gun is in the server list: `dataq-app-pg-wus3-aw6laj` is **still "Dropping"** from the prior attempt. Each retry reuses that same name (the suffix is stable) and collides with the still-dropping server → `InternalServerError`. Fix: give Postgres a **fresh, dedicated name suffix** (decoupled from the KV suffix) so it doesn't collide; the old one finishes dropping on its own.

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
id: toolu_01ALtF68V6VMzPrsMo5KfRh9
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/deploy/terraform/postgres.tf",
  "old_string": "resource \"random_password\" \"pg\" {\n  length  = 28\n  special = false # keep the SQLAlchemy URL clean (no %-encoding)\n}\n\nresource \"azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server\" \"app\" {\n  name                          = \"dataq-app-pg-wus3-${random_string.suffix.result}\"",
  "new_string": "resource \"random_password\" \"pg\" {\n  length  = 28\n  special = false # keep the SQLAlchemy URL clean (no %-encoding)\n}\n\n# Dedicated suffix for the Postgres name (NOT the shared random_string.suffix used\n# by the KV). Postgres Flexible Server leaves a hidden name reservation while a\n# failed server is still \"Dropping\", so a same-name retry InternalServerErrors. A\n# separate suffix lets us mint a fresh name on retry without churning the KV name.\nresource \"random_string\" \"pg_suffix\" {\n  length  = 6\n  lower   = true\n  upper   = false\n  numeric = true\n  special = false\n}\n\nresource \"azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server\" \"app\" {\n  name                          = \"dataq-app-pg-${random_string.pg_suffix.result}\""
}
```

> AGENT

Two new instructions — but the **"rename the server"** one hits a hard conflict I need to surface before acting, because executing it literally would be destructive *and* likely fail:

**Renaming the shared Postgres server isn't safely feasible right now.** Azure Postgres server names are immutable, so a rename = **recreate**, which means:
1. **Data loss:** the existing server holds airflow's *metadata* database — destroying/recreating the server wipes airflow's history/connections (it'd re-init from scratch).
2. **It hits the very capacity wall we just hit:** Terraform would destroy the old server first, then try to create the new-named one — the exact operation that's failed ~4× with `InternalServerError`. That could leave **both** airflow *and* the app with **no database**.

The env rename was safe (its state lives in Postgres, which we didn't touch); a Postgres-server rename is a different animal. So I don't want to gamble the working harness DB on it.

The **"distinct db names"** part I can do cleanly regardless: the app gets its own database, clearly distinct from airflow's (`airflow` → app's `dataq`), plus its own `dataq_app` role. And yes, I'll **update ADR 0024** to record the shared-Postgres decision once we settle this.

1	# Airflow metadata database — Postgres Flexible Server (Burstable B1ms, cheapest).
2	# Public access + "allow Azure services" so the Container Apps Environment reaches it
3	# without VNet integration (fine for a disposable harness). Password generated locally
4	# (random_password) — never committed; state is gitignored.
5	
6	resource "random_password" "pg" {
7	  length  = 24
8	  special = false # keep the SQLAlchemy URL clean (no %-encoding)
9	}
10	
11	resource "azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server" "airflow" {
12	  # "-wus3" (westus3) marker: westus2 is offer-restricted (left a hidden 409 name
13	  # reservation); centralus worked but its cross-region latency starved the Airflow
14	  # scheduler. westus3 is adjacent to westus2 → low latency. New marker avoids the
15	  # centralus server's name on teardown.
16	  name                          = "dataq-airflow-pg-wus3-${random_string.suffix.result}"
17	  resource_group_name           = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name
18	  # Postgres Flexible Server is offer-restricted in West US 2 for this subscription
19	  # (LocationIsOfferRestricted at apply); centralus is unrestricted. Cross-region from
20	  # the Container Apps env is fine — public access + allow-Azure-services firewall.
21	  location                      = var.postgres_location
22	  version                       = "16"

  "content": "# App database — a DISTINCT `dataq` database on the SHARED Postgres Flexible Server\n# (this subscription caps Flexible Servers at 1, so the app shares the harness's\n# server — renamed neutrally to dataq-pg-* / purpose=dataq-shared). > AGENT

Found it: `permission denied for schema public` when alembic creates tables. `dataq_app` owns the `dataq` database but (PG15+ behavior) lacks `CREATE` on its `public` schema. Fix: grant it on the schema, then re-run the migrate job:

> TOOL

tool_use Bash
id: toolu_0136GhRhnaUbTdz2j6wCQZRw
```json
{
  "command": "bash -c '\nset -e\nPGBIN=/opt/homebrew/opt/libpq/bin\nPW=$(terraform -chdir=/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/terraform show -json 2>/dev/null | python3 -c \"import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(next(r[\\\"values\\\"][\\\"result\\\"] for r in d[\\\"values\\\"][\\\"root_module\\\"][\\\"resources\\\"] if r[\\\"address\\\"]==\\\"random_password.pg\\\"))\")\nexport PGPASSWORD=\"REDACTED\" PGSSLMODE=require\nH=dataq-pg-wus3-3erlgd.postgres.database.azure.com\n# Grant the app role CREATE/USAGE on its db public schema (PG15+ no longer grants this to the db owner by default).\n\"$PGBIN/psql\" -h \"$H\" -U airflowadmin -d dataq -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c \"GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA public TO dataq_app;\" -c \"ALTER SCHEMA public OWNER TO dataq_app;\"\necho \"GRANTED\"\n'",
  "description": "Grant dataq_app privileges on public schema of dataq db"
}

The API is **crash-looping** — and it's a real prod bug, not infra. On the first log call at startup ([main.py:44](backend/app/main.py#L44)), the App-Insights logging handler (active because `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING` is set) hits `with self.lock:` where `self.lock` is `None` → `TypeError`, "Application startup failed." This only triggers when App Insights is enabled in prod — which had never run before. Let me look at the logging wiring:

> AGENT

Root cause confirmed: it's **opencensus `AzureLogHandler`** specifically — the `app_startup` JSON line *did* emit via the StreamHandler, but the same record crashes in the App-Insights handler whose `.lock` is `None` (opencensus is unmaintained and not tested on Python 3.13; stdlib `Handler.handle()` does `with self.lock`). A real prod defect, surfaced now because App Insights had never run live.

Per the working agreement (defect → issue → fix with `Fixes #N`), let me file the issue first:

Issue **#393** filed. Now the fix — ensure the handler has a lock before attaching:

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
id: toolu_011wD5tqskM9qaEZSpoJjxtL
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/core/logging.py",
  "old_string": "        ai_handler = AzureLogHandler(connection_string=conn)\n        ai_handler.setLevel(level)\n        root.addHandler(ai_handler)",
  "new_string": "        ai_handler = AzureLogHandler(connection_string=conn)\n        # opencensus-ext-azure (unmaintained, not tested on Python 3.13 — ADR 0017)\n        # can leave the handler's .lock unset (None). stdlib Handler.handle() does\n        # `with self.lock`, so a None lock crashes app startup the first time a\n        # record is emitted. Ensure a real lock. (#393 — proper fix: migrate to\n        # azure-monitor-opentelemetry; opencensus is EOL.)\n        if getattr(ai_handler, \"lock\", None) is None:\n            ai_handler.createLock()\n        ai_handler.setLevel(level)\n        root.addHandler(ai_handler)"
}
```

> AGENT

Critical finding: the v2 image **does** have my fix (`createLock()` at line 115), yet it still crashes with `lock=None`. That means opencensus **overrides `createLock()` to set `self.lock = None`** (its `BaseLogHandler` does its own queue-based thread-safety) — so calling `createLock()` re-nulls it. Let me confirm by inspecting opencensus in the image:

> TOOL

tool_use Bash
id: toolu_01UVJY9J9Mj1ZD3PadXWYLtd
```json
{
  "command": "docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 --entrypoint sh ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:v2 -c \"grep -rn 'def createLock\\|self.lock' /opt/venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/opencensus/ext/azure/ /opt/venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/opencensus/common/ 2>/dev/null | head -20\" 2>&1",
  "description": "Inspect opencensus createLock/lock handling"
}
```

> TOOL

tool_result
id: toolu_01UVJY9J9Mj1ZD3PadXWYLtd
```
/opt/venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/opencensus/ext/azure/log_exporter/__init__.py:105:    def createLock(self):
/opt/venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/opencensus/ext/azure/log_exporter/__init__.py:106:        self.lock = None
```

> AGENT

Confirmed — opencensus `createLock()` literally does `self.lock = None` (it uses its own queue for thread-safety), and Python 3.13's `Handler.handle()` does `with self.lock` with no None-check. So `createLock()` was exactly the wrong call. The fix is to force a real lock **after** construction:

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
id: toolu_017i8VxhFbHUcWtFZNnzmc6C
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/core/logging.py",
  "old_string": "        ai_handler = AzureLogHandler(connection_string=conn)\n        # opencensus-ext-azure (unmaintained, not tested on Python 3.13 — ADR 0017)\n        # can leave the handler's .lock unset (None). stdlib Handler.handle() does\n        # `with self.lock`, so a None lock crashes app startup the first time a\n        # record is emitted. Ensure a real lock. (#393 — proper fix: migrate to\n        # azure-monitor-opentelemetry; opencensus is EOL.)\n        if getattr(ai_handler, \"lock\", None) is None:\n            ai_handler.createLock()\n        ai_handler.setLevel(level)\n        root.addHandler(ai_handler)",
  "new_string": "        ai_handler = AzureLogHandler(connection_string=conn)\n        # opencensus-ext-azure (unmaintained, not tested on Python 3.13 — ADR 0017)\n        # overrides createLock() to set `self.lock = None` (it does its own\n        # queue-based thread-safety). That was fine on older Python, but 3.13's\n        # logging.Handler.handle() does `with self.lock` with no None-check, so the\n        # first emitted record crashes app startup. Force a real lock directly\n        # (assigning, NOT createLock() which would re-null it). (#393 — proper fix:\n        # migrate to azure-monitor-opentelemetry; opencensus is EOL.)\n        ai_handler.lock = threading.RLock()\n        ai_handler.setLevel(level)\n        root.addHandler(ai_handler)"
}
```

> AGENT

**The logging crash is fixed!** v3 gets past it (app_startup logged cleanly). Now it fails on a *different, expected* error: `init_auth()` fails-closed because `AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID` is empty — my "empty SSO is fine for first deploy" assumption was wrong; the app requires real Azure AD SSO config at startup in prod.

Good news: the SSO app registrations **already exist** — `secrets.sh` exports `AZURE_TENANT_ID`/`AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID`/`AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID`. So this is a config-only fix (no rebuild): re-apply with those values wired in.

> AGENT

Two problems surfaced:

1. **KV 403 (`ForbiddenByRbac`)**: sourcing `secrets.sh` exported `ARM_CLIENT_ID/SECRET`, so Terraform authenticated as the **harness SP** (Contributor only, no Key Vault data-plane role) instead of my Owner login. The dataq-app stack must run as *my* az-login, not the harness SP — I shouldn't source secrets.sh for it.
2. **SSO client IDs are blank** in secrets.sh (only tenant is set) — so I need to find or create the real Azure AD app registrations.

{
  "command": "cd /Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ; git add backend/app/core/logging.py && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'\nfix(logging): force a real lock on the App Insights handler (Py3.13)\n\nopencensus AzureLogHandler.createLock() sets self.lock=None (it does its own\nqueue-based thread-safety). That was fine on older Python, but Python 3.13's\nlogging.Handler.handle() does `with self.lock` with no None-check, so the first\nemitted record crashed API startup whenever App Insights was enabled — only\nsurfaced now, on the first live cloud run. Assign a real RLock directly after\nconstruction (not createLock(), which re-nulls it). Verified locally with App\nInsights enabled. Proper fix (migrate opencensus -> azure-monitor-opentelemetry)\ntracked in #393.\n\nFixes #393\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\ngit add deploy/terraform/ docs/adr/0024-app-deployment-infrastructure.md && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'\nrefactor(deploy): share ACA env (dataq-cae) + shared Postgres (dataq-pg)\n\nThe subscription is hard-capped at ONE Container App Environment AND one Postgres\nFlexible Server (free/trial tier; a 2nd of each InternalServerErrors). So the app\nshares both with the harness, keeping everything else separate:\n\n- ACA env: reference the harness env via data source (renamed neutrally to\n  dataq-cae / purpose=dataq-shared in the harness TF); app apps renamed\n  dataq-app-api/worker/migrate; migrate job + SWA backend-region bind to the\n  shared env's region (westus2). Drop the aca_location var.\n- Postgres: the harness server is renamed neutrally (dataq-pg-* / dataq-shared,\n  recreated via backup+restore); the app uses a DISTINCT `dataq` database owned by\n  a least-privilege `dataq_app` role (provisioned out-of-band; see README).\n  DATABASE_URL built from var.app_db_password; runtime reach via allow-azure-svcs.\n- Image bumped to v3 (the #393 logging fix).\n- ADR 0024 updated: shared env + shared Postgres, coupling consequences, the\n  1-of-each cap, and the alternatives (quota increase / App Service) considered.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\ngit log --oneline -3",

`redirectUri = window.location.origin` (no trailing slash), `authority = login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>` (v2), and the API identifier URI must be `api://<api_client_id>`. Now writing the SSO app registrations as `sso.tf`:

> TOOL

tool_use Write
id: toolu_01Pme7BBcg18MySjzApRTaKH
```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/deploy/terraform/sso.tf",
  "content": "# Azure AD SSO app registrations (real auth in prod; AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=false). The\n# backend's init_auth() requires AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID + AZURE_TENANT_ID at startup\n# and validates v2 access tokens; the SPA (MSAL) uses AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID with a\n# redirect URI of the SWA origin. Two registrations:\n#   - API  (dataq-app-api-sso): exposes the `user_impersonation` scope, v2 tokens.\n#   - SPA  (dataq-app-spa): public single-page client, redirect = SWA origin,\n#                           pre-authorized on the API scope (no consent prompt).\n\ndata \"azuread_client_config\" \"current\" {}\n\nresource \"random_uuid\" \"api_scope\" {}\n\n# ── API app registration ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nresource \"azuread_application\" \"api\" {\n  display_name = \"dataq-app-api-sso\"\n  owners       = [data.azuread_client_config.current.object_id]\n\n  api {\n    requested_access_token_version = 2 # v2 tokens (login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/v2.0)\n\n    oauth2_permission_scope {\n      id                         = random_uuid.api_scope.result\n      value                      = var.azure_api_scope\n      type                       = \"User\"\n      enabled                    = true\n      admin_consent_display_name = \"Access the DataQ API\"\n      admin_consent_description  = \"Allow the application to access the DataQ API on behalf of the signed-in user.\"\n      user_consent_display_name  = \"Access the DataQ API\"\n      user_consent_description   = \"Allow the application to access the DataQ API on your behalf.\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n# api://<client_id> identifier URI (separate resource — needs the client_id known).\nresource \"azuread_application_identifier_uri\" \"api\" {\n  application_id = azuread_application.api.id\n  identifier_uri = \"api://${azuread_application.api.client_id}\"\n}\n\nresource \"azuread_service_principal\" \"api\" {\n  client_id = azuread_application.api.client_id\n  owners    = [data.azuread_client_config.current.object_id]\n}\n\n# ── SPA app registration ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────\nresource \"azuread_application\" \"spa\" {\n  display_name = \"dataq-app-spa\"\n  owners       = [data.azuread_client_config.current.object_id]\n\n  single_page_application {\n    # MSAL uses window.location.origin (no trailing slash) — frontend/src/auth/msalInstance.ts.\n    redirect_uris = [\"https://${azurerm_static_web_app.app.default_host_name}\"]\n  }\n\n  # Request the API's user_impersonation scope.\n  required_resource_access {\n    resource_app_id = azuread_application.api.client_id\n    resource_access {\n      id   = random_uuid.api_scope.result\n      type = \"Scope\"\n    }\n  }\n\n  # Microsoft Graph User.Read (sign-in + read profile).\n  required_resource_access {\n    resource_app_id = \"00000003-0000-0000-c000-000000000000\"\n    resource_access {\n      id   = \"e1fe6dd8-ba31-4d61-89e7-88639da4683d\" # User.Read\n      type = \"Scope\"\n    }\n  }\n}\n\nresource \"azuread_service_principal\" \"spa\" {\n  client_id = azuread_application.spa.client_id\n  owners    = [data.azuread_client_config.current.object_id]\n}\n\n# Pre-authorize the SPA on the API scope so users aren't prompted to consent to\n# the custom API (same-tenant, single product).\nresource \"azuread_application_pre_authorized\" \"spa_on_api\" {\n  application_id       = azuread_application.api.id\n  authorized_client_id = azuread_application.spa.client_id\n  permission_ids       = [random_uuid.api_scope.result]\n}\n"
}

1	# DataQ — app infra (Terraform)
2	
3	Provisions the DataQ **application's own** production resources into the existing
4	`dataq-rg`. Deliberately **separate** from the harness stack
5	(`~/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/terraform`, ADR 0021) — only the subscription +
6	RG are shared. All resources here are prefixed `dataq-app-*` and tagged
7	`purpose=dataq-app`; the harness's `dataq-harness-*` / `purpose=dataq-harness`
8	resources are never touched.
9	
10	## What it creates
11	
12	| Resource | Name |
13	|---|---|
14	| Log Analytics workspace | `dataq-app-logs` |
15	| Application Insights | `dataq-app-ai` |
16	| User-assigned identity | `dataq-app-id` (api/worker → Key Vault) |
17	| Key Vault (RBAC) | `dataq-app-kv-<suffix>` (SecretStore + webhook secrets) |
18	| Postgres Flexible Server | `dataq-app-pg-wus3-<suffix>` (westus3, B1ms) |
19	| Container Apps environment | `dataq-app-cae` |
20	| Redis broker (Container App) | `dataq-app-redis` (internal TCP) |
21	| API / worker / migrate | `dataq-api` · `dataq-worker` · `dataq-migrate` (job) |
22	| Static Web App (Standard) | `dataq-app-web` (+ linked api backend) |
23	| GitHub-deploy app registration | `dataq-github-deploy` (OIDC federated cred) |
24	
25	Backend image: `ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:<image_tag>` (GHCR, public —
26	ACA pulls anonymously, ADR 0023). It must exist + be **public** before apply.
27	
28	## Prerequisites
29	
30	- `az login` as a subscription **Owner** (this stack registers RPs + creates role
31	  assignments + an AAD app registration).
32	- The GHCR backend image pushed + public (see repo root `deploy/README.md` /
33	  the Week-7 bring-up steps).
34	- State is **local + gitignored** — do not commit `terraform.tfstate`.
35	
36	## Apply
37	
38	```bash
39	cd deploy/terraform
40	cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars   # optional; defaults work
41	terraform init
42	terraform plan      # review
43	terraform apply
44	```
45	
46	## After apply — wire the Deploy workflow
47	
48	`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` reads these. Push them with `gh` from the outputs:
49	
50	```bash
51	gh secret  set AZURE_CLIENT_ID       -b "$(terraform output -raw github_actions_client_id)"
52	gh secret  set AZURE_TENANT_ID       -b "$(terraform output -raw azure_tenant_id)"
53	gh secret  set AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID -b "$(terraform output -raw azure_subscription_id)"
54	gh secret  set AZURE_STATIC_WEB_APPS_API_TOKEN -b "$(terraform output -raw swa_api_token)"
55	gh variable set AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP -b "$(terraform output -raw resource_group)"
56	gh variable set API_APP_NAME         -b "$(terraform output -raw api_app_name)"
57	gh variable set WORKER_APP_NAME      -b "$(terraform output -raw worker_app_name)"
58	gh variable set MIGRATE_JOB_NAME     -b "$(terraform output -raw migrate_job_name)"
59	# Plus the non-secret VITE_AZURE_* build vars (tenant/spa/api client ids + scope).
60	```
61	
62	Create the `production` GitHub environment (the federated credential subject is
63	`repo:<owner>/<repo>:environment:production`).
64	
65	## Verify
66	
67	```bash
68	# Exactly the app stack — harness untouched:
69	az resource list -g dataq-rg --query "[?tags.purpose=='dataq-app'].name" -o tsv
70	
71	# Re-plan is clean (idempotent):
72	terraform plan      # expect: No changes
73	
74	# API health + Swagger:
75	curl -fsS "$(terraform output -raw api_url)/docs" >/dev/null && echo OK
76	```
77	
```

  "content": "# DataQ — app infra (Terraform)\n\nProvisions the DataQ **application's own** production resources into the existing\n`dataq-rg`. Separate from the harness stack\n(`~/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/terraform`, ADR 0021), **except** for three shared\nresources forced by free/trial subscription caps (1 Container App Environment and\n1 Postgres Flexible Server per subscription — see ADR 0024):\n\n- the **subscription** + **resource group** (`dataq-rg`),\n- the **Container Apps environment** `dataq-cae` (neutral name, `purpose=dataq-shared`),\n- the **Postgres Flexible Server** `dataq-pg-wus3-*` (neutral, `purpose=dataq-shared`).\n\nBoth shared resources are **owned by the harness Terraform**; this stack only\n*references* them (data sources). Everything the app creates is `dataq-app-*` /\n`purpose=dataq-app`; the harness's `dataq-harness-*` resources are untouched.\n\n## What it creates\n\n| Resource | Name |\n|---|---|\n| Log Analytics workspace | `dataq-app-logs` |\n| Application Insights | `dataq-app-ai` |\n| User-assigned identity | `dataq-app-id` (api/worker → Key Vault) |\n| Key Vault (RBAC) | `dataq-app-kv-<suffix>` (SecretStore + webhook secrets) |\n| API / worker / migrate | `dataq-app-api` · `dataq-app-worker` · `dataq-app-migrate` (job) |\n| Redis broker (Container App) | `dataq-app-redis` (internal TCP, password-auth) |\n| Static Web App (Standard) | `dataq-app-web` (+ linked `dataq-app-api` backend) |\n| Azure AD SSO app regs | `dataq-app-api-sso` (API) + `dataq-app-spa` (SPA) |\n| GitHub-deploy app registration | `dataq-github-deploy` (OIDC federated cred) |\n\n**Referenced, not created:** the `dataq-cae` environment and the\n`dataq-pg-wus3-*` server (both harness-owned). The app's database is a **distinct\n`dataq` database** + least-privilege **`dataq_app`** role on the shared server.\n\nBackend image: `ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:<image_tag>` (GHCR, public —\nACA pulls anonymously, ADR 0023). Must exist + be **public** before apply.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n- `az login` as a subscription **Owner** (registers RPs; creates role assignments,\n  AAD app registrations, and Key Vault secrets). **Do not** `source` the harness\n  `secrets.sh` — that switches Terraform to the harness SP, which lacks Key Vault\n  data-plane rights (403) and isn't the right identity for this stack.\n- The shared `dataq-cae` env + `dataq-pg-wus3-*` server already exist (harness).\n- The GHCR backend image pushed + public.\n- The `dataq` database + `dataq_app` role provisioned (one-off, below).\n- State is **local + gitignored**.\n\n## Shared Postgres — one-off role + database\n\nThe app's DB lives on the shared server but is provisioned **out-of-band** (keeps\nthis stack connection-free / CI-friendly — no postgres provider). Run once,\nconnected as the server admin (add a temp firewall rule for your IP first):\n\n```sql\n-- as the server admin, against the `postgres` database:\nCREATE ROLE dataq_app LOGIN PASSWORD '<generated>';\nCREATE DATABASE dataq OWNER dataq_app;\n-- then, connected to the `dataq` database (PG15+ doesn't grant the db owner\n-- CREATE on public by default):\nGRANT ALL ON SCHEMA public TO dataq_app;\nALTER SCHEMA public OWNER TO dataq_app;\n```\n\nPass that password at apply time as `TF_VAR_app_db_password` (it becomes the\n`DATABASE_URL` Container App secret; never committed). The app reaches the server\nat runtime over the server's allow-Azure-services firewall rule.\n\n## Apply\n\n```bash\ncd deploy/terraform\nterraform init\nTF_VAR_app_db_password='REDACTED' terraform plan    # review\nTF_VAR_app_db_password='REDACTED' terraform apply\n```\n\n## After apply — wire the Deploy workflow\n\n`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` reads these. Push them with `gh` from the outputs:\n\n```bash\ngh secret  set AZURE_CLIENT_ID       -b \"$(terraform output -raw github_actions_client_id)\"\ngh secret  set AZURE_TENANT_ID       -b \"$(terraform output -raw azure_tenant_id)\"\ngh secret  set AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID -b \"$(terraform output -raw azure_subscription_id)\"\ngh secret  set AZURE_STATIC_WEB_APPS_API_TOKEN -b \"$(terraform output -raw swa_api_token)\"\ngh variable set AZURE_RESOURCE_GROUP -b \"$(terraform output -raw resource_group)\"\ngh variable set API_APP_NAME         -b \"$(terraform output -raw api_app_name)\"\ngh variable set WORKER_APP_NAME      -b \"$(terraform output -raw worker_app_name)\"\ngh variable set MIGRATE_JOB_NAME     -b \"$(terraform output -raw migrate_job_name)\"\ngh variable set VITE_AZURE_TENANT_ID    -b \"$(terraform output -raw azure_tenant_id)\"\ngh variable set VITE_AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID -b \"$(terraform output -raw azure_spa_client_id)\"\ngh variable set VITE_AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID -b \"$(terraform output -raw azure_api_client_id)\"\ngh variable set VITE_AZURE_API_SCOPE    -b \"$(terraform output -raw azure_api_scope)\"\n```\n\nCreate the `production` GitHub environment (federated-credential subject\n`repo:<owner>/<repo>:environment:production`). **One-time GHCR step:** in the\n`dataq-backend` package settings, *Connect repository* + grant the repo Actions\n**write** access so the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` can push (label-linking alone\ndoesn't grant it for user-scoped packages).\n\n## Verify\n\n```bash\n# App resources only — harness untouched:\naz resource list -g dataq-rg --query \"[?tags.purpose=='dataq-app'].name\" -o tsv\n\n# API up (401 = healthy + auth-enforced):\ncurl -s -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code}\\n\" \"$(terraform output -raw api_url)/api/v1/runs\"\n\n# SPA + same-origin /api proxy:\ncurl -s -o /dev/null -w \"%{http_code}\\n\" \"$(terraform output -raw swa_url)/\"\n```\n"
}

Good question. My call: **a single PR**, not chained.

**Why single:** these 13 commits are one cohesive, already-applied-and-verified milestone (the deploy literally doesn't function without all of them — image + infra + shared-env/PG + SSO + frontend). The repo **squash-merges into `main`**, so any PR collapses to one commit regardless; chaining tightly-coupled changes into stacked PRs would be artificial overhead and force a rebase/re-verify of live infra. The per-functionality commits stay visible *inside* the PR for review granularity. (The one arguably-separable piece — the #393 backend logging fix — is already its own clean commit with `Fixes #393`.)

Fix: only tolerate the specific 'already linked' case; fail on other errors, or check link state. If the status query returns an empty/unexpected string (control-plane hiccup, CLI status rename), the loop falls through and polls until the 15-min deadline before failing. It still fails-closed (timeout→exit 1), so the gate holds, but feedback is delayed and the prod concurrency group is tied up. Fix: treat unknown/empty status with a bounded retry + clearer abort. # Betterleaks Configuration Details

## 1. Auto-detected Config File

The documentation does not specify the exact filename or auto-detection mechanism. It only references "the `betterleaks.toml` file" as controlling detection and filtering, but doesn't confirm whether this is `.betterleaks.toml` at repo root or how `betterleaks git /repo` discovers it.

## 2. Extending Default Rules

The config includes an `[extend]` field to "inherit rules/settings from another config or from built-in defaults." The documentation doesn't provide concrete TOML syntax examples for this inheritance mechanism, so the exact usage pattern isn't detailed here.

## 3. Global Filter Expression & Available Variables

For filter expressions, three data sources are available:

- **`attributes`**: Source metadata including `"path"`, `"git.sha"`, `"git.author_name"`, etc.
- **`finding`**: Matched secret data with keys like `"secret"`, `"match"`, `"rule_id"`, and `"description"`
- **`captures`**: Named regex capture groups (validate scope only)

### Example Filter Expressions

Path-based allowlisting:
```expr
filter.matchesAny(get(attributes, "path", ""), [`^tests/fixtures/`])
```

Filename filtering (documentation markdown/text files):
```expr
filter.matchesAny(get(attributes, "path", ""), [`(?i)\.(?:md|txt|csv)$`])
```

Excluding specific rule IDs would use the `finding["rule_id"]` variable, though the provided examples don't demonstrate rule-ID exclusion directly.

1. **The real bug:** in my `bl.toml` the `filter` key sat *after* `[extend]`, so TOML scoped it as `extend.filter` (nested), not the **top-level** global `filter` — that's why it never applied (and why `filter="true"` just now still found 2). The mechanism + `attributes.path` (`sub/full.jsonl`, `resource: git.patch_content` — matches CI exactly) are right; the placement was wrong.
2. **On the PEM:** correct — a properly-formatted PEM *should* be caught; mine had placeholder (non-base64) body so it failed the rule's checks. I was trial-fitting a detectable token instead of using a real one. ```
# Global `filter` CEL Expression Variables

## Variable Access Syntax

For the global `filter` expression, variables are accessed as:
- `attributes[?"path"]` (optional access with `.orValue()` fallback)
- `finding["secret"]` (map-style indexing)

There is no direct `attributes.path` dot notation or dedicated `get()`/`has()` function shown.

## Exact Examples from Documentation

The doc provides this working example:

```toml
filter = '''
(
    attributes[?"git.author_name"].orValue("").endsWith("[bot]") &&
    attributes[?"path"].orValue("").startsWith("tests/fixtures/")
)
```

Another snippet shows:

```toml
filter.matchesAny(attributes[?"path"].orValue(""), [r"""(?i)\.(?:md|txt|csv)$"""])
```

## Evaluation Logic

"If a filter expression evaluates to `true`, the item is skipped." Therefore, findings are **discarded when the expression returns true**.
```

=== airflow.tf ===
# Airflow on Container Apps — scheduler + webserver (LocalExecutor), backed by the
# Postgres metadata DB. min_replicas = 1 (the scheduler can't scale to zero); HTTPS
# ingress so Event-Grid (file-landing push) and DataQ can reach it. ~$25-75/mo always-on.
#
# Starts on the public airflow image (no DAGs). §3 swaps `airflow_image` for a custom
# registry image (FROM apache/airflow + COPY dags/) that calls the mockdata tick CLI / loads.

resource "random_id" "fernet" {
  byte_length = 32
}

resource "random_password" "airflow_webserver_secret" {
  length  = 32
  special = false
}

resource "random_password" "airflow_admin" {
  length  = 20
  special = false
}

locals {
  # Valid Fernet key = url-safe base64 of 32 bytes (swap +/ for -_, keep padding).
  airflow_fernet_key = replace(replace(random_id.fernet.b64_std, "+", "-"), "/", "_")

  airflow_pg_conn = join("", [
    "postgresql+psycopg2://",
    var.postgres_admin_login, ":", random_password.pg.result,
    "@", azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.airflow.fqdn, ":5432/",
    azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_database.airflow.name, "?sslmode=require",
  ])

  # Custom registry image (apache/airflow + the harness DAGs + client libs).
  airflow_image = "${azurerm_container_registry.harness.login_server}/airflow-dataq:${var.airflow_image_tag}"

  # CeleryExecutor: Redis broker (internal) + Postgres result backend. Workers run in a
  # SEPARATE, horizontally scalable container app (airflow_worker.tf) — that's what lifts
  # the single-executor / 2-vCPU-per-replica ceiling that throttled LocalExecutor.
  # Container Apps internal service-to-service: the short app name resolves over the
  # environment's internal DNS (the full .internal. FQDN did not connect for TCP).
  celery_broker_url = "redis://${azurerm_container_app.redis.name}:6379/0"
  celery_result_backend = join("", [
    "db+postgresql://",
    var.postgres_admin_login, ":", random_password.pg.result,
    "@", azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.airflow.fqdn, ":5432/",
    azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_database.airflow.name, "?sslmode=require",
  ])

  # Shared scheduler + webserver env (DRYed into both containers via dynamic blocks).
  # LocalExecutor runs tasks in the scheduler, so the connection env must live here.
  airflow_env = [
    { name = "AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_CONN", secret_name = "pg-conn" },
    { name = "AIRFLOW__CORE__EXECUTOR", value = "CeleryExecutor" },
    { name = "AIRFLOW__CELERY__BROKER_URL", value = local.celery_broker_url },
    { name = "AIRFLOW__CELERY__RESULT_BACKEND", secret_name = "celery-result-backend" },
    # Tasks per worker replica — each cold-starts a fresh interpreter, so keep it modest
    # vs the worker's 2 vCPU / 4 GiB; horizontal scaling (more replicas) is the lever.
    { name = "AIRFLOW__CELERY__WORKER_CONCURRENCY", value = "3" },
    { name = "AIRFLOW__CORE__FERNET_KEY", secret_name = "fernet-key" },
    { name = "AIRFLOW__WEBSERVER__SECRET_KEY", secret_name = "webserver-secret" },
    { name = "AIRFLOW__CORE__LOAD_EXAMPLES", value = "False" },
    # Enable basic-auth on the REST API so DAG runs can be triggered programmatically.
    { name = "AIRFLOW__API__AUTH_BACKENDS", value = "airflow.api.auth.backend.basic_auth,airflow.api.auth.backend.session" },
    # Run each task in a FRESH interpreter (spawn) instead of forking the scheduler.
    # The scheduler is multi-threaded (Azure SDK / gRPC bg threads); LocalExecutor's
    # fork() of it deadlocks the child → tasks stick in 'scheduled' and never run.
    { name = "AIRFLOW__CORE__EXECUTE_TASKS_NEW_PYTHON_INTERPRETER", value = "True" },

    # ADLS read (key-based connection string).
    { name = "AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING", secret_name = "adls-conn" },
    { name = "ADLS_FILESYSTEM", value = var.adls_filesystems[0] },

    # Snowflake load — write with DATAQ_LOADER (ETL), not the read-only DATAQ_READER.
    { name = "SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT", value = "${var.snowflake_organization_name}-${var.snowflake_account_name}" },
    { name = "SNOWFLAKE_USER", value = var.snowflake_reader_user },
    { name = "SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD", secret_name = "snowflake-password" },
    { name = "SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE", value = var.snowflake_warehouse },
    { name = "SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE", value = var.snowflake_database },
    { name = "SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA", value = var.snowflake_schemas[0] },
    { name = "SNOWFLAKE_ROLE", value = var.snowflake_loader_role },

    # Databricks — UC reference loads (flow_a_uc_reference) + Flow B notebook submit.
    { name = "DATABRICKS_HOST", value = var.databricks_host },
    { name = "DATABRICKS_TOKEN", secret_name = "databricks-token" },
    { name = "DATABRICKS_HTTP_PATH", value = var.databricks_http_path },
    { name = "UC_CATALOG", value = var.uc_catalog },
  ]
}

resource "azurerm_container_app" "airflow" {
  name                         = "dataq-harness-airflow"
  container_app_environment_id = azurerm_container_app_environment.harness.id
  resource_group_name          = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name
  revision_mode                = "Single"

  identity {
    type = "SystemAssigned"
  }

  registry {
    server               = azurerm_container_registry.harness.login_server
    username             = azurerm_container_registry.harness.admin_username
    password_secret_name = "acr-password"
  }

  secret {
    name  = "acr-password"
    value = azurerm_container_registry.harness.admin_password
  }
  secret {
    name  = "adls-conn"
    value = azurerm_storage_account.landing.primary_connection_string
  }
  secret {
    name  = "snowflake-password"
    value = var.snowflake_password
  }
  secret {
    name  = "databricks-token"
    value = var.databricks_token

> AGENT

The logs I got are from the **scheduler** container, and they reveal a real problem (separate from the webpage error): **every task is stuck in `queued`, never picked up by a worker, then fails** ("Task requeue attempts exceeded max; marking failed"). That's the Celery **worker** not consuming from the Redis broker. The webserver "Ooops!" is likely the same root cause surfacing in the UI. Let me get the webserver container's logs and the worker's status.

> AGENT

Root cause found. The webserver throws:

```
psycopg2.OperationalError) could not translate host name
"dataq-airflow-pg-wus3-3erlgd.postgres.database.azure.com" to address: Name or service not known
```

The Airflow app is still pointing at the **old Postgres hostname** `dataq-airflow-pg-wus3-3erlgd`. That server no longer exists under that name — during the DataQ deploy we **backed-up → deleted → recreated** the shared Postgres under the neutral name (`dataq-pg-wus3-*`, `purpose=dataq-shared`). DNS can't resolve the old name → webserver 500 ("Ooops!"), and the workers hit the same wall → tasks stay `queued` and fail. (The scheduler container is limping along on an established pooled connection, which is why it still logs DB writes.) Let me confirm the actual server name vs. what the app holds.
