Diagnosis confirmed — and it's a simple fix, not a config error:

- The **secret is already correct**: `pg-conn` points at the new `dataq-pg-wus3-3erlgd` (the only Postgres server that now exists).
- But the **running webserver/worker processes still hold the *old* hostname** in their injected env. Container Apps inject `secretRef` values at container start and don't refresh them when the secret changes. The scheduler container crash-restarted after the Postgres recreate (so it re-read the new host and works), but the webserver never crashed — it only 500s per request — so it's still serving the stale `dataq-airflow-pg-wus3-*` name.

**Fix = restart the active revisions** so every container re-reads the corrected secret. No terraform change needed (state already matches reality). Let me verify the worker's backend secret is also current, then restart both apps.

> AGENT

Fixed. The Airflow "Ooops!" is resolved.

## What was wrong
During the DataQ deploy, the **shared Postgres was deleted and recreated under a new name** (`dataq-airflow-pg-wus3-*` → neutral `dataq-pg-wus3-*`, `purpose=dataq-shared`). Terraform updated the `pg-conn` secret correctly, **but Container Apps inject `secretRef` values as env vars at container start and don't refresh them on secret change.** So the already-running webserver and worker processes kept resolving the *old, now-deleted* hostname → `could not translate host name ... Name or service not known` → webserver 500 + tasks stuck `queued` then failing. (The scheduler had crash-restarted on the DB drop and already picked up the new host, which is why it alone looked alive.)

## Fix
Restarted the active revisions of `dataq-harness-airflow` (scheduler+webserver) and `dataq-harness-airflow-worker` so every container re-read the corrected secret. No code/Terraform change — state already matched reality.

## Verified
- Webserver `/health` → **200**; `/` and `/home` → **302** (normal redirect-to-login). No more `OperationalError` / host-translation errors.
- Worker reconnected: `Connected to redis://dataq-harness-redis:6379/0` … `celery@… ready.` — tasks will be consumed again from the next scheduled cycle.

This was all in the **harness** (your out-of-repo demo env), so nothing in the DataQ repo changed.

One thing worth flagging for next time: **any delete-recreate of the shared Postgres needs a restart of every dependent Container App** (DataQ's `dataq-app-api`/`-worker` too, if their secrets are refreshed the same way) — the secret update alone isn't enough. Want me to save that as a harness operational note in memory?

So apps keep resolving the *old, deleted* hostname → `psycopg2.OperationalError: could not translate host name ... Name or service not known` → webserver 500s, Celery tasks stick in `queued` then fail. A container only picks up the new value if it happens to crash-restart (that's why the Airflow scheduler self-healed but the webserver/worker didn't).\n\n**Why:** secret env is a start-time snapshot, not live-bound.\n\n**How to apply:** after any delete-recreate of the shared Postgres, **restart the active revision of every dependent Container App** so each re-reads the corrected secret — `az containerapp revision restart -g dataq-rg -n <app> --revision <active-rev>`. In the harness that's `dataq-harness-airflow` (scheduler+webserver) + `dataq-harness-airflow-worker`; for the DataQ app it's `dataq-app-api` + `dataq-app-worker` (their `DATABASE_URL` is an inline secret too). 1	"""Flow A — event-driven load to Snowflake (payments). §3a.
2	
3	The *event* half of the Airflow trigger mix (the schedule half is
4	``flow_a_snowflake_load``). Payments land with every orders tick, so this DAG
5	watches the ``snowflake/payments/`` landing dir and loads on **arrival** rather
6	than on a daily clock.
7	
8	This uses the documented **file-sensor** pattern: a reschedule-mode
9	``PythonSensor`` pokes ADLS for a rising batch-file count (vs an Airflow Variable
10	watermark); when a new file lands it fires a whole-subdir overwrite load
11	(idempotent, like the schedule DAG). The poke interval bounds arrival latency.
12	
13	Required env (key-based): AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING,
14	SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT/USER/PASSWORD/WAREHOUSE/DATABASE[/SCHEMA/ROLE].
15	"""
16	
17	from __future__ import annotations
18	
19	import pendulum
20	from _harness import count_feed_files, load_to_snowflake, read_feed
21	from airflow import DAG
22	from airflow.models import Variable
23	from airflow.operators.python import PythonOperator
24	from airflow.sensors.python import PythonSensor
25	
26	PAYMENTS_SUBDIR = "snowflake/payments"
27	WATERMARK_KEY = "payments_event_filecount"
28	
29	
30	def _new_files_arrived(**_: object) -> bool:
31	    """True once payment batch files are present in the landing zone (the file-landing
32	    'event'). A whole-subdir overwrite load follows, so re-firing is idempotent — no
33	    fragile across-run watermark needed for a single-warehouse harness."""
34	    return count_feed_files(PAYMENTS_SUBDIR) > 0
35	
36	
37	def _load_payments(**_: object) -> None:
38	    df = read_feed(PAYMENTS_SUBDIR, "csv")
39	    if not df.empty:
40	        load_to_snowflake(df, "payments")  # overwrite — idempotent
41	    Variable.set(WATERMARK_KEY, count_feed_files(PAYMENTS_SUBDIR))
42	
43	
44	with DAG(
45	    default_args={
46	        # Retry transient failures (e.g. serverless SQL warehouse / job-cluster
47	        # cold starts) with exponential backoff so a starting warehouse recovers.
48	        "retries": 4,
49	        "retry_delay": pendulum.duration(seconds=30),
50	        "retry_exponential_backoff": True,
51	        "max_retry_delay": pendulum.duration(minutes=5),
52	    },
53	    dag_id="flow_a_payments_event",
54	    description="DataQ harness Flow A — event/arrival-driven payments load (file-sensor)",
55	    schedule="*/10 * * * *",  # poke cadence — bounds file-arrival latency
56	    start_date=pendulum.datetime(2026, 6, 1, tz="UTC"),
57	    catchup=False,
58	    max_active_runs=1,
59	    tags=["dataq-harness", "flow-a", "snowflake", "event"],
60	):
61	    wait = PythonSensor(
62	        task_id="wait_for_new_payments",
63	        python_callable=_new_files_arrived,
64	        mode="reschedule",  # free the worker slot between pokes
65	        poke_interval=120,
66	        timeout=540,  # give up within the 10-min window; next run re-pokes
67	        soft_fail=True,  # no new file in the window -> skip, not fail
68	    )
69	    load = PythonOperator(task_id="load_payments", python_callable=_load_payments)
70	    wait >> load
71

> AGENT

They're **not** all schedule-based — there's a deliberate 3-schedule + 1-event mix. The catch is that the event one *also* carries a cron, so in the UI it looks identical. Here's the actual split:

| DAG | `schedule=` | Real trigger modality |
|---|---|---|
| `flow_a_snowflake_load` | `30 1 * * *` | **Schedule** — daily clock load |
| `flow_a_uc_reference` | `45 1 * * *` | **Schedule** — daily |
| `flow_b_medallion` | `0 2 * * *` | **Schedule** — daily |
| `flow_a_payments_event` | `*/10 * * * *` | **Event / arrival-driven** (file sensor) |

## Why the event DAG still has a cron
`flow_a_payments_event` is the event half. Its `*/10` cron is **not a load cadence — it's the poke/wake cadence**. Each wake, a `PythonSensor` (reschedule mode, 120s pokes, 540s timeout) checks ADLS `snowflake/payments/` for newly-landed files:
- **file landed** → `load_payments` runs (the "event" fired);
- **nothing in the 10-min window** → `soft_fail=True` → the sensor **skips**, no load.

So the *trigger* is file arrival; the cron just bounds how often it looks. That's Airflow's documented **file-sensor** pattern — event semantics implemented on a polling wake-up. Airflow has no truly "scheduleless" entry point for a sensor DAG, which is exactly why it visually reads as schedule-based.

## Two honest caveats
1. **It's poll-based, not true push.** Genuinely event-based would be **Event-Grid (blob-created) → Airflow REST `POST /dagRuns`** (or a Dataset/Asset trigger). The harness `airflow.tf` even names "Event-Grid (file-landing push)" as the intended ingress, but the DAG as written uses a sensor poll, not a push trigger. The 10-min poll is the demo-grade stand-in.
2. **This is the harness, not DataQ.** These DAGs just generate pipeline runs for DataQ to *observe*. DataQ's own event path is genuinely event-driven — the Airflow `on_success/on_failure_callback → POST /orchestration/events/airflow` webhook (ADR 0007). So at the platform level the real event path exists; it's the callback, separate from these demo DAGs.

One note tied to the outage we just fixed: while Postgres was unreachable, that sensor task was stuck `queued` → requeued → "marking failed," so the event DAG looked like it was failing on a schedule. That was the DB, not the design — it should poke-or-skip cleanly now that the worker reconnected.

Want me to wire the **true push path** for `flow_a_payments_event` (Event-Grid blob-created subscription → Airflow REST `dagRuns`, drop the sensor)? That's the only way to make it genuinely event-based rather than a 10-min poll — but it's real added infra in the harness, so I'd scope it as its own task.

=== airflow/Dockerfile (custom image w/ DAGs) ===
# Harness Airflow image — apache/airflow + key-based client libs + the DAGs baked in.
# Once built+pushed to the registry, set Terraform's `airflow_image` to this
# (replacing the public apache/airflow default) so the Airflow Container App ships the DAGs.
#
# Build (from harness root, so the context can see airflow/):
#   docker build -f airflow/Dockerfile -t airflow-dataq:latest .

FROM apache/airflow:2.10.5

COPY airflow/requirements.txt /tmp/harness-requirements.txt
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r /tmp/harness-requirements.txt

COPY airflow/dags/ /opt/airflow/dags/

1	"""Shared load helpers for the DataQ-harness Airflow DAGs (§3).
2	
3	All auth is key-based (the disposable-harness decision): ADLS via the storage
4	**connection string**, Snowflake via user/password, Databricks via PAT. Heavy
5	client libs are imported lazily inside the functions so DAG *parsing* stays cheap
6	(the scheduler imports this module on every parse).
7	
8	Reads are "load the whole landing-zone subdir": each scheduled run concatenates all
9	batch files for a feed and overwrites the target table — idempotent and simple for a
10	demo. (Production would track a per-file watermark; noted as a follow-up.)
11	"""
12	
13	from __future__ import annotations
14	
15	import io
16	import os
17	
18	import pandas as pd
19	
20	ADLS_FILESYSTEM = os.environ.get("ADLS_FILESYSTEM", "landing")
21	
22	
23	def _adls_filesystem():
24	    from azure.storage.filedatalake import DataLakeServiceClient
25	
26	    conn = os.environ["AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING"]
27	    return DataLakeServiceClient.from_connection_string(conn).get_file_system_client(
28	        ADLS_FILESYSTEM
29	    )
30	
31	
32	def count_feed_files(subdir: str) -> int:
33	    """Number of batch files currently under <filesystem>/<subdir> — an arrival signal
34	    for the event (file-sensor) DAG: a rising count means a new batch landed."""
35	    fs = _adls_filesystem()
36	    return sum(1 for p in fs.get_paths(path=subdir) if not p.is_directory)
37	
38	
39	def _read_buf(buf: io.BytesIO, fmt: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
40	    if fmt == "csv":
41	        return pd.read_csv(buf)
42	    if fmt == "parquet":
43	        return pd.read_parquet(buf)
44	    if fmt == "json":  # NDJSON (bronze)
45	        return pd.read_json(buf, lines=True)
46	    raise ValueError(f"unknown format {fmt!r}")
47	
48	
49	def read_feed(subdir: str, fmt: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
50	    """Concatenate every batch file under <filesystem>/<subdir> into one DataFrame."""
51	    fs = _adls_filesystem()
52	    paths = sorted(p.name for p in fs.get_paths(path=subdir) if not p.is_directory)
53	    frames = []
54	    for path in paths:
55	        data = fs.get_file_client(path).download_file().readall()
56	        frames.append(_read_buf(io.BytesIO(data), fmt))
57	    return pd.concat(frames, ignore_index=True) if frames else pd.DataFrame()
58	
59	
60	def run_uc_sql(statements: list[str]) -> None:
61	    """Execute SQL statements on the Databricks SQL warehouse (silver/gold transforms)."""
62	    from databricks import sql
63	
64	    conn = sql.connect(
65	        server_hostname=os.environ["DATABRICKS_HOST"]
66	        .replace("https://", "")
67	        .rstrip("/"),
68	        http_path=os.environ["DATABRICKS_HTTP_PATH"],
69	        access_token=os.environ["DATABRICKS_TOKEN"],
70	    )
71	    try:
72	        cur = conn.cursor()
73	        for stmt in statements:
74	            cur.execute(stmt)
75	    finally:
76	        conn.close()
77	
78	
79	def load_to_snowflake(df: pd.DataFrame, table: str) -> int:
80	    """Overwrite a Snowflake table from a DataFrame (write_pandas, auto-create)."""
81	    import snowflake.connector
82	    from snowflake.connector.pandas_tools import write_pandas
83	
84	    conn = snowflake.connector.connect(
85	        account=os.environ["SNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT"],
86	        user=os.environ["SNOWFLAKE_USER"],
87	        password=os.environ["SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD"],
88	        warehouse=os.environ["SNOWFLAKE_WAREHOUSE"],
89	        database=os.environ["SNOWFLAKE_DATABASE"],
90	        schema=os.environ.get("SNOWFLAKE_SCHEMA", "RETAIL"),
91	        role=os.environ.get("SNOWFLAKE_ROLE") or None,
92	    )
93	    try:
94	        df.columns = [c.upper() for c in df.columns]
95	        _ok, _chunks, rows, _ = write_pandas(
96	            conn, df, table.upper(), auto_create_table=True, overwrite=True
97	        )
98	        return int(rows)
99	    finally:
100	        conn.close()
101	
102	
103	_PANDAS_TO_SQL = {
104	    "int64": "BIGINT",
105	    "float64": "DOUBLE",
106	    "bool": "BOOLEAN",
107	    "datetime64[ns]": "TIMESTAMP",
108	}
109	
110	
111	def load_to_uc(df: pd.DataFrame, catalog: str, schema: str, table: str) -> int:
112	    """Create-or-replace + insert a (small, reference-sized) DataFrame into a UC table."""
113	    from databricks import sql
114	
115	    full = f"`{catalog}`.`{schema}`.`{table}`"
116	    cols = ", ".join(
117	        f"`{c}` {_PANDAS_TO_SQL.get(str(t), 'STRING')}" for c, t in df.dtypes.items()
118	    )
119	    rows = [
120	        tuple(None if pd.isna(v) else v for v in record)
121	        for record in df.itertuples(index=False, name=None)
122	    ]
123	    conn = sql.connect(
124	        server_hostname=os.environ["DATABRICKS_HOST"]
125	        .replace("https://", "")
126	        .rstrip("/"),
127	        http_path=os.environ["DATABRICKS_HTTP_PATH"],  # SQL warehouse path
128	        access_token=os.environ["DATABRICKS_TOKEN"],
129	    )
130	    try:
131	        cur = conn.cursor()
132	        cur.execute(f"CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE {full} ({cols})")
133	        # Chunked multi-row INSERT: databricks-sql executemany is row-by-row (one
134	        # round-trip per row → minutes for 100s of rows). One execute per ~200-row
135	        # batch keeps even the 2.4k-row bronze loads to a handful of round-trips.
136	        if rows:
137	            one = "(" + ", ".join(["?"] * len(df.columns)) + ")"
138	            batch = 200
139	            for i in range(0, len(rows), batch):
140	                chunk = rows[i : i + batch]
141	                values = ", ".join([one] * len(chunk))
142	                flat = [v for row in chunk for v in row]
143	                cur.execute(f"INSERT INTO {full} VALUES {values}", flat)
144	        return len(rows)
145	    finally:
146	        conn.close()
147

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/airflow/dags/flow_a_payments_event.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Flow A — event-driven load to Snowflake (payments). §3a.\n\nThe *event* half of the Airflow trigger mix (the schedule half is\n``flow_a_snowflake_load``). Payments land with every orders tick, so this DAG\nloads on **arrival** rather than on a daily clock.\n\n**True push** (replaces the former file-sensor poll): a blob landing under\n``snowflake/payments/`` raises an Azure **Event Grid** ``BlobCreated`` event →\nthe harness Event-Grid receiver (``eventgrid_receiver/``, a Container App) →\nAirflow REST ``POST /api/v1/dags/flow_a_payments_event/dagRuns``. So this DAG is\n``schedule=None`` — it runs ONLY when externally triggered by an arrival event,\nnot on any cron. The triggering blob url arrives in ``dag_run.conf['blob_url']``\n(informational); the load itself is a whole-subdir overwrite (idempotent), so a\nduplicate trigger is harmless and no conf is required.\n\nRequired env (key-based): AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING,\nSNOWFLAKE_ACCOUNT/USER/PASSWORD/WAREHOUSE/DATABASE[/SCHEMA/ROLE].\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pendulum\nfrom _harness import count_feed_files, load_to_snowflake, read_feed\nfrom airflow import DAG\nfrom airflow.models import Variable\nfrom airflow.operators.python import PythonOperator\n\nPAYMENTS_SUBDIR = \"snowflake/payments\"\nWATERMARK_KEY = \"payments_event_filecount\"\n\n\ndef _load_payments(**context: object) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Whole-subdir overwrite load of the payments feed. Idempotent, so re-firing on a\n    duplicate arrival event is safe — no across-run watermark needed for a single-warehouse\n    harness. Logs the triggering blob (Event Grid passes it in dag_run.conf).\"\"\"\n    import logging\n\n    dag_run = context.get(\"dag_run\")\n    conf = getattr(dag_run, \"conf\", None) or {}\n    blob_url = conf.get(\"blob_url\", \"(none — manual/empty trigger)\")\n    logging.info(\"flow_a_payments_event triggered by arrival: %s\", blob_url)\n\n    df = read_feed(PAYMENTS_SUBDIR, \"csv\")\n    if not df.empty:\n        load_to_snowflake(df, \"payments\")  # overwrite — idempotent\n    Variable.set(WATERMARK_KEY, count_feed_files(PAYMENTS_SUBDIR))\n\n\nwith DAG(\n    default_args={\n        # Retry transient failures (e.g. serverless SQL warehouse / job-cluster\n        # cold starts) with exponential backoff so a starting warehouse recovers.\n        \"retries\": 4,\n        \"retry_delay\": pendulum.duration(seconds=30),\n        \"retry_exponential_backoff\": True,\n        \"max_retry_delay\": pendulum.duration(minutes=5),\n    },\n    dag_id=\"flow_a_payments_event\",\n    description=\"DataQ harness Flow A — event/arrival-driven payments load (Event Grid push)\",\n    schedule=None,  # externally triggered ONLY (Event Grid BlobCreated → REST dagRuns)\n    start_date=pendulum.datetime(2026, 6, 1, tz=\"UTC\"),\n    catchup=False,\n    max_active_runs=1,\n    tags=[\"dataq-harness\", \"flow-a\", \"snowflake\", \"event\"],\n):\n    PythonOperator(task_id=\"load_payments\", python_callable=_load_payments)\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/eventgrid_receiver/app.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Event Grid → Airflow REST trigger (the harness's true-push adapter).\n\nAzure Event Grid cannot call the Airflow REST API directly: it (1) requires a\nsubscription-validation handshake the Airflow API doesn't perform, (2) can't send\nthe ``Authorization: Basic`` header Airflow's basic_auth backend needs, and (3)\nposts its own event schema, not Airflow's ``dagRuns`` body. This tiny FastAPI app\nis the translator that sits between them.\n\nFlow:  ADLS BlobCreated → Event Grid system topic → (this receiver) → Airflow\n``POST /api/v1/dags/{dag}/dagRuns``.\n\nIncoming auth = a shared ``?token=`` query secret (mirrors the ADF webhook\nsecret-in-URL pattern, DataQ ADR 0006). Outgoing auth = Airflow admin basic-auth.\nEnv (all injected as Container App secrets/values):\n  EVENTGRID_TOKEN, AIRFLOW_BASE_URL, AIRFLOW_USER, AIRFLOW_PASSWORD,\n  TRIGGER_DAG_ID (default flow_a_payments_event),\n  PAYMENTS_PREFIX (default snowflake/payments/).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nimport os\nimport secrets\nfrom datetime import datetime, timezone\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport httpx\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Query, Request, Response, status\n\nlogging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)\nlog = logging.getLogger(\"eventgrid-receiver\")\n\nEVENTGRID_TOKEN = os.environ[\"EVENTGRID_TOKEN\"]\nAIRFLOW_BASE_URL = os.environ[\"AIRFLOW_BASE_URL\"].rstrip(\"/\")\nAIRFLOW_USER = os.environ[\"AIRFLOW_USER\"]\nAIRFLOW_PASSWORD = os.environ[\"AIRFLOW_PASSWORD\"]\nTRIGGER_DAG_ID = os.environ.get(\"TRIGGER_DAG_ID\", \"flow_a_payments_event\")\nPAYMENTS_PREFIX = os.environ.get(\"PAYMENTS_PREFIX\", \"snowflake/payments/\")\n\nVALIDATION_EVENT = \"Microsoft.EventGrid.SubscriptionValidationEvent\"\nBLOB_CREATED_EVENT = \"Microsoft.Storage.BlobCreated\"\n\napp = FastAPI(title=\"DataQ harness — Event Grid → Airflow trigger\")\n\n\n@app.get(\"/healthz\")\ndef healthz() -> dict[str, str]:\n    return {\"status\": \"ok\"}\n\n\ndef _authorized(token: str | None) -> bool:\n    return bool(token) and secrets.compare_digest(token, EVENTGRID_TOKEN)\n\n\ndef _trigger_dag(blob_url: str) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Fire one Airflow DAG run. Returns the Airflow HTTP status. A unique run_id avoids\n    409 collisions; max_active_runs=1 on the DAG means a burst of arrivals collapses to\n    one in-flight run (the load reads the whole subdir, so that's correct, not lossy).\"\"\"\n    run_id = f\"eventgrid__{datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%f')}\"\n    resp = httpx.post(\n        f\"{AIRFLOW_BASE_URL}/api/v1/dags/{TRIGGER_DAG_ID}/dagRuns\",\n        auth=(AIRFLOW_USER, AIRFLOW_PASSWORD),\n        json={\"dag_run_id\": run_id, \"conf\": {\"blob_url\": blob_url}},\n        timeout=30.0,\n    )\n    if resp.status_code not in (200, 409):\n        log.error(\"Airflow trigger failed %s: %s\", resp.status_code, resp.text[:500])\n    else:\n        log.info(\"Airflow trigger %s -> %s (run_id=%s)\", TRIGGER_DAG_ID, resp.status_code, run_id)\n    return resp.status_code\n\n\n@app.post(\"/events\")\nasync def events(request: Request, token: str | None = Query(default=None)) -> Response:\n    if not _authorized(token):\n        return Response(status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED)\n\n    payload: Any = await request.json()\n    eventslist = payload if isinstance(payload, list) else [payload]\n\n    # Subscription-validation handshake (sent once when the subscription is created).\n    for ev in eventslist:\n        if ev.get(\"eventType\") == VALIDATION_EVENT:\n            code = ev.get(\"data\", {}).get(\"validationCode\")\n            log.info(\"Event Grid subscription validation handshake\")\n            return Response(\n                content=f'{{\"validationResponse\": \"{code}\"}}',\n                media_type=\"application/json\",\n            )\n\n    # BlobCreated → trigger once per delivery if any payments blob is present (the load\n    # is a whole-subdir overwrite, so one trigger covers every file in the batch).\n    blob_urls = [\n        ev.get(\"data\", {}).get(\"url\", \"\")\n        for ev in eventslist\n        if ev.get(\"eventType\") == BLOB_CREATED_EVENT\n        and PAYMENTS_PREFIX in ev.get(\"data\", {}).get(\"url\", \"\")\n        and ev.get(\"data\", {}).get(\"url\", \"\").endswith(\".csv\")\n    ]\n    if blob_urls:\n        _trigger_dag(blob_urls[0])\n        return Response(status_code=status.HTTP_202_ACCEPTED)\n\n    # Nothing actionable (non-payments blob, or non-blob event) — ack so Event Grid\n    # doesn't retry.\n    return Response(status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT)\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/terraform/eventgrid.tf",
  "content": "# True-push path for Flow A payments (replaces the former file-sensor poll).\n#\n#   ADLS BlobCreated -> Event Grid system topic -> receiver Container App\n#   (eventgrid_receiver/) -> Airflow REST POST /api/v1/dags/flow_a_payments_event/dagRuns\n#\n# Event Grid can't call the Airflow REST API directly (validation handshake +\n# basic-auth header + payload shape all mismatch), so the small FastAPI receiver\n# is the translator. Incoming auth = a shared ?token= query secret (the ADF\n# webhook secret-in-URL pattern, DataQ ADR 0006); outgoing = Airflow admin basic-auth.\n\nlocals {\n  airflow_trigger_image = \"${azurerm_container_registry.harness.login_server}/airflow-trigger:${var.airflow_trigger_image_tag}\"\n}\n\n# Shared secret the receiver requires on the ?token= query param.\nresource \"random_password\" \"eventgrid_token\" {\n  length  = 40\n  special = false\n}\n\n# The receiver Container App. min_replicas = 1 so the Event Grid subscription's\n# create-time validation handshake hits a warm endpoint (a scale-from-zero cold\n# start can fail validation during apply). Tiny (0.25 vCPU / 0.5 GiB).\nresource \"azurerm_container_app\" \"airflow_trigger\" {\n  name                         = \"dataq-harness-airflow-trigger\"\n  container_app_environment_id = azurerm_container_app_environment.harness.id\n  resource_group_name          = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name\n  revision_mode                = \"Single\"\n\n  registry {\n    server               = azurerm_container_registry.harness.login_server\n    username             = azurerm_container_registry.harness.admin_username\n    password_secret_name = \"acr-password\"\n  }\n\n  secret {\n    name  = \"acr-password\"\n    value = azurerm_container_registry.harness.admin_password\n  }\n  secret {\n    name  = \"eventgrid-token\"\n    value = random_password.eventgrid_token.result\n  }\n  secret {\n    name  = \"airflow-password\"\n    value = random_password.airflow_admin.result\n  }\n\n  ingress {\n    external_enabled = true\n    target_port      = 8000\n    transport        = \"auto\"\n    traffic_weight {\n      latest_revision = true\n      percentage      = 100\n    }\n  }\n\n  template {\n    min_replicas = 1\n    max_replicas = 2\n\n    container {\n      name   = \"trigger\"\n      image  = local.airflow_trigger_image\n      cpu    = 0.25\n      memory = \"0.5Gi\"\n\n      env {\n        name        = \"EVENTGRID_TOKEN\"\n        secret_name = \"eventgrid-token\"\n      }\n      env {\n        name  = \"AIRFLOW_BASE_URL\"\n        value = \"https://${azurerm_container_app.airflow.ingress[0].fqdn}\"\n      }\n      env {\n        name  = \"AIRFLOW_USER\"\n        value = var.airflow_admin_user\n      }\n      env {\n        name        = \"AIRFLOW_PASSWORD\"\n        secret_name = \"airflow-password\"\n      }\n      env {\n        name  = \"TRIGGER_DAG_ID\"\n        value = \"flow_a_payments_event\"\n      }\n      env {\n        name  = \"PAYMENTS_PREFIX\"\n        value = \"snowflake/payments/\"\n      }\n\n      liveness_probe {\n        transport = \"HTTP\"\n        port      = 8000\n        path      = \"/healthz\"\n      }\n      readiness_probe {\n        transport = \"HTTP\"\n        port      = 8000\n        path      = \"/healthz\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  tags = local.common_tags\n}\n\n# Event Grid system topic on the landing storage account.\nresource \"azurerm_eventgrid_system_topic\" \"landing\" {\n  name                   = \"dataq-harness-landing-evt\"\n  resource_group_name    = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name\n  location               = azurerm_storage_account.landing.location\n  source_arm_resource_id = azurerm_storage_account.landing.id\n  topic_type             = \"Microsoft.Storage.StorageAccounts\"\n\n  tags = local.common_tags\n}\n\n# Subscription: payments .csv blobs under landing/snowflake/payments/ -> receiver webhook.\nresource \"azurerm_eventgrid_system_topic_event_subscription\" \"payments\" {\n  name                = \"payments-arrival\"\n  system_topic        = azurerm_eventgrid_system_topic.landing.name\n  resource_group_name = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name\n\n  included_event_types = [\"Microsoft.Storage.BlobCreated\"]\n  # Blob subject shape: /blobServices/default/containers/<filesystem>/blobs/<path>\n  subject_filter {\n    subject_begins_with = \"/blobServices/default/containers/${var.adls_filesystems[0]}/blobs/snowflake/payments/\"\n    subject_ends_with   = \".csv\"\n  }\n\n  webhook_endpoint {\n    url = \"https://${azurerm_container_app.airflow_trigger.ingress[0].fqdn}/events?token=${random_password.eventgrid_token.result}\"\n  }\n\n  retry_policy {\n    max_delivery_attempts = 10\n    event_time_to_live    = 60 # minutes\n  }\n\n  # The receiver must be live to answer the create-time validation handshake.\n  depends_on = [azurerm_container_app.airflow_trigger]\n}\n"
}

# Provider blocks. No credentials live in these files — every provider reads
# its secrets from the environment exported by `source ../secrets.sh`:
#   azurerm    -> ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID / ARM_TENANT_ID / ARM_CLIENT_ID / ARM_CLIENT_SECRET
#   snowflake  -> SNOWFLAKE_USER / SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD / SNOWFLAKE_ROLE
#   databricks -> DATABRICKS_HOST / DATABRICKS_TOKEN
# Only non-secret identifiers (org/account name) are passed as variables.

provider "azurerm" {
  features {}
  # subscription_id / tenant_id / client_id / client_secret come from ARM_* env vars.
  #
  # The Terraform SP is Contributor on dataq-rg ONLY — it has no rights at the
  # subscription scope, so it cannot auto-register resource providers. Skip that;

  resource_provider_registrations = "none"

provider "snowflake" {

  # picked up as a second, conflicting auth method (Azure SP).
  auth_type = "pat"
}

{

  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/terraform/eventgrid.tf",
  "old_string": "# Event Grid system topic on the landing storage account.\nresource \"azurerm_eventgrid_system_topic\" \"landing\" {\n  name                   = \"dataq-harness-landing-evt\"\n  resource_group_name    = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name\n  location               = azurerm_storage_account.landing.location\n  source_arm_resource_id = azurerm_storage_account.landing.id\n  topic_type             = \"Microsoft.Storage.StorageAccounts\"\n\n  tags = local.common_tags\n}\n\n# Subscription: payments .csv blobs under landing/snowflake/payments/ -> receiver webhook.\nresource \"azurerm_eventgrid_system_topic_event_subscription\" \"payments\" {\n  name                = \"payments-arrival\"\n  system_topic        = azurerm_eventgrid_system_topic.landing.name\n  resource_group_name = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name\n\n  included_event_types = [\"Microsoft.Storage.BlobCreated\"]\n  # Blob subject shape: /blobServices/default/containers/<filesystem>/blobs/<path>\n  subject_filter {\n    subject_begins_with = \"/blobServices/default/containers/${var.adls_filesystems[0]}/blobs/snowflake/payments/\"\n    subject_ends_with   = \".csv\"\n  }\n\n  webhook_endpoint {\n    url = \"https://${azurerm_container_app.airflow_trigger.ingress[0].fqdn}/events?token=${random_password.eventgrid_token.result}\"\n  }\n\n  retry_policy {\n    max_delivery_attempts = 10\n    event_time_to_live    = 60 # minutes\n  }\n\n  # The receiver must be live to answer the create-time validation handshake.\n  depends_on = [azurerm_container_app.airflow_trigger]\n}",
  "new_string": "# Subscription: payments .csv blobs under landing/snowflake/payments/ -> receiver webhook.\n# Scoped directly to the storage account (not a managed system topic): the account\n# already has an auto-created system topic from ADF's storage-event trigger, and Azure\n# allows only ONE system topic per source — a scope-based subscription reuses it.\nresource \"azurerm_eventgrid_event_subscription\" \"payments\" {\n  name  = \"dataq-harness-payments-arrival\"\n  scope = azurerm_storage_account.landing.id\n\n  included_event_types = [\"Microsoft.Storage.BlobCreated\"]\n  # Blob subject shape: /blobServices/default/containers/<filesystem>/blobs/<path>\n  subject_filter {\n    subject_begins_with = \"/blobServices/default/containers/${var.adls_filesystems[0]}/blobs/snowflake/payments/\"\n    subject_ends_with   = \".csv\"\n  }\n\n  webhook_endpoint {\n    url = \"https://${azurerm_container_app.airflow_trigger.ingress[0].fqdn}/events?token=${random_password.eventgrid_token.result}\"\n  }\n\n  retry_policy {\n    max_delivery_attempts = 10\n    event_time_to_live    = 60 # minutes\n  }\n\n  # The receiver must be live to answer the create-time validation handshake.\n  depends_on = [azurerm_container_app.airflow_trigger]\n}"

| **Airflow** | `flow_a_payments_event` (ADLS file-sensor) → Snowflake `PAYMENTS` | `flow_a_snowflake_load` (9 feeds) + `flow_a_uc_reference` (8 dims) + `flow_b_medallion` (bronze→silver→gold) |

**Decoupled from DataQ by design:** orchestrators run *pure ETL* — no push to DataQ.
DataQ (one of several possible monitors) discovers runs by **polling** the ADF/Airflow
REST APIs (ADR 0006/0007). No `NotifyDataQ` web activity; no Airflow callback.

## Data model — 24 datasets / route map

> AGENT

Done. The true push path for `flow_a_payments_event` is live and verified.

## What changed
**Before:** `schedule="*/10 * * * *"` + a `PythonSensor` polling ADLS every 10 min (event *semantics* on a poll).
**Now:** genuine push —

```
ADLS BlobCreated (snowflake/payments/*.csv)
  → Event Grid (scope-based subscription on the storage account)
  → dataq-harness-airflow-trigger  (FastAPI receiver Container App)
  → Airflow REST POST /api/v1/dags/flow_a_payments_event/dagRuns
  → DAG run (schedule=None, externally-triggered only)
```

## Pieces built (all in the out-of-repo harness)
- **DAG rewrite** — `airflow/dags/flow_a_payments_event.py`: sensor gone, `schedule=None`, idempotent whole-subdir load kept; logs the triggering blob from `dag_run.conf`.
- **Receiver** — `eventgrid_receiver/` (FastAPI + Dockerfile): Event Grid validation handshake, `?token=` shared-secret check (ADF secret-in-URL pattern, ADR 0006), payments-`.csv` filter, Airflow basic-auth trigger. Five behaviors smoke-tested locally before pushing (`test_local.py`).
- **Terraform** — `terraform/eventgrid.tf`: `random_password.eventgrid_token`, the receiver Container App (min_replicas=1 so validation hits a warm endpoint), and a **scope-based** `azurerm_eventgrid_event_subscription` (the storage account already has a system topic from ADF's trigger — one-per-source — so I attached to the scope instead). New `airflow_trigger_image_tag` var; `airflow_image_tag` bumped so app+worker carry the new DAG.

## Verified end-to-end
- Subscription **validated** at apply (32 s) — the receiver answered the handshake.
- Blob overwrite at `15:28:03Z` → receiver trigger at `15:28:05Z` (**~2 s**) → DAG run `eventgrid__…152804` → **`success`** (real Snowflake load).
- DAG confirmed `schedule: None`, unpaused — no new `scheduled__` runs.
- `terraform plan` → **No changes** (idempotent; pinned the batch defaults to kill the perpetual diff).

## Two notes
- I **targeted** my apply to avoid bundling one piece of unrelated pre-existing drift (`azurerm_data_factory_linked_custom_service.snowflake`) — left untouched.
- An HNS overwrite emits the create event twice, so you'll see two triggers per file; `max_active_runs=1` + the idempotent load makes that harmless.

Docs updated (harness README §3 + `HARNESS_TODO.md`), and I recorded the apply gotcha (the `TF_VAR_*` secret mapping) in memory. ADF's `pl_flow_a_orders` is still a poll-sensor-free native blob-event trigger; only Airflow's payments path needed this adapter.

> AGENT

Confirmed the full mechanism end-to-end. Short answer: **it's an artifact of the load path + a pandas dtype gotcha, not an intentional modeling choice.** Here's the precise chain.

## The generator types them fine — as Python objects
In [generate.py](../DataQ-harness/mockdata/generate.py), temporal fields are built as Python `datetime` objects, in two flavors:
- `*_ts` (e.g. `order_ts`, `paid_ts`, `load_ts`) → `datetime.datetime` → pandas infers **`datetime64[ns]`**.
- `*_date` (e.g. `signup_date`, `order_date`, `start_date`, `snapshot_date`) → built with `.date()` → `datetime.date` → pandas keeps these as **`object`** dtype. This is the classic pandas trap: a column of `datetime.date` is *not* promoted to `datetime64`, it stays object (= effectively string-like).

## Then the load path erases/loses the type

**Snowflake (all 12 feeds are CSV — [config.py:79-91](../DataQ-harness/mockdata/config.py#L79), [flow_a_snowflake_load.py:20](../DataQ-harness/airflow/dags/flow_a_snowflake_load.py#L20)):**
1. `read_feed(..., "csv")` does a plain `pd.read_csv(buf)` with **no `parse_dates`** ([_harness.py:49](../DataQ-harness/airflow/dags/_harness.py#L49)). CSV carries no types, and `read_csv` infers numbers but leaves *every* date/timestamp as `object`.
2. `load_to_snowflake` → `write_pandas(auto_create_table=True)` ([_harness.py:79](../DataQ-harness/airflow/dags/_harness.py#L79)) infers the DDL from those dtypes → `object` → **VARCHAR**.

→ In Snowflake, **every** temporal column (both `_ts` and `_date`) is VARCHAR, because CSV round-trips through text.

**Unity Catalog (reference dims are Parquet — [config.py:93-101](../DataQ-harness/mockdata/config.py#L93)):**
Parquet *preserves* dtypes, but `_PANDAS_TO_SQL` only promotes `datetime64[ns]`→TIMESTAMP; everything else falls through to the `STRING` default ([_harness.py:103-118](../DataQ-harness/airflow/dags/_harness.py#L103)).
- `_ts` columns (datetime64) → **TIMESTAMP** ✅
- `.date()` columns (object) → **STRING** ❌

→ So in UC it should be **only the DATE columns** (e.g. `date_dim.date`, `promotions.start_date/end_date`, `exchange_rates.rate_date`) that land as STRING — the `_ts` columns ought to be real TIMESTAMP. If you're seeing `_ts` columns as string in UC too, that's worth a closer look.

## Is it a bug?
For a **DQ demo harness, loosely-typed dates are arguably useful** — string dates are a real-world smell and give you something to write checks against (castability, format/regex validation, "freshness on a VARCHAR needs `TO_TIMESTAMP` first"). So it may be working as intended. But if you want them typed, three fixes by intent:

| Fix | Where | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `parse_dates=[...]` / post-read `pd.to_datetime` per feed | `read_feed` / the load DAGs | object→datetime64 → SF TIMESTAMP + UC TIMESTAMP |
| Promote `object`-of-`date` → `DATE` in the type map; emit `.date()` cols as datetime64 | `_PANDAS_TO_SQL` + `generate.py` | fixes the UC date columns |
| Explicit typed DDL + `COPY INTO`/`INSERT` instead of `auto_create_table` | both loaders | authoritative schema, no inference |

Two clarifying questions before I'd touch anything: (1) do you want the demo to **keep** string dates as a DQ test surface, or have them properly typed? And (2) want me to **query the live SF/UC `INFORMATION_SCHEMA`** to confirm exactly which columns are VARCHAR/STRING vs TIMESTAMP right now, so we're working from ground truth rather than the code?

```
dataq_retail.raw.feedback.created_ts     ->  string
dataq_retail.silver.feedback.created_ts  ->  string

So `created_ts` is **STRING** in both bronze (`raw`) and silver — even though it's a *timestamp* field (`_ts`), and even though the values are clean ISO-8601 (100% castable).

## Why this one is string — a *different* path than we discussed
`feedback` is the **Flow B medallion bronze (JSON)** feed, not the parquet reference path. The chain:

1. Generator emits `created_ts` as a real `datetime.datetime` ([generate.py:654](../DataQ-harness/mockdata/generate.py#L654)).
2. `emit.py` writes feedback as NDJSON with `df.to_json(..., date_format="iso")` ([emit.py:42](../DataQ-harness/mockdata/emit.py#L42)) → `created_ts` is serialized to an **ISO string** in the JSON.
3. The notebook does `spark.read.json(...).saveAsTable(raw.feedback)` — schema-on-read ([medallion_notebook.py:33](../DataQ-harness/databricks/medallion_notebook.py#L33)). **Spark's JSON reader does not infer timestamps by default** (`spark.sql.json.inferTimestamp=false` since Spark 3.0), so an ISO-looking string stays **STRING**.
4. Silver just dedups → type unchanged.

## This refines what I told you earlier
I'd said UC `_ts` columns "ought to be TIMESTAMP." That holds **only for the parquet reference path** (where datetime64 survives). You pointed at exactly the case that breaks it: the **JSON bronze path stringifies the timestamp** regardless. So there are really *three* roads to string-typed temporals here:

| Path | Feeds | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| CSV → Snowflake | 12 SF feeds | CSV erases all types → VARCHAR |
| Parquet → UC | reference dims | `datetime.date` → object → STRING (datetime64 `_ts` *do* get TIMESTAMP) |
| **JSON bronze → UC** | **feedback, sales_events** | ISO string in NDJSON + Spark `inferTimestamp` off → STRING |

## Fix for the JSON path, if you want it typed
- Quickest: `spark.read.option("inferTimestamp", "true").json(...)` (re-infers ISO → TIMESTAMP), or
- Explicit bronze schema (`StructType` with `TimestampType`) on `read.json` — authoritative, no inference cost, and the proper medallion practice, or
- Cast in the silver transform: `to_timestamp(created_ts)` — given it's 80/80 castable, this is clean.

Want me to apply one of these (and the same to `sales_events`), or leave it as-is — it's honestly a decent DQ test fixture (a "should-be-timestamp stored as string, fully castable" case)?

"""Azure AD bearer-token auth + user upsert.

Two operating modes — picked once at import time from settings:

- **Real mode** — `AZURE_TENANT_ID` + `AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID` are set.
  Tokens are validated by `fastapi-azure-auth`: issuer, audience, signature,
  expiry, and the configured scope. The OpenID config is loaded at app
  startup via `init_auth()` and refreshed automatically.

- **Dev bypass** — all three of:
  `ENVIRONMENT=dev`, `AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true`, Azure vars empty.
  No token required. Resolves every request to a fixed dev user upserted
  into the `users` table. Intended for local development against a
  Postgres in `docker-compose` without a real Azure tenant.

If neither mode is configured, `init_auth` raises at startup — fail-closed.
"""

from collections.abc import Callable
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from typing import Annotated, Any

from fastapi import Depends, Security
from fastapi_azure_auth import SingleTenantAzureAuthorizationCodeBearer
from fastapi_azure_auth.user import User as AzureUser
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import insert
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from backend.app.core.config import Settings, get_settings
from backend.app.core.errors import DataQError
from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
from backend.app.db.models import User
from backend.app.db.session import get_db

log = get_logger(__name__)

DEV_BYPASS_AAD_OID = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"
DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL = "dev-bypass@dataq.local"
DEV_BYPASS_DISPLAY_NAME = "Dev Bypass User"


def _dev_bypass_allowed(settings: Settings) -> bool:
    return (
        settings.environment == "dev"
        and settings.auth_dev_bypass
        and not settings.azure_auth_configured
    )


def _build_azure_scheme(
    settings: Settings,
) -> SingleTenantAzureAuthorizationCodeBearer | None:
    if not settings.azure_auth_configured:
        return None
    assert settings.azure_api_client_id is not None
    assert settings.azure_tenant_id is not None
    assert settings.azure_api_scope_uri is not None
    return SingleTenantAzureAuthorizationCodeBearer(
        app_client_id=settings.azure_api_client_id,
        tenant_id=settings.azure_tenant_id,
```

=== rest of auth.py (validator / claims) ===
        tenant_id=settings.azure_tenant_id,
        scopes={settings.azure_api_scope_uri: settings.azure_api_scope},
    )


_settings = get_settings()
azure_scheme: SingleTenantAzureAuthorizationCodeBearer | None = _build_azure_scheme(_settings)


def _upsert_user(
    db: Session,
    *,
    aad_object_id: str,
    email: str,
    display_name: str | None,
) -> User:
    now = datetime.now(UTC)
    stmt = (
        insert(User)
        .values(
            aad_object_id=aad_object_id,
            email=email,
            display_name=display_name,
            last_seen_at=now,
        )
        .on_conflict_do_update(
            index_elements=["aad_object_id"],
            set_={
                "email": email,
                "display_name": display_name,
                "last_seen_at": now,
                "updated_at": now,
            },
        )
        .returning(User)
    )
    user = db.execute(stmt).scalar_one()
    db.commit()
    return user


def _extract_claims(azure_user: AzureUser) -> tuple[str, str, str | None]:
    claims: dict[str, Any] = azure_user.claims
    aad_oid = str(claims["oid"])
    email = str(claims.get("preferred_username") or claims.get("email") or claims.get("upn") or "")
    display_name_raw = claims.get("name")
    display_name = str(display_name_raw) if display_name_raw is not None else None
    return aad_oid, email, display_name


async def init_auth() -> None:
    """Wire app startup: load OIDC config in real mode, or fail-closed.

    Called from the FastAPI lifespan.
    """
    if azure_scheme is not None:
        await azure_scheme.openid_config.load_config()
        log.info(
            "auth_real_mode_ready",
            tenant_id=_settings.azure_tenant_id,
            client_id=_settings.azure_api_client_id,
            scope=_settings.azure_api_scope_uri,
        )
        return
    if _dev_bypass_allowed(_settings):
        log.warning(
            "auth_dev_bypass_active",
            environment=_settings.environment,
            note=(
                "Every request resolves to a fixed dev user. "
                "Do NOT run with this configuration outside local dev."
            ),
        )
        return
    raise RuntimeError(
        "Auth not configured. Set AZURE_TENANT_ID + AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID, "
        "or set ENVIRONMENT=dev with AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=true for local dev."
    )


def _get_current_user_real(
    azure_user: Annotated[AzureUser, Security(azure_scheme)],
    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
) -> User:
    aad_oid, email, display_name = _extract_claims(azure_user)
    user = _upsert_user(db, aad_object_id=aad_oid, email=email, display_name=display_name)
    log.info("auth_user_resolved", mode="real", aad_oid=aad_oid, user_id=str(user.id))
    return user


def _get_current_user_dev_bypass(
    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
) -> User:
    user = _upsert_user(
        db,
        aad_object_id=DEV_BYPASS_AAD_OID,
        email=DEV_BYPASS_EMAIL,
        display_name=DEV_BYPASS_DISPLAY_NAME,
    )
    log.debug("auth_user_resolved", mode="dev_bypass", user_id=str(user.id))
    return user


def _get_current_user_unconfigured() -> User:
    # init_auth will have raised at startup; this is defence-in-depth.
    raise DataQError(
        code="auth_not_configured",
        message="Authentication is not configured for this environment.",
        status_code=503,
    )


get_current_user: Callable[..., User]
if azure_scheme is not None:
    get_current_user = _get_current_user_real
elif _dev_bypass_allowed(_settings):
    get_current_user = _get_current_user_dev_bypass
else:
    get_current_user = _get_current_user_unconfigured
```

196	function initialsOf(name: string): string {
197	  const parts = name.trim().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);

Three paths:\n * - dev_bypass: renders children directly.\n * - unconfigured: renders a setup-needed banner (no MSAL, no children).\n * - real: renders sign-in button when no account, children when authenticated.\n */\nexport function AuthGate({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {\n  if (authMode === 'dev_bypass') return <>{children}</>;\n  if (authMode === 'unconfigured') return <UnconfiguredBanner />;\n  return <RealAuthGate>{children}</RealAuthGate>;\n}\n\nfunction RealAuthGate({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {\n  const isAuthenticated = useIsAuthenticated();\n  const { instance } = useMsal();\n\n  if (isAuthenticated) return <>{children}</>;\n\n  const onLogin = () => {\n    void instance.loginRedirect({\n      scopes: authConfig.apiScopeUri ? [authConfig.apiScopeUri] : [],\n    });\n  };\n\n  return (\n    <Flex vertical align=\"center\" justify=\"center\" gap={16} style={{ paddingTop: 80 }}>\n      <Title level={3}>Sign in to DataQ</Title>\n      <Paragraph type=\"secondary\">Use your organisation Microsoft account.</Paragraph>\n      <Button type=\"primary\" size=\"large\" onClick={onLogin}>\n        Sign in with Microsoft\n      </Button>\n    </Flex>\n  );\n}",
  "new_string": "import { InteractionStatus } from '@azure/msal-browser';\nimport { useIsAuthenticated, useMsal } from '@azure/msal-react';\nimport { Alert } from 'antd';\nimport type { ReactNode } from 'react';\n\nimport { LoginPage } from './LoginPage';\nimport { authConfig, authMode } from './config';\n\n/**\n * Gates children behind auth. Three paths:\n * - dev_bypass: renders children directly.\n * - unconfigured: renders a setup-needed banner (no MSAL, no children).\n * - real: renders the sign-in page when no account, children when authenticated.\n */\nexport function AuthGate({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {\n  if (authMode === 'dev_bypass') return <>{children}</>;\n  if (authMode === 'unconfigured') return <UnconfiguredBanner />;\n  return <RealAuthGate>{children}</RealAuthGate>;\n}\n\nfunction RealAuthGate({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {\n  const isAuthenticated = useIsAuthenticated();\n  const { instance, inProgress } = useMsal();\n\n  if (isAuthenticated) return <>{children}</>;\n\n  const onSignIn = () => {\n    void instance.loginRedirect({\n      scopes: authConfig.apiScopeUri ? [authConfig.apiScopeUri] : [],\n    });\n  };\n\n  // A redirect is mid-flight (the click, or the post-redirect handshake) → keep\n  // the button busy so the page doesn't look idle while MSAL navigates.\n  const signingIn = inProgress !== InteractionStatus.None;\n\n  return <LoginPage onSignIn={onSignIn} signingIn={signingIn} />;\n}"
}

Now I can see it — and it surfaced **two real issues**:

1. **The login page renders *inside* the authenticated app shell** (sidebar nav + header are visible around it). A login page must take over the full viewport — the auth gate is currently nested inside the `Layout`/`Sider`.
2. **The ledger rows are invisible** — they're in the DOM but the reveal animation leaves them stuck at `opacity:0` (base state) when the animation is canceled/not-yet-run. Content should rest at `opacity:1` and only animate *from* 0.

Important — the review's suggested narrowing is wrong for this MSAL version: `InteractionStatus` here has **no `Login` member** (only Startup/Logout/AcquireToken/HandleRedirect/None). Pre-auth, the only states that occur are `Startup` (brief boot) and `HandleRedirect` (the login handshake) — both legitimately "auth in progress." So the original `!== None` is actually correct here; I'll revert it with a clearer comment, and fix the test to use a *real* status value instead of the bogus `'login'`:

> AGENT

That's the smoking gun: the API app registration's **`identifierUris` is empty** (`[]`). The scope `user_impersonation` and the service principal both exist, but with no `api://21491115-…` identifier URI, AAD can't resolve the resource the SPA asks for (`api://21491115-…/user_impersonation`) → AADSTS500011. The fix is to set the identifier URI (which AAD then propagates onto the service principal's names):

> TOOL

tool_use Bash
id: toolu_0139vRTsYn1AxWjGF4g86fUS
```json
{
  "command": "API_APP=REDACTED\necho \"=== set the api:// identifier URI on the API app registration ===\" \naz ad app update --id $API_APP --identifier-uris \"api://$API_APP\" 2>&1 | tail -3\necho \"=== verify on the app ===\" \naz ad app show --id $API_APP --query \"identifierUris\" -o json 2>&1\necho \"=== verify it propagated to the service principal's names ===\" \naz ad sp show --id $API_APP --query \"servicePrincipalNames\" -o json 2>&1",
  "description": "Set API identifier URI and verify propagation",
  "timeout": 90000
}
```

> AGENT

Root cause fully resolved. Here's what was wrong and what I fixed.

## The bug
The console error **AADSTS500011** wasn't from my build — my `VITE_*` values matched the canonical repo vars exactly. The real problem was in **Azure AD**: the API app registration (`21491115-…`) had an **empty `identifierUris`**. The SPA requests a token for `api://21491115-…/user_impersonation`, but with no `api://…` identifier URI on the app, AAD couldn't resolve that resource → "resource principal not found."

This was pre-existing drift (the empty URI also explains the *earlier* friction) — not caused by the redeploy.

## The fix (applied)
Set the identifier URI on the API app registration:
- API app `identifierUris` → `["api://21491115-…"]` ✓
- Service principal names now include `api://21491115-…` ✓ (so AAD resolves it)
- Confirmed the rest is already correct: the SPA holds the delegated permission **and** the API **pre-authorizes** the SPA for it → **no consent prompt** needed.

This matches what `deploy/terraform/sso.tf` already declares (`azuread_application_identifier_uri.api = "api://${client_id}"`), so my manual fix **reconciles the drift** — a future `terraform apply` will see it as already-correct, no conflict.

## Please retry
AAD changes propagate within seconds to a couple of minutes. **Reload https://black-meadow-034fc261e.7.azurestaticapps.net/ and click "Sign in with Microsoft" again.** If the old error sticks (a stale redirect state in the tab), open a fresh tab or clear the site's session storage — MSAL caches there.

You should now get all the way through to the dashboard (the guest gate is already open on the backend). If anything else surfaces in the console, paste it and I'll chase it down.

Two follow-ups I'd suggest once you confirm it works:
- **Why the URI was empty** despite being in Terraform — likely the `azuread_application_identifier_uri` resource didn't apply cleanly in the original bring-up. Worth a quick `terraform plan` on `deploy/terraform` to confirm state matches reality (I can run it).
- I can fold the live `AZURE_ALLOW_GUEST_USERS=true` into the Terraform too, so neither setting drifts on the next apply.

> AGENT

All fixes applied and merged to `main` (`184a66b`). Summary:

## What I did
**1. Live Azure fix (already working for you):** set the missing `api://21491115-…` identifier URI on the API app registration — that was the `AADSTS500011` cause.

**2. Codified into Terraform** (`deploy/terraform/`, PR [#399](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/399)) so the next `terraform apply` won't revert the live hotfix:
- `image_tag` default **`v3` → `v4`** (the login-page + guest-flag backend) — without this, an apply would roll the API back and re-break guest auth.
- New **`azure_allow_guest_users`** variable wired to `AZURE_ALLOW_GUEST_USERS` on the API.
- The `api://` identifier URI needed no Terraform change — it's declared (`azuread_application_identifier_uri.api`) and **already tracked in state**; only the live registration had drifted, which the manual `az` fix reconciled.

**3. Addressed a background security review:** it flagged defaulting guests *on* as an insecure IaC default (would leak into BYOL deployments, ADR 0013). Fixed → variable default is now **`false` (secure)**, with the `true` opt-in documented in `terraform.tfvars.example`. `terraform validate` passes; CI green; squash-merged.

## ⚠️ One operational caveat to remember
Because the secure default is now `false`, **the next `terraform apply` must pass `azure_allow_guest_users=true`** (via tfvars or `TF_VAR_azure_allow_guest_users=true`) or it will set the flag back to `false` and re-break guest sign-in. The live env is correct right now (`true`, set out-of-band); this only matters on the next apply. The `v4` image bump is unconditional, so the backend won't regress.

Live state and `main` are now consistent — login works, and the IaC reflects reality with a secure default.

> AGENT

Confirmed the cause: the outer `Layout` is `minHeight: 100vh` and grows with content, so the `Sider` grows as tall as a long page. The footer is flex-pinned to the bottom of that **full-height sider** — i.e., the bottom of the whole page — so it's below the fold until you scroll all the way down. 

Fix: pin the sider to the viewport (sticky, bounded to viewport height) so its footer stays visible, and let a long nav scroll *within* the sider instead of pushing the footer off:

> TOOL

> AGENT

Done — both layout issues fixed, merged, and live.

## What I fixed
1. **Sider footer hidden on scroll** → the sidebar (`Documentation`/`Admin`/`Settings`) was pinned to the bottom of a sider that grew with page height, so it fell below the fold.
2. **Header disappearing on scroll** (the regression from my first cut) → the page body was still scrolling and carried the header off.

**The real fix:** a proper **fixed app shell** — the `Layout` is exactly viewport height (`height:100vh; overflow:hidden`), so the **header and sider stay put** and only `<Content>` scrolls. Now both the DataQ logo/header *and* the Documentation footer remain visible no matter how long the page is.

## Verified + shipped
- `tsc` + ESLint clean, **277 tests** pass, `vite build` clean.
- Visually confirmed in-browser (tall scrolled content): header at top, footer at bottom, content scrolling between them.
- **PR [#400](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/400)** squash-merged to `main` (`5d1d36c`).
- **Redeployed to production** — new bundle live (`index-DPyDqpjI.js`, was `index-jlyRyz92.js`).

Reload the app (hard-refresh to dodge cache) and the header + sidebar footer should both stay fixed while page content scrolls. Let me know if anything else looks off.

1	"""Suite authorization — the single primitive every suite-scoped endpoint gates on.
2	
3	A user's effective permission on a suite is the highest of: **owner** (they are
4	`suite.created_by` — implicit, immutable, never a share row) or their `shares`
5	row (`view` < `edit` < `admin`). Capability ladder (decided for v1):
6	
7	    view   — read the suite, its checks, its results
8	    edit   — + create/update/delete checks, update the suite, trigger runs
9	    admin  — + manage shares (grant/revoke) AND delete the suite
10	    owner  — same capabilities as admin, but it is the creator: cannot be
11	             revoked or demoted, and granting a share to the owner is rejected.
12	
13	`require_permission` is the gate the API layer calls: it 404s a suite the user
14	can't see at all (existence is hidden), and 403s one they can see but lack the
15	level for. It returns the `Suite` so callers don't re-fetch.
16	
17	FastAPI-free (takes a `Session` + the user id); the API layer passes
18	`current_user.id`.
19	"""
20	
21	from __future__ import annotations
22	
23	import uuid
24	from collections.abc import Sequence
25	
26	from sqlalchemy import select
27	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
28	
29	from backend.app.core.errors import DataQError
30	from backend.app.db.models import Share, Suite
31	from backend.app.services.suite_service import SuiteNotFoundError
32	
33	OWNER = "owner"
34	
35	# Ordered capability ranks. `owner` ranks above `admin` so it always clears an
36	# admin gate, even though their capabilities are identical — the distinction is
37	# that owner is the immutable creator, not a grantable/revocable share.
38	_RANK = {"view": 1, "edit": 2, "admin": 3, OWNER: 4}
39	
40	
41	class SuiteForbiddenError(DataQError):
42	    status_code = 403
43	    code = "suite_forbidden"
44	
45	
46	def effective_permission(session: Session, suite: Suite, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> str | None:
47	    """The user's level on `suite` (`owner`/`admin`/`edit`/`view`), or None."""
48	    if suite.created_by == user_id:
49	        return OWNER
50	    share = session.scalars(
51	        select(Share).where(Share.suite_id == suite.id, Share.user_id == user_id)
52	    ).first()
53	    return share.permission if share is not None else None
54	
55	
56	def effective_permissions(
57	    session: Session, suites: Sequence[Suite], user_id: uuid.UUID
58	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, str | None]:
59	    """Batch `effective_permission` for many suites in one shares query (no N+1).
60	
61	    Owned suites resolve to `owner` without touching `shares`; the rest are
62	    looked up in a single `IN` query. Used to stamp each suite in a list with the
63	    caller's level so the UI can gate per-suite actions (manage shares, delete).
64	    """
65	    owned = {s.id for s in suites if s.created_by == user_id}
66	    shared_ids = [s.id for s in suites if s.id not in owned]
67	    levels: dict[uuid.UUID, str] = {}
68	    if shared_ids:
69	        rows = session.scalars(
70	            select(Share).where(Share.user_id == user_id, Share.suite_id.in_(shared_ids))
71	        )
72	        levels = {row.suite_id: row.permission for row in rows}
73	    return {s.id: (OWNER if s.id in owned else levels.get(s.id)) for s in suites}
74	
75	
76	def require_permission(
77	    session: Session,
78	    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
79	    user_id: uuid.UUID,
80	    *,
81	    minimum: str,
82	) -> Suite:
83	    """Return the suite iff the user has at least `minimum` permission on it.
84	
85	    Raises `SuiteNotFoundError` (404) if the suite doesn't exist **or** the user
86	    has no access at all (existence is hidden), and `SuiteForbiddenError` (403)
87	    if they have some access but below `minimum`.
88	    """
89	    suite = session.get(Suite, suite_id)
90	    if suite is None:
91	        raise SuiteNotFoundError("suite not found", detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id)})
92	    level = effective_permission(session, suite, user_id)
93	    if level is None:
94	        # No access → indistinguishable from "doesn't exist" (don't leak the id).
95	        raise SuiteNotFoundError("suite not found", detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id)})
96	    if _RANK[level] < _RANK[minimum]:
97	        raise SuiteForbiddenError(
98	            f"this action requires {minimum!r} permission on the suite",
99	            detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id), "have": level, "need": minimum},
100	        )
101	    return suite
102

> AGENT

DataQ has access on **two orthogonal axes**, which together give it **4 per-suite levels + 1 workspace-wide flag**.

## 1. Per-suite access — 4 levels (the main "access types")
Defined in [suite_authz.py](backend/app/services/suite_authz.py#L33-L38), gated by [models.py:41](backend/app/db/models.py#L41) `PERMISSIONS = ("view", "edit", "admin")`:

| Level | How it's held | Capabilities |
|---|---|---|
| **view** | `shares` row | read the suite, its checks, its results |
| **edit** | `shares` row | + create/update/delete checks, update suite, **trigger runs** |
| **admin** | `shares` row | + manage shares (grant/revoke) **and** delete the suite |
| **owner** | implicit (`suite.created_by`) | same as admin, but immutable — can't be revoked/demoted, and can't be granted a share |

Only **3 are grantable** (`view`/`edit`/`admin`, the `Share.permission` enum); **owner** is the 4th, implicit and non-grantable. Ranked `view(1) < edit(2) < admin(3) < owner(4)`.

## 2. Workspace-admin — 1 orthogonal flag
Separate from suite sharing: a config allowlist (`WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS`) surfaced as `is_workspace_admin` on `/me`. It bypasses owned-or-shared scoping for the `/admin/{suites,users,access}` endpoints (the Admin control centre, #289). It's **not** a per-suite level — it's a global capability axis with no Azure/Entra claim read.

---

So the precise answer depends on what you mean by "access type":
- **Grantable suite permissions:** 3 (`view`, `edit`, `admin`)
- **Effective suite levels:** 4 (the above + `owner`)
- **Plus** the orthogonal **workspace-admin** flag (global, not a suite level)

The Admin page's **"Access"** tab lists the actual `shares` grant rows across the workspace.

1	"""Suite sharing — grant / list / update / revoke per-user permissions.
2	
3	Managing shares requires `admin` on the suite (the owner always qualifies);
4	listing collaborators requires `view`. The target must be a real user and not
5	the suite's owner (the creator already has full, immutable access — a share row
6	for them would be meaningless). All authorization flows through
7	`suite_authz.require_permission`, so a caller without access gets a 404 (hidden)
8	and one with insufficient level gets a 403.
9	
10	FastAPI-free: takes a `Session` + ids; the API layer passes `current_user.id` as
11	the actor.
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import uuid
17	
18	from sqlalchemy import select
19	from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError
20	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session, selectinload
21	
22	from backend.app.core.errors import DataQError
23	from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
24	from backend.app.db.models import Share, User
25	from backend.app.services.suite_authz import require_permission

27	log = get_logger(__name__)

30	class ShareNotFoundError(DataQError):
31	    status_code = 404
32	    code = "share_not_found"
33	
34	
35	class ShareConflictError(DataQError):
36	    status_code = 409
37	    code = "share_conflict"
38	
39	
40	class ShareTargetInvalidError(DataQError):
41	    status_code = 422
42	    code = "share_target_invalid"
43	
44	
45	def _reject_self_target(
46	    suite_id: uuid.UUID, actor_id: uuid.UUID, target_user_id: uuid.UUID
47	) -> None:
48	    """Forbid an admin from changing/revoking their *own* share. A non-owner admin
49	    who self-downgrades or self-revokes loses access mid-session, and every later
50	    share mutation then 403s — bricking the share panel (#240). Self-management is
51	    never a legitimate need here (the owner has immutable full access; a non-owner
52	    leaving a suite is a separate flow we don't offer in v1)."""
53	    if target_user_id == actor_id:
54	        raise ShareTargetInvalidError(
55	            "cannot change or revoke your own share (would self-revoke your access)",
56	            detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id), "user_id": str(target_user_id)},
57	        )
58	
59	
60	def _get_share(session: Session, suite_id: uuid.UUID, user_id: uuid.UUID) -> Share:
61	    share = session.scalars(
62	        select(Share).where(Share.suite_id == suite_id, Share.user_id == user_id)
63	    ).first()
64	    if share is None:
65	        raise ShareNotFoundError(
66	            "no share for this user on this suite",
67	            detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id), "user_id": str(user_id)},
68	        )
69	    return share
70	
71	
72	def grant_share(
73	    session: Session,
74	    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
75	    *,
76	    actor_id: uuid.UUID,
77	    target_user_id: uuid.UUID,
78	    permission: str,
79	) -> Share:
80	    """Grant `target_user_id` a permission on the suite. Actor needs `admin`."""
81	    suite = require_permission(session, suite_id, actor_id, minimum="admin")
82	    if target_user_id == suite.created_by:
83	        raise ShareTargetInvalidError(
84	            "cannot share a suite with its owner (already has full access)",
85	            detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id), "user_id": str(target_user_id)},
86	        )
87	    if session.get(User, target_user_id) is None:
88	        raise ShareTargetInvalidError(
89	            "target user does not exist", detail={"user_id": str(target_user_id)}
90	        )
91	
92	    share = Share(suite_id=suite_id, user_id=target_user_id, permission=permission)
93	    session.add(share)
94	    try:
95	        session.commit()
96	    except IntegrityError as exc:
97	        session.rollback()
98	        raise ShareConflictError(
99	            "user already has a share on this suite; use PATCH to change it",
100	            detail={"suite_id": str(suite_id), "user_id": str(target_user_id)},
101	        ) from exc
102	    session.refresh(share)
103	    log.info(
104	        "share_granted", suite_id=str(suite_id), user_id=str(target_user_id), permission=permission
105	    )
106	    return share
107	
108	
109	def list_shares(session: Session, suite_id: uuid.UUID, *, actor_id: uuid.UUID) -> list[Share]:
110	    """List a suite's shares. Actor needs `view` (collaborators can see who else has access)."""
111	    require_permission(session, suite_id, actor_id, minimum="view")
112	    # Eager-load the grantee here (not model-wide) so the API can name each
113	    # collaborator without an N+1 — the only Share query that reads `.user`.
114	    return list(
115	        session.scalars(
116	            select(Share)
117	            .where(Share.suite_id == suite_id)
118	            .options(selectinload(Share.user))
119	            .order_by(Share.created_at)
120	        )
121	    )
122	
123	
124	def update_share(
125	    session: Session,
126	    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
127	    target_user_id: uuid.UUID,
128	    *,
129	    actor_id: uuid.UUID,
130	    permission: str,
131	) -> Share:
132	    """Change a user's permission. Actor needs `admin`."""
133	    require_permission(session, suite_id, actor_id, minimum="admin")
134	    _reject_self_target(suite_id, actor_id, target_user_id)
135	    share = _get_share(session, suite_id, target_user_id)
136	    share.permission = permission
137	    session.commit()
138	    session.refresh(share)
139	    log.info(
140	        "share_updated", suite_id=str(suite_id), user_id=str(target_user_id), permission=permission
141	    )
142	    return share
143	
144	
145	def revoke_share(
146	    session: Session,
147	    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
148	    target_user_id: uuid.UUID,
149	    *,
150	    actor_id: uuid.UUID,
151	) -> None:
152	    """Revoke a user's share. Actor needs `admin`."""
153	    require_permission(session, suite_id, actor_id, minimum="admin")
154	    _reject_self_target(suite_id, actor_id, target_user_id)
155	    share = _get_share(session, suite_id, target_user_id)
156	    session.delete(share)
157	    session.commit()
158	    log.info("share_revoked", suite_id=str(suite_id), user_id=str(target_user_id))
159

Confirmed feasibility. Here's the situation:

**Yes, it's possible.** I'm **Global Administrator** in your tenant (`07b592a3…`), and there's a verified domain (`royarijit04outlook.onmicrosoft.com`), so I can create directory users via `az ad user create`. Directory has 2 users today; adding ~6 is free (Entra free tier).

**But there's an important architectural split** — Entra and DataQ access are two different layers:

| Layer | What it controls | How it's set |
|---|---|---|
| **Entra ID** | *Authentication* — who can log in | `az ad user create` (I can do this) |

## Q1 — Can we bypass MFA?

**Partially, and only tenant-wide.** Two findings from your tenant:
- **No paid licenses** (`subscribedSkus` = `[]`) → no Entra ID **P1/P2** → **no Conditional Access**. CA is the only mechanism that can exempt *specific* users from MFA. So **per-user MFA bypass is not available** here.
- Your tenant almost certainly has **Security Defaults = ON** (the default for signup tenants; I couldn't read the exact flag because the az CLI token lacks the `Policy.Read` scope). With Security Defaults on, every user — including new ones — is **required to register MFA** on first sign-in.

So the only lever is the **tenant-wide toggle**: Entra admin center → **Overview → Properties → Manage security defaults → Disabled**. That removes the MFA prompt for *everyone* (including you, `royarijit04`). For a throwaway demo tenant that's a reasonable trade, but it's a genuine security downgrade and I **can't flip it from here** (the CLI token is missing `Policy.ReadWrite.SecurityDefaults`, and I wouldn't make a tenant-wide security change unilaterally anyway).

**Options:**
- **(a)** Leave Security Defaults on — each demo user does a one-time Authenticator/phone registration at first login. Simplest, no security change.
- **(b)** You disable Security Defaults in the portal (30 seconds), then these users sign in with just username + password, no MFA. Tell me once it's done and I'll proceed.

## Q2 — Will each user have owner access in their own login?

**Not on the shared demo suite — but yes on anything they create themselves.** This is the key DataQ semantic: **"owner" is per-suite = whoever created that suite**, not a global account role.

- On the **shared seeded suite** (owned by Olivia): the others get exactly their assigned level — Adam=admin, Ethan=edit, Vera=view, Nora=nothing (hidden), Wesley=workspace-admin. That's the whole point: different levels against the *same* resource.
- On **suites they create in their own login**: each is **automatically the owner** of their own creations. So Vera (view-only on the demo suite) can still log in, create her *own* suite, and be its owner.

So if your goal is "each login feels fully functional," that already happens for their own work. If instead you want me to **also seed one suite per user that they own** (so every demo account starts with an owned suite *plus* their shared-suite level), say the word and I'll add that — it just slightly muddies the "different levels on one shared suite" demo.

How does the the option B for MFA works? 
Also does MFA works only with secutity questions?

> AGENT

Good questions — let me clear up both, including a common misconception in the second one.

## How Option B (disabling Security Defaults) works

**Security Defaults** is a single tenant-wide on/off policy that Microsoft turns **on** for new tenants. While it's on, it forces three things:
1. **All users must register for MFA** (within 14 days of first sign-in) and get challenged when Microsoft deems the sign-in risky.
2. **Admins are always MFA-challenged** every sign-in.
3. **Legacy auth protocols are blocked.**

**Disabling it** is one toggle in the portal:

> **Entra admin center** (entra.microsoft.com) → **Identity → Overview → Properties** → bottom link **"Manage security defaults"** → set the dropdown to **Disabled** → pick a reason → **Save**.

Once it's off, and because your tenant has **no Entra ID P1** (so no Conditional Access policies can re-impose MFA), there is **nothing left enforcing a second factor**. New users then sign in with **just username + password** — the only first-login step is the **forced password change** (because I create them with `forceChangePasswordNextSignIn`). No Authenticator, no phone, no extra prompt.

Effects to be aware of:
- It's **tenant-wide** — it also drops MFA for **you** (`royarijit04`) and any future user. Fine for a throwaway demo tenant; a real security downgrade otherwise.
- **Reversible** anytime by flipping the same toggle back to Enabled.
- I **can't do it from the CLI** (token lacks `Policy.ReadWrite.SecurityDefaults`, and it's a tenant-wide security change I shouldn't make unilaterally) — it's a ~30-second portal action on your side.

## Does MFA work only with security questions?

**No — and importantly, security questions are *not* an MFA method at all.** That's a common mix-up:

- **Security questions** are only used for **SSPR** (Self-Service Password *Reset*) — recovering a forgotten password. They are **never** accepted as a second factor at sign-in.
- **MFA second factors** in Entra are things you *have* or *are*:
  - **Microsoft Authenticator app** — push approval or 6-digit TOTP code (the default/recommended)
  - **Phone** — SMS code or automated voice call
  - **OATH tokens** — software or hardware TOTP
  - **FIDO2 security keys**, **Windows Hello**, **certificate-based auth**

So if you keep Security Defaults **on** (Option A), each demo user's one-time setup is registering the **Microsoft Authenticator app** (or a phone number) — not security questions. If you turn Security Defaults **off** (Option B), there's **no second factor at all**, just password.

---

So your two real paths remain:
- **(a) MFA on** → each user does a one-time Authenticator/phone enrollment at first login.
- **(b) MFA off** → you flip the Security Defaults toggle once; users sign in with password only.

Tell me which, and whether you want the optional **one-owned-suite-per-user** seeding, and I'll create the 6 users + pre-seed the access rows.

> DEVELOPER

What will happen if I keep MFA off while creating the users and later toggel it on?

> AGENT

**Security Defaults is evaluated live at each sign-in — it's not stamped onto users at creation time.** So toggling it on later applies retroactively to everyone, including the users you made while it was off. Concretely:

**While it's off (create + use):**
- Users are created normally; no MFA registration is forced.
- They sign in with **password only** (plus the one-time forced password change on first login, which is independent of MFA).

**When you flip it back on later:**
- The policy immediately covers **all** users, including those 6 — they are **not grandfathered**.
- Each will be pushed into the **"More information required"** flow to register Microsoft Authenticator/phone, with the standard **14-day grace period** to do it.
- After the grace window (or immediately for any admin-role user, and on any sign-in Microsoft flags as risky), an un-enrolled user is **blocked until they enroll**.
- Anyone who *had* already registered an MFA method stays fine — no re-enrollment.

**Net:** turning it on later doesn't break the accounts, but it does mean each demo user will get nagged to set up Authenticator on subsequent logins (and can be hard-blocked once the 14 days lapse). Nothing you've seeded in DataQ is affected — Security Defaults only governs Entra *authentication*, never the DataQ `shares`/access rows.

**Practical takeaways for a demo:**
- **Most stable:** leave it **off** for the life of the demo → password-only the whole time.
- **If you must turn it back on:** do it knowing each user hits a one-time Authenticator enrollment within 14 days. Turning it back **off** again clears the enforcement.
- The forced **password change** on first login happens either way — if you'd rather skip even that, tell me and I'll create the users with `forceChangePasswordNextSignIn = false`.
