=== resolve_webhook impl ===
def resolve_webhook(
    config: SuiteNotification | None,
    *,
    secret_store: SecretStore,
    workspace_secret_name: str | None,
) -> str | None:
    """The webhook URL to deliver to: the per-suite one, else the workspace one.

    Returns ``None`` when neither resolves (delivery is then skipped). A missing
    secret is logged (by ref/name, never the value) and falls through.
    """
    ref = config.webhook_secret_ref if config is not None else None
    if ref:
        try:
            return secret_store.get(ref)
        except SecretNotFoundError:
            log.warning("suite_webhook_unresolved", secret_ref=ref)
    if workspace_secret_name:
        try:
            return secret_store.get(workspace_secret_name)
        except SecretNotFoundError:
            log.warning("teams_webhook_unresolved", secret_name=workspace_secret_name)
    return None

\":rotating_light:\", \"fail\": \":x:\", \"warn\": \":warning:\"}\n\n\ndef render_slack_message(report: RunReport, route: Route) -> dict[str, object]:\n    \"\"\"The Slack incoming-webhook payload (``text`` + Block Kit ``blocks``).\n\n    ``text`` is the notification fallback/summary; ``blocks`` render the card.\n    Pure — boundary DTO in, JSON body out — so it's unit-testable without a send.\n    \"\"\"\n    if report.success:\n        headline = f\":white_check_mark: DataQ — {report.suite_name}: all {report.total_checks} checks passed\"\n    else:\n        emoji = _SEVERITY_EMOJI.get(report.worst_severity or \"fail\", \":x:\")\n        headline = (\n            f\"{emoji} DataQ — {report.suite_name}: \"\n            f\"{report.failed_checks}/{report.total_checks} checks failed\"\n        )\n\n    blocks: list[dict[str, object]] = [\n        {\"type\": \"header\", \"text\": {\"type\": \"plain_text\", \"text\": headline[:150]}},\n        {\n            \"type\": \"section\",\n            \"fields\": [\n                {\"type\": \"mrkdwn\", \"text\": f\"*Datasource:*\\n{report.datasource_type}\"},\n                {\"type\": \"mrkdwn\", \"text\": f\"*Target:*\\n{report.target_label}\"},\n                {\"type\": \"mrkdwn\", \"text\": f\"*Severity:*\\n{report.worst_severity or '—'}\"},\n                {\"type\": \"mrkdwn\", \"text\": f\"*Run:*\\n{report.run_status}\"},\n            ],\n        },\n    ]\n\n    failing = [c for c in report.checks if c.status != \"pass\"]\n    if failing:\n        lines = \"\\n\".join(_check_line(c) for c in failing[:_MAX_CHECK_LINES])\n        if len(failing) > _MAX_CHECK_LINES:\n            lines += f\"\\n…and {len(failing) - _MAX_CHECK_LINES} more\"\n        blocks.append({\"type\": \"section\", \"text\": {\"type\": \"mrkdwn\", \"text\": lines}})\n\n    # `<!channel>` escalates a critical breach to everyone in the channel.\n    if route.mention_channel:\n        blocks.insert(0, {\"type\": \"section\", \"text\": {\"type\": \"mrkdwn\", \"text\": \"<!channel> *CRITICAL*\"}})\n\n    return {\"text\": headline, \"blocks\": blocks}\n\n\ndef _check_line(check: CheckReport) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One failing check as a Slack mrkdwn bullet (name · status · redacted sample).\"\"\"\n    line = f\"• *{check.check_name}* — `{check.status}`\"\n    sample = check.sample_summary or {}\n    pct = sample.get(\"unexpected_percent\")\n    count = sample.get(\"unexpected_count\")\n    if pct is not None:\n        line += f\" ({pct}% unexpected)\"\n    elif count is not None:\n        line += f\" ({count} unexpected)\"\n    return line\n\n\nclass SlackPublisher:\n    \"\"\"Posts a run's report to a workspace Slack incoming webhook.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        *,\n        secret_store: SecretStore,\n        webhook_secret_name: str | None,\n        allowed_hosts: tuple[str, ...],\n        timeout: float = _POST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,\n    ) -> None:\n        self._secret_store = secret_store\n        self._webhook_secret_name = webhook_secret_name\n        self._allowed_hosts = allowed_hosts\n        self._timeout = timeout\n\n    def publish(self, session: Session, report: RunReport) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Deliver to Slack per the run's suite notification policy.\n\n        Quiet no-op when Slack is unconfigured, the suite disabled alerting, or\n        the run is below the suite's threshold. Raises on an HTTP error — the\n        dispatch/composite layer isolates that so a flaky webhook can't fail the\n        run or block the other channels.\n        \"\"\"\n        if not self._webhook_secret_name:\n            return\n        config = notification_service.get_config(session, report.suite_id)\n        if config is not None and not config.enabled:\n            return\n        policy = config.alert_on if config is not None else notification_service.DEFAULT_ALERT_ON\n        route = route_for(report, policy)\n        if not route.should_send:\n            return\n        try:\n            webhook = self._secret_store.get(self._webhook_secret_name)\n        except SecretNotFoundError:\n            log.warning(\"slack_webhook_unresolved\", secret_name=self._webhook_secret_name)\n            return\n        # SSRF guard at the request sink: only POST to an allowlisted Slack host.\n        host = (urlparse(webhook).hostname or \"\").lower()\n        if not any(host == a or host.endswith(f\".{a}\") for a in self._allowed_hosts):\n            log.warning(\"slack_webhook_host_not_allowed\", run_id=str(report.run_id))\n            return\n        response = httpx.post(\n            webhook, json=render_slack_message(report, route), timeout=self._timeout\n        )\n        response.raise_for_status()\n        log.info(\n            \"slack_alert_sent\",\n            run_id=str(report.run_id),\n            suite=report.suite_name,\n            worst_severity=report.worst_severity,\n            urgency=route.urgency,\n            failed_checks=report.failed_checks,\n        )\n"
}

  "content": "\"\"\"Email (SMTP) ``ResultPublisher`` — sends a run's report as an email.\n\nWorkspace-level: one sender (SMTP submission with STARTTLS) and a fixed\nrecipient list. The password (e.g. a Gmail app-password) is resolved from the\nSecretStore by name; the rest of the SMTP coordinates are non-secret config.\nDelivery follows the **same** per-suite policy as the other publishers (the\nsuite's `enabled` flag + `alert_on` threshold via :func:`routing.route_for`);\nonly the rendering + transport differ. Unconfigured (no recipients / username /\npassword secret) is a quiet no-op.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport smtplib\nimport ssl\nfrom email.message import EmailMessage\n\nfrom sqlalchemy.orm import Session\n\nfrom backend.app.alerting.base import CheckReport, RunReport\nfrom backend.app.alerting.routing import Route, route_for\nfrom backend.app.core.logging import get_logger\nfrom backend.app.core.secrets import SecretNotFoundError, SecretStore\nfrom backend.app.services import notification_service\n\nlog = get_logger(__name__)\n\n_SMTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 15.0\n_MAX_CHECK_LINES = 20\n\n\ndef render_subject(report: RunReport) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The email subject line — verdict + suite + counts at a glance.\"\"\"\n    if report.success:\n        return f\"[DataQ] {report.suite_name}: all {report.total_checks} checks passed\"\n    sev = (report.worst_severity or \"fail\").upper()\n    return (\n        f\"[DataQ] {sev} — {report.suite_name}: \"\n        f\"{report.failed_checks}/{report.total_checks} checks failed\"\n    )\n\n\ndef render_text_body(report: RunReport) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Plain-text body (the alternative for non-HTML clients).\"\"\"\n    lines = [\n        render_subject(report),\n        \"\",\n        f\"Suite:       {report.suite_name}\",\n        f\"Datasource:  {report.datasource_type}\",\n        f\"Target:      {report.target_label}\",\n        f\"Run status:  {report.run_status}\",\n        f\"Worst severity: {report.worst_severity or '—'}\",\n        \"\",\n    ]\n    failing = [c for c in report.checks if c.status != \"pass\"]\n    if failing:\n        lines.append(\"Failing checks:\")\n        lines.extend(_check_line(c) for c in failing[:_MAX_CHECK_LINES])\n        if len(failing) > _MAX_CHECK_LINES:\n            lines.append(f\"  …and {len(failing) - _MAX_CHECK_LINES} more\")\n    return \"\\n\".join(lines)\n\n\ndef render_html_body(report: RunReport) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Minimal HTML body (inline-styled, email-client safe).\"\"\"\n    colour = \"#16a34a\" if report.success else \"#dc2626\"\n    rows = \"\".join(\n        f\"<tr><td style='padding:2px 8px;'><code>{_esc(c.status)}</code></td>\"\n        f\"<td style='padding:2px 8px;'>{_esc(c.check_name)}</td>\"\n        f\"<td style='padding:2px 8px;color:#6b7280;'>{_esc(_sample_note(c))}</td></tr>\"\n        for c in report.checks\n        if c.status != \"pass\"\n    )\n    table = (\n        f\"<table style='border-collapse:collapse;margin-top:8px;'>{rows}</table>\"\n        if rows\n        else \"\"\n    )\n    return (\n        f\"<div style='font-family:system-ui,Arial,sans-serif;'>\"\n        f\"<h2 style='color:{colour};margin:0 0 8px;'>{_esc(render_subject(report))}</h2>\"\n        f\"<p style='margin:0;color:#374151;'>\"\n        f\"<b>Datasource:</b> {_esc(report.datasource_type)} &nbsp;·&nbsp; \"\n        f\"<b>Target:</b> {_esc(report.target_label)} &nbsp;·&nbsp; \"\n        f\"<b>Severity:</b> {_esc(report.worst_severity or '—')}</p>\"\n        f\"{table}</div>\"\n    )\n\n\ndef _check_line(check: CheckReport) -> str:\n    note = _sample_note(check)\n    return f\"  - [{check.status}] {check.check_name}\" + (f\" — {note}\" if note else \"\")\n\n\ndef _sample_note(check: CheckReport) -> str:\n    sample = check.sample_summary or {}\n    pct = sample.get(\"unexpected_percent\")\n    count = sample.get(\"unexpected_count\")\n    if pct is not None:\n        return f\"{pct}% unexpected\"\n    if count is not None:\n        return f\"{count} unexpected\"\n    return \"\"\n\n\ndef _esc(value: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Minimal HTML escaping for interpolated text.\"\"\"\n    return (\n        value.replace(\"&\", \"&amp;\").replace(\"<\", \"&lt;\").replace(\">\", \"&gt;\").replace('\"', \"&quot;\")\n    )\n\n\nclass EmailPublisher:\n    \"\"\"Sends a run's report over SMTP (STARTTLS) to a fixed recipient list.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        *,\n        secret_store: SecretStore,\n        smtp_host: str,\n        smtp_port: int,\n        username: str | None,\n        password_secret_name: str | None,\n        sender: str | None,\n        recipients: tuple[str, ...],\n        timeout: float = _SMTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,\n    ) -> None:\n        self._secret_store = secret_store\n        self._smtp_host = smtp_host\n        self._smtp_port = smtp_port\n        self._username = username\n        self._password_secret_name = password_secret_name\n        self._sender = sender or username\n        self._recipients = recipients\n        self._timeout = timeout\n\n    def publish(self, session: Session, report: RunReport) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Send the email per the run's suite notification policy.\n\n        Quiet no-op when email is unconfigured, the suite disabled alerting, or\n        the run is below the suite's threshold. Raises on an SMTP error — the\n        composite layer isolates it so a flaky mailer can't fail the run or block\n        the other channels.\n        \"\"\"\n        if not (self._recipients and self._username and self._password_secret_name and self._sender):\n            return\n        config = notification_service.get_config(session, report.suite_id)\n        if config is not None and not config.enabled:\n            return\n        policy = config.alert_on if config is not None else notification_service.DEFAULT_ALERT_ON\n        route = route_for(report, policy)\n        if not route.should_send:\n            return\n        try:\n            password = self._secret_store.get(self._password_secret_name)\n        except SecretNotFoundError:\n            log.warning(\"email_password_unresolved\", secret_name=self._password_secret_name)\n            return\n\n        message = EmailMessage()\n        message[\"Subject\"] = render_subject(report)\n        message[\"From\"] = self._sender\n        message[\"To\"] = \", \".join(self._recipients)\n        message.set_content(render_text_body(report))\n        message.add_alternative(render_html_body(report), subtype=\"html\")\n\n        context = ssl.create_default_context()\n        with smtplib.SMTP(self._smtp_host, self._smtp_port, timeout=self._timeout) as server:\n            server.starttls(context=context)\n            server.login(self._username, password)\n            server.send_message(message)\n        log.info(\n            \"email_alert_sent\",\n            run_id=str(report.run_id),\n            suite=report.suite_name,\n            recipients=len(self._recipients),\n            worst_severity=report.worst_severity,\n        )\n"

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/alerting/composite.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"A ``ResultPublisher`` that fans a report out to several channels.\n\nEach child publisher is best-effort and isolated: a raising / slow channel is\nlogged and the rest still run, so a broken Slack webhook can't suppress the\nemail (and vice versa). Children self-no-op when their channel is unconfigured,\nso the composite can always hold all of them.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Sequence\n\nfrom sqlalchemy.orm import Session\n\nfrom backend.app.alerting.base import ResultPublisher, RunReport\nfrom backend.app.core.logging import get_logger\n\nlog = get_logger(__name__)\n\n\nclass CompositePublisher:\n    \"\"\"Delivers a report through every child publisher, isolating failures.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, publishers: Sequence[ResultPublisher]) -> None:\n        self._publishers = tuple(publishers)\n\n    def publish(self, session: Session, report: RunReport) -> None:\n        for publisher in self._publishers:\n            try:\n                publisher.publish(session, report)\n            except Exception:\n                # One channel failing must not stop the others or fail the run.\n                log.exception(\n                    \"channel_publish_failed\",\n                    channel=type(publisher).__name__,\n                    run_id=str(report.run_id),\n                )\n"
}

=== CheckReport + RunReport fields ===

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CheckReport:
    """One check's outcome, shaped for an outbound notification.

    ``observed_value`` / ``expected_value`` are GX aggregates as stored (already
    JSON-sanitized at write time). ``sample_summary`` is the **redacted** form of
    the result's ``sample_failures`` — counts/percentages only, raw cell values
    masked — so a card can say "12 rows failed" without leaking which.
    """

    check_name: str
    expectation_type: str
    status: str
    metric_value: float | None
    observed_value: dict[str, Any] | None
    expected_value: dict[str, Any] | None
    sample_summary: dict[str, Any] | None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunReport:
    """A completed run's redacted outcome — the unit a ``ResultPublisher`` sends.

    ``run_status`` is the run *lifecycle* (``succeeded``/``failed``); ``success``
    is the derived data-quality verdict (every check passed). ``counts`` is the
    per-status histogram the derived count properties read, and ``worst_severity``
    is the highest failing tier present (``None`` when nothing breached).
    """

    run_id: uuid.UUID
    suite_id: uuid.UUID
    suite_name: str
    run_status: str
    datasource_type: str
    target_label: str
    worst_severity: str | None
    counts: dict[str, int]
    checks: list[CheckReport]
    finished_at: datetime | None

    @property
    def success(self) -> bool:
        """Data-quality verdict: the run executed cleanly *and* nothing breached.
        Derived (not stored) so it can never drift from ``worst_severity`` — the
        same drift-free pattern as the count properties below."""
        return self.run_status == "succeeded" and self.worst_severity is None

    @property
    def total_checks(self) -> int:
        return sum(self.counts.values())

    @property
    def failed_checks(self) -> int:
        """Checks that genuinely breached (``fail`` + ``critical``) — ``warn`` is
        surfaced via ``worst_severity``, not counted as a failure here."""
        return self.counts.get("fail", 0) + self.counts.get("critical", 0)

    @property
    def has_failures(self) -> bool:
        """Alert-worthy: the run couldn't execute, or any check breached a tier
        (incl. ``warn``). Publishers/routing refine *whether* to send on top of
        this (severity-aware routing + the per-suite on-fail/warn/always policy)."""
        return self.run_status == "failed" or any(
            self.counts.get(tier, 0) for tier in FAILING_TIERS
        )

> AGENT

You're exactly right, and you've found a genuine product gap. Here's what's happening and why:

## What the redactor does today
`redact_sample_failures` ([run_service.py:373](backend/app/services/run_service.py#L373)) is **value-based blanket masking**: it keeps only two summary keys — `unexpected_count` and `unexpected_percent` — and `<redacted>`s **every other value** in the failing rows. It preserves the *shape* (row count + column names) but masks all cell values — so **LINE_TOTAL (the offending value) and ORDER_NUMBER (the identifier) are both masked**, even though neither is PII.

## Why it was built blunt (the real rationale)
From the code's own docstring: it can't know *which* columns are PII ahead of time — a `name`/`email`/`ssn` could be any column in any table — so it masks everything as the safe default, deliberately *not* key-based ("masking only known-PII keys would leak any un-enumerated column"). It's **secure but blunt.**

## Why your critique is correct
A failing-row sample where **both the bad value and the identifier are redacted is not actionable** — you can't see *what* was wrong or *which* row. That defeats the entire purpose of a sample. For a data-quality tool, "here are the rows that failed" *is* the value, and right now it delivers "some rows failed, can't tell you anything about them."

So: **only PII should be redacted, and a real identifier must survive** — exactly your point. The blunt default traded away the feature's usefulness to be safe.

## The right fix — surgical, column-aware redaction
The blanket approach is wrong; the fix is **column classification** (and there's already a documented seam for it at that call site — "a future opt-in could surface raw rows"):

1. **Classify columns** as *PII* (redact) vs *safe* (show) — per connection/suite, with a sensible auto-guess (column-name heuristics like the log redactor's `email/ssn/phone/name`) that you can override.
2. **Designate an identifier/key column** (e.g. `ORDER_NUMBER`) that's always shown, so the row is locatable. (Must itself be non-PII — the classification guarantees that.)
3. **Show the check's tested column** (here `LINE_TOTAL`) by default — it's the metric the check is *about*, the whole reason the row failed.
4. Result: `email` stays `<redacted>`; `ORDER_NUMBER` + `LINE_TOTAL` show → **the sample is finally actionable** ("order ORD-1041 had line_total = −12.50").

This is a far higher-value DQ feature than anything in the admin pile — it's the difference between "alert me something's wrong" and "show me exactly what to fix."

Want me to **file this as an enhancement and build it**? I'd start minimal: a per-suite **identifier column** + a **PII-column list** (default-redact-all stays the fallback for unclassified columns, so security doesn't regress), then surface the safe columns in run-detail + the Slack/email sample.

> AGENT

That GHCR screenshot is the package→repo connect (already done — CI can push). Now to your questions — all three are good calls, and the first two have a payoff you might not expect.

## Detection: metadata/tags first, then column name — yes, and it's *better* than you think
Snowflake and Databricks both ship **native data classification** that maps almost perfectly onto what we need:
- **Snowflake** `SYSTEM$CLASSIFY` / classification returns a **`privacy_category`** per column ∈ `{IDENTIFIER, QUASI_IDENTIFIER, SENSITIVE}` — that's *literally* "identifier column" vs "PII column", authoritative from the warehouse. Plus object **tags**.
- **Unity Catalog** has **column tags** + `system.information_schema.column_tags` and classification.

So the layering you described is exactly right, and there's a clean precedence:
1. **Datasource tags/classification** (authoritative — Snowflake `privacy_category`, UC tags)
2. **Column-name heuristics** (fallback — reuse the log redactor's `email/ssn/phone/name/...`)
3. **Manual override** (what the user sets)
4. **Default-redact** anything still unclassified (so security never regresses)

## Suite-level metadata — agree, with one nuance
Storing **identifier column + PII columns** at the suite level is the right pragmatic v1 (a suite targets one table, so it's natural config). The only nuance: PII-ness is really a property of the *table/column*, not the suite — so two suites on the same table would re-declare it. I'd build it suite-level now, but shape the field so it can **promote to a connection/column catalog later** without a rewrite. Net: **suite-level, yes.**

## Notifications — yes, they're skeletal; enrich them
Today's alert has suite/datasource/target/severity/failing-check-names. I'd add: a **deep link to the run** (click straight to run-detail), **per-check expected-vs-observed + metric value**, the **actionable sample row** (once redaction is fixed — `ORDER-1041: line_total = −12.50`), **env / duration / triggered-by**, and tighter severity styling. The redaction fix and the enrichment are the same story: *make the alert tell you what to fix.*

Let me file both and start building:

def build_run_report(session: Session, run: Run) -> RunReport:
    """Build the redacted, GX-agnostic report for a terminal ``run``.

    Joins each ``Result`` back to its ``Check`` (by id) for the check name +
    expectation; a result whose check was since deleted degrades to a placeholder
    name rather than failing the build. ``metric_value`` is widened ``Decimal`` →
    ``float`` for JSON-friendly transport.
    """
    suite = session.get(Suite, run.suite_id)
    connection = session.get(Connection, suite.connection_id) if suite is not None else None
    checks = {c.id: c for c in session.scalars(select(Check).where(Check.suite_id == run.suite_id))}
    results: list[Result] = run_service.list_results(session, run.id)

    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    check_reports: list[CheckReport] = []
    for result in results:
        counts[result.status] = counts.get(result.status, 0) + 1
        check = checks.get(result.check_id)
        check_reports.append(
            CheckReport(
                check_name=check.name if check is not None else "(deleted check)",
                expectation_type=check.expectation_type if check is not None else "",
                status=result.status,
                metric_value=(
                    float(result.metric_value) if result.metric_value is not None else None
                ),
                observed_value=result.observed_value,
                expected_value=result.expected_value,
                # Redaction policy at the seam: counts only, never raw rows.
                sample_summary=run_service.redact_sample_failures(result.sample_failures),
            )
        )

    worst = _worst_severity([r.status for r in results])
    return RunReport(
        run_id=run.id,
        suite_id=run.suite_id,
        suite_name=suite.name if suite is not None else "(deleted suite)",
        run_status=run.status,
        datasource_type=connection.type if connection is not None else "",
        target_label=_target_label(suite),

def _result_read(result: Any) -> ResultRead:
    """Map a `Result` ORM row to `ResultRead`, redacting `sample_failures`.

    Built field-by-field rather than via `model_validate(from_attributes)` so the
    raw, PII-bearing `sample_failures` can never be auto-copied onto the wire —
    redaction is the only path it can take out of here (#226)."""
    return ResultRead(
        id=result.id,
        check_id=result.check_id,
        status=result.status,
        metric_value=result.metric_value,
        duration_ms=result.duration_ms,
        observed_value=result.observed_value,
        expected_value=result.expected_value,
        sample_failures=svc.redact_sample_failures(result.sample_failures),

349	# they are safe to surface. Everything else — notably `partial_unexpected_list`,
350	# the raw offending cell values — is treated as potential PII and masked. These
351	# mirror the producer's `gx_runner._SAMPLE_KEYS`; keep the two in sync when the
352	# sample shape grows (a new safe aggregate must be added here or it gets masked).
353	_SAMPLE_SAFE_KEYS = frozenset({"unexpected_count", "unexpected_percent"})
354	# Same sentinel string as the structlog redactor (core.logging._REDACTED); the
355	# two redactors stay deliberately separate (key-based for logs, value-based here).
356	_REDACTED_VALUE = "<redacted>"
357	
358	
359	def _redact_sample_value(value: Any) -> Any:
360	    """Mask data values while preserving container shape and dict keys.
361	
362	    List length and row-dict column names are *schema*, not row data, so they
363	    stay (they tell the viewer how many rows / which columns failed); every leaf
364	    value is replaced with ``"<redacted>"``.
365	    """
366	    if isinstance(value, dict):
367	        return {key: _redact_sample_value(val) for key, val in value.items()}
368	    if isinstance(value, list):
369	        return [_redact_sample_value(item) for item in value]
370	    return _REDACTED_VALUE
371	
372	
373	def redact_sample_failures(sample: dict[str, Any] | None) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
374	    """Redact a result's `sample_failures` for safe surfacing on the read API.
375	
376	    `sample_failures` carries aggregate counts plus `partial_unexpected_list` —
377	    the actual failing cell values, which can be PII. Suite-level ``view`` authz
378	    lets share-recipients read a suite's results, so the raw rows must not cross
379	    that boundary unredacted (CLAUDE.md PII rule; the column is redactor-only
380	    everywhere else and is purged on the retention sweep below).
381	
382	    Policy: keep the numeric summary keys; mask every value in the rest,
383	    preserving shape (list length, row-dict column names) so the drill-down shows
384	    *how much* failed without leaking *what*. ``None`` (passing / errored /
385	    purged results) passes through unchanged. A future opt-in could surface raw
386	    rows to privileged viewers — that policy seam lives at this one call site.
387	
388	    This redacts by *value* (mask everything except an allowlist), not by *key*
389	    like the structlog redactor (``core.logging._PII_KEYS``): a failing sample is
390	    arbitrary table columns whose PII-ness can't be enumerated as key names ahead
391	    of time, so masking only known-PII keys would leak any un-enumerated column.
392	    Do not "harmonise" this toward the key-based approach.
393	
394	    A safe key is passed through only when its value is actually a scalar number —
395	    the boundary trusts value *shape*, not just the key name — so a future runner
396	    that ever stowed row data under one of those keys can't bypass redaction.
397	    """
398	    if not sample:
399	        return None
400	    return {
401	        key: (value if _is_safe_summary(key, value) else _redact_sample_value(value))
402	        for key, value in sample.items()

The authoritative layers (warehouse classification, the suite policy's\n# explicit `pii_columns`) sit above this; unclassified columns still default-mask.\n_PII_COLUMN_TOKENS = frozenset(\n    {\n        \"email\", \"phone\", \"mobile\", \"ssn\", \"passport\", \"name\", \"address\",\n        \"street\", \"city\", \"zip\", \"postal\", \"dob\", \"birth\", \"credit\", \"card\",\n        \"iban\", \"account_number\",\n    }\n)\n\n\ndef _is_pii_column(column: str, policy: dict[str, Any] | None) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Whether a column must be masked in a sample: explicitly in the suite\n    policy's ``pii_columns``, or matched by the column-name heuristic.\"\"\"\n    name = column.strip().lower()\n    if policy:\n        listed = {str(c).strip().lower() for c in (policy.get(\"pii_columns\") or [])}\n        if name in listed:\n            return True\n    return any(token in name for token in _PII_COLUMN_TOKENS)\n\n\ndef _redact_row(row: Any, policy: dict[str, Any] | None) -> Any:\n    \"\"\"Mask a failing-row dict per-column: show non-PII columns (the identifier +\n    the tested column a future runner records under ``unexpected_index_list``),\n    mask PII (policy / heuristic).     run_id: uuid.UUID,
    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],

) -> RunDetailRead:
    run = svc.get_run(db, run_id)
    if run is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND, detail="run not found")
    # Gate on the run's suite: a caller who can't see the suite can't see its
    # runs (404 hides the run id too, matching the suite existence-hiding rule).
    require_permission(db, run.suite_id, current_user.id, minimum="view")
    results = svc.list_results(db, run_id)
    # `Run` has no `results` relationship to validate a RunDetailRead from
    # directly, so validate the run fields (as RunRead) and graft the
    # separately-fetched, redaction-gated results on.
    return RunDetailRead(
        **RunRead.model_validate(run).model_dump(),
        results=[_result_read(r) for r in results],
    )


@router.get(

)
def get_run_progress(
    run_id: uuid.UUID,
    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
) -> RunProgressRead:
    run = svc.get_run(db, run_id)
    if run is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND, detail="run not found")
    # Same suite-scoped gate as the run detail: can't see the suite → 404 the run.
    require_permission(db, run.suite_id, current_user.id, minimum="view")
    progress = svc.get_run_progress(db, run)

412	def _redact_row(row: Any, policy: dict[str, Any] | None) -> Any:
413	    """Mask a failing-row dict per-column: show non-PII columns (the identifier +
414	    the tested column a future runner records under ``unexpected_index_list``),
415	    mask PII (policy / heuristic). Non-dict rows fall back to full masking."""
416	    if not isinstance(row, dict):

424	def redact_sample_failures(
425	    sample: dict[str, Any] | None,
426	    *,
427	    tested_column: str | None = None,
428	    policy: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
429	) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
430	    """Redact a result's `sample_failures` for safe surfacing on the read API.
431	
432	    `sample_failures` carries aggregate counts plus `partial_unexpected_list` —
433	    the failing values of the **tested column** — and (when a future runner records
434	    it) an `unexpected_index_list` of failing rows. Suite-level ``view`` authz lets
435	    share-recipients read a suite's results, so PII must not cross that boundary
436	    unredacted (CLAUDE.md PII rule; purged on the retention sweep below).
437	
438	    Column-aware policy (#415) — surgical, not blanket:
439	    * numeric summary keys (`unexpected_count` / `unexpected_percent`) always pass;
440	    * `partial_unexpected_list` (the tested column's failing values) passes when
441	      ``tested_column`` is **not** PII — per the suite ``policy.pii_columns`` or the
442	      name heuristic — so a non-PII breach (e.g. a bad ``LINE_TOTAL``) is finally
443	      *visible*, while a PII tested column (``email``) stays masked;
444	    * `unexpected_index_list` row-dicts are masked **per column** (identifier +
445	      non-PII shown, PII masked);
446	    * everything else default-masks (unclassified → redacted, so security can't
447	      regress).
448	
449	    With neither ``tested_column`` nor ``policy`` the legacy **blanket mask** is
450	    kept (the safe default for callers that don't know the column) — only the
451	    summary keys survive. ``None`` sample passes through unchanged.
452	    """
453	    if not sample:
454	        return None
455	    show_tested = tested_column is not None and not _is_pii_column(tested_column, policy)
456	    out: dict[str, Any] = {}
457	    for key, value in sample.items():
458	        if _is_safe_summary(key, value):
459	            out[key] = value
460	        elif key == "partial_unexpected_list" and show_tested:
461	            out[key] = value  # the tested column's failing values — non-PII, surfaced
462	        elif key == "unexpected_index_list" and isinstance(value, list):
463	            out[key] = [_redact_row(row, policy) for row in value]
464	        else:
465	            out[key] = _redact_sample_value(value)
466	    return out

Non-dict rows fall back to full masking.\"\"\"\n    if not isinstance(row, dict):\n        return _redact_sample_value(row)\n    return {\n        col: (_REDACTED_VALUE if _is_pii_column(str(col), policy) else val)\n        for col, val in row.items()\n    }\n\n\ndef redact_sample_failures(",
  "new_string": "def _safe_sample_columns(tested_column: str | None, policy: dict[str, Any] | None) -> set[str]:\n    \"\"\"Columns whose raw values may be surfaced in a sample: the tested column +\n    the suite policy's identifier column, each only if **not** PII (policy\n    ``pii_columns`` / name heuristic). Empty when nothing is classified → the\n    blanket mask (default-redact, so security never regresses).\"\"\"\n    safe: set[str] = set()\n    if tested_column and not _is_pii_column(tested_column, policy):\n        safe.add(tested_column)\n    identifier = (policy or {}).get(\"identifier_column\")\n    if identifier and not _is_pii_column(str(identifier), policy):\n        safe.add(str(identifier))\n    return safe\n\n\ndef _redact_row(row: Any, safe_columns: set[str]) -> Any:\n    \"\"\"Mask a failing-row dict per-column: **default-redact** — a column's value\n    is kept only when it's in ``safe_columns`` (the identifier + tested column),\n    every other column (PII or unclassified) is masked. }

=== list_pipeline_runs service (any user filter?) ===
def list_pipeline_runs(
    session: Session,
    *,
    provider: str | None = None,
    status: str | None = None,
    limit: int = 50,
) -> list[PipelineRun]:
    """Monitored orchestrator pipeline/DAG runs, newest first (`created_at` desc).

    Optionally filtered by ``provider`` (adf / airflow) and/or ``status``.
    """
    stmt = select(PipelineRun).order_by(PipelineRun.created_at.desc()).limit(limit)
    if provider is not None:
        stmt = stmt.where(PipelineRun.provider == provider)
    if status is not None:
        stmt = stmt.where(PipelineRun.status == status)
    return list(session.scalars(stmt))

## On Airflow (you mentioned ADF *&* Airflow)
Airflow monitoring is **not** Azure RBAC — the Airflow webserver has its own auth. To let the 6 users monitor DAG runs in the Airflow UI, they'd each need an **Airflow account (Viewer role)** created in the harness Airflow (via `airflow users create`). > DEVELOPER

Is Airflow also RBAC?

> AGENT

Yes — but it's **Airflow's *own* RBAC, not Azure RBAC.** Important distinction:

## Airflow has RBAC, but it's application-level
Airflow (2.x) ships RBAC via **Flask App Builder** — users + roles live in Airflow's **own metadata database**, completely separate from Azure AD / Entra. So **Azure role assignments don't touch the Airflow UI** — granting someone "Reader" on an Azure resource does nothing for Airflow.

**Built-in Airflow roles:**
| Role | Access |
|---|---|
| **Viewer** | read-only — view DAGs, runs, logs (what you'd give for *monitoring*) |
| **User** | Viewer + trigger/clear DAG runs |
| **Op** | + connections/variables/pools |
| **Admin** | full (the harness's `admin` account I'm using) |

## So the contrast with ADF
- **ADF** → Entra users get access via **Azure RBAC** (what I just did — Reader on the factory). Their Entra login works directly.
- **Airflow** → there is **no Azure-RBAC path**. The harness Airflow currently authenticates with a **local admin username/password** (the creds I pulled for the connection), not SSO.

## Two ways to give the 6 users Airflow monitoring
- **(a) Local Airflow Viewer accounts** — quick. `airflow users create … --role Viewer` (one per user) in the harness Airflow. Downside: separate Airflow-only passwords, *not* their Entra login.
- **(b) Azure AD OAuth SSO** — proper. Reconfigure the harness Airflow's `webserver_config.py` with Azure AD as an OAuth provider + role mapping (and an app registration), so they log in with their **Entra** account and auto-map to Viewer. More setup, but one identity.

For a demo, **(a)** is the pragmatic choice (5 min, six `Viewer` users). **(b)** is the "do it right" path if you want single-sign-on parity with ADF/DataQ.

Want me to set up the **6 Viewer accounts** in the harness Airflow now (a), or wire **Entra SSO** (b)? (And separately — say the word on broadening the ADF grant to **RG-level Reader** so the factory is browsable, vs the direct link.)

# Harness Airflow image — apache/airflow + key-based client libs + the DAGs baked in.
# Once built+pushed to the registry, set Terraform's `airflow_image` to this
# (replacing the public apache/airflow default) so the Airflow Container App ships the DAGs.
#
# Build (from harness root, so the context can see airflow/):
#   docker build -f airflow/Dockerfile -t airflow-dataq:latest .

FROM apache/airflow:2.10.5

COPY airflow/requirements.txt /tmp/harness-requirements.txt
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r /tmp/harness-requirements.txt

COPY airflow/dags/ /opt/airflow/dags/

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ-harness/airflow/webserver_config.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Airflow webserver auth — Azure AD (Entra) OAuth SSO with app-role mapping.\n\nHumans sign in with their Entra account; the Azure **app role** assigned on the\n\"DataQ Harness Airflow\" app registration (\"Admin\" / \"Viewer\") maps to the Airflow\nrole of the same name (synced every login). New users self-register as Viewer.\n\nThis governs the **UI** only. The REST API keeps its basic-auth backend\n(`REDACTED,session`) against the local admin user\n(still created at init) so DataQ's orchestration poller keeps working unchanged —\nUI=OAuth and API=basic_auth coexist.\n\nOAuth client id / secret / tenant come from the container env (the secret is a\nContainer App secret, never baked into the image).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\n\nfrom flask_appbuilder.security.manager import AUTH_OAUTH\n\nAUTH_TYPE = AUTH_OAUTH\n\n# Self-register first-time SSO users; default role is Viewer, then the app-role\n# claim (below) is applied and re-synced on every login.\nAUTH_USER_REGISTRATION = True\nAUTH_USER_REGISTRATION_ROLE = \"Viewer\"\nAUTH_ROLES_SYNC_AT_LOGIN = True\n\n# Map the Azure app-role values (in the token's `roles` claim) → Airflow roles.\nAUTH_ROLES_MAPPING = {\n    \"Admin\": [\"Admin\"],\n    \"Viewer\": [\"Viewer\"],\n}\n\n_TENANT = os.environ[\"AZURE_OAUTH_TENANT_ID\"]\n\nOAUTH_PROVIDERS = [\n    {\n        \"name\": \"azure\",\n        \"icon\": \"fa-windows\",\n        \"token_key\": \"access_token\",\n        \"remote_app\": {\n            \"client_id\": os.environ[\"AZURE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID\"],\n            \"client_secret\": os.environ[\"AZURE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET\"],\n            \"api_base_url\": f\"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{_TENANT}/oauth2\",\n            \"server_metadata_url\": (\n                f\"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{_TENANT}/v2.0/.well-known/openid-configuration\"\n            ),\n            \"request_token_url\": None,\n            \"client_kwargs\": {\"scope\": \"openid email profile\"},\n        },\n    }\n]\n"
}

## Fix — clear the stale session
1. **Sign out completely**, or just open a **fresh incognito/private window** (clears the cached token/cookies that triggered the GET-vs-POST error).
2. Go to **`https://adf.azure.com`** fresh and sign in as the user — **don't reuse a bookmarked deep-link** (a stale link to a mid-OAuth URL is the classic AADSTS900561 trigger).
3. **Check the directory switcher** (top-right) is on **`royarijit04outlook.onmicrosoft.com`**. If ADF Studio opened under a different/Default directory, switch to that tenant — otherwise the factory genuinely won't be visible (wrong tenant context, not a role problem).
4. Alternative path that's less flaky: **portal.azure.com → search `dataq-harness-adf` → Monitor**.

That re-login almost always clears AADSTS900561.

1	# Airflow on Container Apps — scheduler + webserver (LocalExecutor), backed by the
2	# Postgres metadata DB. min_replicas = 1 (the scheduler can't scale to zero); HTTPS
3	# ingress so Event-Grid (file-landing push) and DataQ can reach it. ~$25-75/mo always-on.
4	#
5	# Starts on the public airflow image (no DAGs). §3 swaps `airflow_image` for a custom
6	# registry image (FROM apache/airflow + COPY dags/) that calls the mockdata tick CLI / loads.
7	
8	resource "random_id" "fernet" {
9	  byte_length = 32
10	}

13	  length  = 32

15	}

18	  length  = 20
19	  special = false

23	  # Valid Fernet key = url-safe base64 of 32 bytes (swap +/ for -_, keep padding).
24	  airflow_fernet_key = replace(replace(random_id.fernet.b64_std, "+", "-"), "/", "_")
25	
26	  airflow_pg_conn = join("", [
27	    "postgresql+psycopg2://",
28	    var.postgres_admin_login, ":", random_password.pg.result,
29	    "@", azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.airflow.fqdn, ":5432/",
30	    azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_database.airflow.name, "?sslmode=require",
31	  ])

33	  # Custom registry image (apache/airflow + the harness DAGs + client libs).
34	  airflow_image = "${azurerm_container_registry.harness.login_server}/airflow-dataq:${var.airflow_image_tag}"
35	
36	  # CeleryExecutor: Redis broker (internal) + Postgres result backend. Workers run in a
37	  # SEPARATE, horizontally scalable container app (airflow_worker.tf) — that's what lifts
38	  # the single-executor / 2-vCPU-per-replica ceiling that throttled LocalExecutor.
39	  # Container Apps internal service-to-service: the short app name resolves over the
40	  # environment's internal DNS (the full .internal. FQDN did not connect for TCP).
41	  celery_broker_url = "redis://${azurerm_container_app.redis.name}:6379/0"
42	  celery_result_backend = join("", [
43	    "db+postgresql://",
44	    var.postgres_admin_login, ":", random_password.pg.result,
45	    "@", azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.airflow.fqdn, ":5432/",
46	    azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server_database.airflow.name, "?sslmode=require",
47	  ])
48	
49	  # Shared scheduler + webserver env (DRYed into both containers via dynamic blocks).
50	  # LocalExecutor runs tasks in the scheduler, so the connection env must live here.
51	  airflow_env = [
52	    { name = "AIRFLOW__DATABASE__SQL_ALCHEMY_CONN", secret_name = "pg-conn" },
53	    { name = "AIRFLOW__CORE__EXECUTOR", value = "CeleryExecutor" },
54	    { name = "AIRFLOW__CELERY__BROKER_URL", value = local.celery_broker_url },
55	    { name = "AIRFLOW__CELERY__RESULT_BACKEND", secret_name = "celery-result-backend" },
56	    # Tasks per worker replica — each cold-starts a fresh interpreter, so keep it modest
57	    # vs the worker's 2 vCPU / 4 GiB; horizontal scaling (more replicas) is the lever.
58	    { name = "AIRFLOW__CELERY__WORKER_CONCURRENCY", value = "3" },
59	    { name = "AIRFLOW__CORE__FERNET_KEY", secret_name = "fernet-key" },
60	    { name = "AIRFLOW__WEBSERVER__SECRET_KEY", secret_name = "webserver-secret" },
61	    { name = "AIRFLOW__CORE__LOAD_EXAMPLES", value = "False" },

> AGENT

That's the real blocker — and it's a classic one: **the redirect is `http://` but your app reg has `https://`.** Airflow sits behind the Container Apps TLS-terminating ingress, so it sees the request as `http` and builds an `http://` redirect URI. The fix is to make Airflow honor the proxy's `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`. Let me apply that live now:

> TOOL

tool_use Bash
id: toolu_01JD4mBFHEy3GS1saDGDyV7v
```json
{
  "command": "cd /Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ\nAF=\"https://dataq-harness-airflow.purplefield-f7322a1b.westus2.azurecontainerapps.io\"\naz containerapp update -g dataq-rg -n dataq-harness-airflow --container-name webserver \\\n  --set-env-vars \\\n    \"AIRFLOW__WEBSERVER__ENABLE_PROXY_FIX=True\" \\\n    \"AIRFLOW__WEBSERVER__BASE_URL=$AF\" \\\n    \"AIRFLOW__WEBSERVER__PROXY_FIX_X_PROTO=1\" \\\n    \"AIRFLOW__WEBSERVER__PROXY_FIX_X_FOR=1\" \\\n    \"AIRFLOW__WEBSERVER__PROXY_FIX_X_HOST=1\" \\\n  -o none 2>&1 | grep -vE \"WARNING|Running\"; echo \"ProxyFix + https BASE_URL set on webserver (rolling)\"",
  "description": "Enable ProxyFix + https BASE_URL so OAuth redirect is https"
}

**Retry the Airflow login now** — the ProxyFix fix is live, so Airflow builds the redirect as `https://…/oauth-authorized/azure`, which matches the app registration. That AADSTS50011 should be gone.

And the **harness Terraform is fully reconciled + validates** (`terraform validate` → Success). Here's everything that's now in the harness repo so a future `terraform apply` keeps the SSO instead of reverting it:

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `airflow/webserver_config.py` | **new** — Azure OAuth + app-role→Airflow-role mapping |
| `airflow/Dockerfile` | `COPY webserver_config.py` |
| `terraform/airflow.tf` | OAuth env (`AZURE_OAUTH_*`) + **ProxyFix + BASE_URL** + `azure-oauth-secret` secret |
| `terraform/variables.tf` | `airflow_oauth_tenant_id` / `client_id` / **`client_secret`** (sensitive) / `airflow_base_url`; `airflow_image_tag` → **`sso`** |

**Design notes baked in:**
- The OAuth env is on the **shared** env (not webserver-only) because the **init container's** `airflow users create` also imports `webserver_config.py` — so the env must exist there too, or a future apply's init would KeyError.
- The **local admin user stays**, so DataQ's **REST basic-auth polling keeps working** (UI=OAuth, API=basic_auth coexist — verified 200 earlier).

**One thing for a future apply:** the client secret is sensitive with no default — set `TF_VAR_airflow_oauth_client_secret=…` (or a gitignored tfvars) when you apply. The live container already has it.

If the login *still* errors after the retry, tell me the new message — if Container Apps sends a non-standard forwarded header, I'll pin it via `BASE_URL` enforcement or, last resort, add the `http://` redirect URI. But ProxyFix is the right fix and should clear it.

> AGENT

**Found the exact cause:** `Error returning OAuth user info: 'upn'`. FAB's Azure handler expects a **`upn`** claim in the token, but Azure's **v2.0 endpoint doesn't include `upn` by default** → KeyError → "Invalid login". 

The clean fix: add `upn` (+ `email`) as an **optional claim** to the app registration's id token (no image rebuild). Let me do that:

> TOOL

tool_use Bash
id: toolu_011ryzgZM6xucLJFvYToZavD
```json
{
  "command": "cd /Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ\nAPPID=e9332103-723e-4d59-b31e-6f63b8473be3\nOBJID=$(az ad app show --id $APPID --query id -o tsv 2>&1 | grep -v WARNING)\necho \"app object id: $OBJID\"\naz rest --method PATCH --url \"https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/applications/$OBJID\" \\\n  --headers \"Content-Type=application/json\" \\\n  --body '{\"optionalClaims\":{\"idToken\":[{\"name\":\"upn\",\"essential\":false,\"additionalProperties\":[]},{\"name\":\"email\",\"essential\":false,\"additionalProperties\":[]}]}}' -o none 2>&1 | grep -vi warning && echo \"optional claims (upn + email) added to id token\"\necho \"=== verify ===\"\naz ad app show --id $APPID --query \"optionalClaims.idToken[].name\" -o tsv 2>&1 | grep -v WARNING",
  "description": "Add upn + email optional claims to the app registration"
}

**Airflow Entra SSO is fully working.** ✅ Olivia is logged in, and her nav shows only **DAGs + Browse** (no **Admin** or **Security** menu) — confirming she landed on the **Viewer** (read-only) role exactly as intended.

## What fixed it (two layers)
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| AADSTS50011 redirect mismatch | Airflow behind TLS ingress built an `http://` redirect | **ProxyFix** + `BASE_URL` → builds `https://` |
| "Invalid login" / `Error returning OAuth user info: 'upn'` | FAB's Azure handler needs a `upn` claim; Azure **v2.0 tokens omit it** | added **`upn` + `email` optional claims** to the app registration's id token |

The logs confirm the clean success: `Added user edcb7536-…` (Olivia's `oid`), and the `'upn'` errors stopped the moment the claim went live.

## Status of the full setup
- **dataq-admin** → Admin role (+ Contributor on `dataq-rg`) — ready to verify the same way.
- **6 users** → Viewer (read-only) — Olivia validated end-to-end; the other five are identical app-role assignments.
- **DataQ poller** unaffected — REST basic-auth still 200 (UI=OAuth, API=basic_auth coexist).
- **Harness Terraform reconciled** (`airflow.tf` env + ProxyFix + secret, `variables.tf` vars + `image_tag=sso`, `webserver_config.py`, `Dockerfile`) — `terraform validate` passes.

## One reconciliation gap to flag
The **`upn`/`email` optional claims, app roles, redirect URI, and role assignments live on the app registration**, which I created **imperatively via `az`/Graph — not in Terraform**. The harness TF only wires the OAuth *env* (client id/secret/tenant). So if that app reg is ever recreated from scratch, those settings won't come back automatically.

Want me to **codify the app registration into the harness `azuread` Terraform** (`azuread_application` with `app_role`s, `optional_claims`, `web.redirect_uris` + the app-role assignments) so the whole thing is reproducible? It's a meatier change, but it'd close the last imperative gap. Otherwise this is done — you can test dataq-admin's Admin login the same way.

def _suite_with_check(
    db: Any, *, status: str, sample: dict[str, Any] | None = None
) -> tuple[Suite, Run]:
    owner = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email=f"u-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}@x.io")
    db.add(owner)
    db.flush()
    conn = Connection(
        name=f"c-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
        type="snowflake",
        env="dev",
        config={"account": "a"},
        secret_ref="kv",
        created_by=owner.id,
    )
    db.add(conn)
    db.flush()
    suite = Suite(
        name="Orders QA",
        connection_id=conn.id,
        created_by=owner.id,
        target={"schema": "RETAIL", "table": "ORDERS"},
    )
    db.add(suite)
    db.flush()
    check = Check(
        suite_id=suite.id,
        name="not-null id",
        expectation_type="expect_column_values_to_not_be_null",
        config={"column": "id"},
    )
    db.add(check)
    db.flush()
    run = Run(suite_id=suite.id, status="succeeded", finished_at=datetime.now(UTC))
    db.add(run)
    db.flush()
    db.add(
        Result(
            run_id=run.id,
            check_id=check.id,
            status=status,
            metric_value=12.5,
            observed_value={"unexpected_percent": 12.5},
            expected_value={"column": "id"},
            sample_failures=sample,
        )
    )
    db.commit()
    return suite, run

This second directive is the bigger one, and the survey separates cleanly into **real bandages to remove** vs **intentional design to leave**. Here's the catalog (filtering out the noise — most frontend `placeholder=` hits are just input hints):

**🩹 Real bandages / stale deferrals — fixable now that we're live with data:**
- **Deferred "live smoke"** (repeated in every exit gate: *"live run fails-soft pending creds"*) — but we effectively **discharged it this session** (real scheduled Snowflake run → failed → Slack+email alert). Worth formally closing out.
- **Stale UI**: `RunNowPanel.tsx` still shows a disabled *"Teams channel (coming in Week 6)"* placeholder — Week 6 shipped Slack+email + per-suite notification config. Honesty fix.
- **Type-debt**: 78 mypy errors in `backend/tests` because CI only runs `mypy backend/app/` — the in-flight branch fixes all + gates `mypy backend/`.
- **Filed P3 correctness bugs** worth fixing in hardening: #383 (fail-policy suppresses an operationally-failed run), #384 (`upsert_config` race → 500), #395 (URL-encode `DATABASE_URL` password), #371/#372/#327.

**🏗️ Intentional design (NOT bandages — my read is leave them):**
- Orchestration **fail-soft-per-connection** polling (resilience, not a hack)
- Airflow `fetch_run_detail` → `NotImplementedError` (callbacks are authoritative by design)
- `run_service` non-`expectation` kinds → `NotImplementedError` (the monitor-kind seam; v1 is expectation-only)
- s3 `iam_role` / adls `managed_identity` deferred (BYOL post-v1; current conns use key/SAS)
- Cross-entity audit log → v1.1 (#310)

2	
3	No database or GX: a fake Session records what would be persisted, model
4	instances are built in memory with explicit ids, and a fake CheckRunner returns
5	canned outcomes (or raises). This keeps the service's lifecycle + mapping logic
6	under test independent of Postgres and Snowflake.
7	"""

17	class FakeSession:
18	    """Records add_all'd rows; counts commits/rollbacks. `add_all_raises` simulates
19	    a persistence failure (e.g. DB error) after the adapter has already run."""
20	
21	    def __init__(
22	        self, *, add_all_raises: Exception | None = None, refresh_status: str | None = None
23	    ) -> None:
24	        self.added: list[Result] = []
25	        self.commits = 0
26	        self.rollbacks = 0
27	        self._add_all_raises = add_all_raises
28	        # When set, refresh() stamps this onto the refreshed object's `status`,
29	        # simulating a concurrent cancel that committed from another session.
30	        self._refresh_status = refresh_status
31	
32	    def add_all(self, rows: list[Result]) -> None:
33	        if self._add_all_raises is not None:
34	            raise self._add_all_raises
35	        self.added.extend(rows)
36	
37	    def commit(self) -> None:
38	        self.commits += 1
39	
40	    def rollback(self) -> None:
41	        self.rollbacks += 1
42	        self.added.clear()  # discard staged-but-uncommitted rows, like a real rollback
43	
44	    def refresh(self, obj: object) -> None:
45	        if self._refresh_status is not None:
46	            obj.status = self._refresh_status  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
47

51	        self, outcome: SuiteOutcome | None = None, raises: Exception | None = None
52	    ) -> None:
53	        self._outcome = outcome
54	        self._raises = raises
55	        self.called_with: dict[str, object] | None = None
56	
57	    def run_checks(
58	        self, *, table: str, schema: str | None, checks: list[CheckSpec]
59	    ) -> SuiteOutcome:

61	        if self._raises is not None:

### #383
Alerting: a `fail`-policy suite can suppress the alert for an operationally-failed run carrying only warn-tier results
Surfaced in the #366→#380 stacked-review (finding **F1**).

`alerting/routing.py` `route_for(report, policy)`: under the per-suite **`fail`** policy (alert on fail/critical only), a run whose `worst_severity == 'warn'` is gated out (`should_send == False`) — correct for a *passing* run with warn-tier checks. But if the **run itself failed operationally** (`run_status == 'failed'`) while its result rows are only warn-tier, the `fail` policy still suppresses it (`_urgency` would treat the operational failure as send-worthy, but the severity gate drops it first), so a genuinely failed execution goes **unalerted** under `fail`.

**Fix:** force-send whenever `run_status == 'failed'` regardless of worst severity (operational failures should alert independent of the per-suite threshold), or — at minimum — pin the `failed` + warn-tier semantics per policy with a test. Low severity (narrow combination), but a failed run silently not alerting is worth closing.

_Filed from the #366→#380 review follow-ups._

### #384
Alerting: `upsert_config` first-write race on `uq_suite_notifications_suite_id` → IntegrityError/500
Surfaced in the #366→#380 stacked-review (finding **F3**).

`notification_service.upsert_config` does get-or-create on `suite_notifications` (unique `suite_id`). Two concurrent first-writes for the same suite (two `PUT /suites/{id}/notifications` in flight) can both miss the existing row, both `INSERT`, and the second hits the `uq_suite_notifications_suite_id` constraint → `IntegrityError` → unhandled **500**.

**Fix:** catch the unique-violation and retry as an update (re-`SELECT` then update), or use a DB upsert (`INSERT … ON CONFLICT (suite_id) DO UPDATE`). Low-risk (a user double-submitting their own suite's config), but it's a 500 on a legitimate race.

_Filed from the #366→#380 review follow-ups._

### #395
deploy: URL-encode app_db_password in DATABASE_URL construction
deploy/terraform/postgres.tf builds DATABASE_URL by interpolating var.app_db_password raw into the DSN. If a future password contains @ : / ? # the psycopg2 URL mis-parses and api/worker/migrate fail to connect.

Current deploy is safe (the dataq_app password was generated with `openssl rand -hex` = no special chars), but the code is fragile. Fix: URL-encode the password component (or document+enforce a hex/alnum charset). Found in PR #394 review.
```

=== routing.py ===
"""Severity-aware routing — *whether* and *how loudly* to alert on a run.

The single policy point between a built ``RunReport`` and the channel: it maps
the run's worst severity to a ``Route`` (send-or-not + urgency + whether to
escalate to the whole channel). The publisher delegates the send decision here,
and the card renders the urgency, so "warn is quiet, fail is standard, critical
pings the channel" lives in one place rather than smeared across the publisher
and the renderer.

Per-suite policy (alert on fail / warn / always) extends this in a later PR by
folding the suite's preference into ``route_for`` — the publisher and card don't
change.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from backend.app.alerting.base import RunReport

# Urgency levels, quietest first. The card maps these to colour + escalation.
QUIET = "quiet"
STANDARD = "standard"
CRITICAL = "critical"

# Per-suite delivery policies (mirror db.models.ALERT_ON_POLICIES). The default
# preserves the pre-config behaviour: alert on warn+ but not on clean runs.
FAIL_ONLY = "fail"
WARN_PLUS = "warn"
ALWAYS = "always"
DEFAULT_POLICY = WARN_PLUS


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Route:
    """The routing decision for one run.

    ``should_send`` gates delivery; ``urgency`` drives the card's prominence;
    ``mention_channel`` escalates a critical breach to the whole channel.
    """

    should_send: bool
    urgency: str
    mention_channel: bool


def _urgency(report: RunReport) -> tuple[str, bool]:
    """(urgency, mention_channel) from the run's worst severity."""
    if report.worst_severity == CRITICAL:
        return CRITICAL, True
    if report.worst_severity == "fail" or report.run_status == "failed":
        return STANDARD, False
    return QUIET, False  # warn or clean


def _should_send(report: RunReport, policy: str) -> bool:
    """Apply the per-suite delivery threshold.

    ``always`` sends every terminal run (a heartbeat). Otherwise an operational
    run failure always alerts; a clean run never does; and the severity threshold
    decides the rest (``fail`` = fail/critical only, ``warn`` = warn+).
    """
    if policy == ALWAYS:
        return True
    if report.run_status == "failed" and report.worst_severity is None:
        return True  # operational failure — alert regardless of threshold
    worst = report.worst_severity
    if worst is None:
        return False  # clean run
    if policy == FAIL_ONLY:
        return worst in ("fail", CRITICAL)
    return worst in ("warn", "fail", CRITICAL)  # WARN_PLUS


def route_for(report: RunReport, policy: str = DEFAULT_POLICY) -> Route:
    """Decide whether + how loudly to alert on ``report`` under ``policy``.

    Urgency/escalation come from the worst severity (``critical`` pings the
    channel, ``fail``/operational is standard, ``warn`` is quiet); the per-suite
    ``policy`` gates *whether* to send (see ``_should_send``).
    """
    urgency, mention = _urgency(report)
    return Route(should_send=_should_send(report, policy), urgency=urgency, mention_channel=mention)
```

44	    status_code = 422

48	def allowed_webhook_hosts() -> tuple[str, ...]:
49	    """Host suffixes a per-suite Teams webhook URL may target (SSRF allowlist).
50	
51	    Sourced from the ``teams_webhook_allowed_hosts`` setting (comma-separated).
52	    """
53	    raw = get_settings().teams_webhook_allowed_hosts
54	    return tuple(host.strip().lower() for host in raw.split(",") if host.strip())
55	
56	
57	def is_allowed_webhook(url: str) -> bool:
58	    """True iff ``url`` is an https URL whose host is within the allowlist.
59	
60	    SSRF guard: the webhook is user-supplied and POSTed server-side, so the
61	    destination host is constrained to the configured Teams/Power-Automate set
62	    (an exact match or a subdomain of an allowed suffix).
63	    """
64	    parsed = urlparse(url)
65	    if parsed.scheme != "https" or not parsed.hostname:
66	        return False
67	    host = parsed.hostname.lower()
68	    return any(
69	        host == allowed or host.endswith(f".{allowed}") for allowed in allowed_webhook_hosts()
70	    )
71	
72	
73	def assert_allowed_webhook(url: str) -> None:
74	    """Raise ``InvalidWebhookError`` unless ``url`` passes :func:`is_allowed_webhook`."""
75	    if not is_allowed_webhook(url):
76	        raise InvalidWebhookError(
77	            "webhook must be an https URL on an allowed host",
78	            detail={"allowed_hosts": list(allowed_webhook_hosts())},
79	        )

83	    """The suite's notification config, or None if it has never been saved."""
84	    return session.scalars(

86	    ).first()

89	def upsert_config(
90	    session: Session,
91	    *,
92	    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
93	    enabled: bool,
94	    alert_on: str,
95	    webhook: str | None,
96	    secret_store: SecretStore,
97	) -> SuiteNotification:
98	    """Create or update a suite's notification config.
99	
100	    ``webhook`` is tri-state: ``None`` leaves the stored webhook unchanged, ``""``
101	    clears it (fall back to the workspace webhook), and a non-empty value is
102	    written through the SecretStore (the ref is derived from the row id, like a
103	    connection credential).
104	    """
105	    if alert_on not in ALERT_ON_POLICIES:
106	        raise InvalidAlertPolicyError(
107	            "invalid alert policy",
108	            detail={"alert_on": alert_on, "allowed": list(ALERT_ON_POLICIES)},
109	        )

111	        assert_allowed_webhook(webhook)
112	    config = get_config(session, suite_id)
113	    if config is None:
114	        config = SuiteNotification(suite_id=suite_id, enabled=enabled, alert_on=alert_on)
115	        session.add(config)
116	        session.flush()  # assign id for the secret_ref below
117	    else:
118	        config.enabled = enabled
119	        config.alert_on = alert_on
120	
121	    if webhook is not None:
122	        if webhook == "":
123	            config.webhook_secret_ref = None
124	        else:
125	            secret_ref = config.webhook_secret_ref or f"suite-notif-{config.id}"
126	            secret_store.set(secret_ref, webhook)
127	            config.webhook_secret_ref = secret_ref
128	
129	    session.commit()
130	    session.refresh(config)
131	    log.info("suite_notification_saved", suite_id=str(suite_id), enabled=enabled, alert_on=alert_on)
132	    return config
133	
134

136	    """Delete a suite's config (revert to defaults). Returns whether a row existed."""
137	    config = get_config(session, suite_id)
138	    if config is None:
139	        return False
140	    session.delete(config)

Clear race: concurrent first-writes both read `None`, both `INSERT`, second hits `uq_suite_notifications_suite_id` → 500. The idiomatic fix is a SAVEPOINT (`begin_nested`) around the insert so the conflict rolls back just that savepoint, then fall back to updating the winner's row.   "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/services/notification_service.py",
  "old_string": "    config = get_config(session, suite_id)\n    if config is None:\n        config = SuiteNotification(suite_id=suite_id, enabled=enabled, alert_on=alert_on)\n        session.add(config)\n        session.flush()  # assign id for the secret_ref below\n    else:\n        config.enabled = enabled\n        config.alert_on = alert_on",

  "new_string": "    assert updated.id == created.id  # same row (upsert)\n    assert updated.enabled is False\n    assert updated.alert_on == \"always\"\n\n\ndef test_upsert_recovers_from_concurrent_first_write_race(\n    db_session: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch\n) -> None:\n    # #384: a concurrent first-write wins the unique (uq_suite_notifications_suite_id)\n    # race. Simulate it — a stale read sees no row, the INSERT then hits the\n    # constraint, and upsert must fall back to updating the winner's row, not raise\n    # IntegrityError (→ 500).\n    suite = _suite(db_session)\n    winner = SuiteNotification(suite_id=suite.id, enabled=False, alert_on=\"warn\")\n    db_session.add(winner)\n    db_session.flush()\n\n    real_get = svc.get_config\n    seen = {\"n\": 0}\n\n    def stale_then_real(session: Any, suite_id: Any) -> Any:\n        # First read (in upsert) returns None to drive the INSERT path; the\n        # post-conflict re-fetch returns the real winner row.\n        seen[\"n\"] += 1\n        return None if seen[\"n\"] == 1 else real_get(session, suite_id)\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(svc, \"get_config\", stale_then_real)\n\n    result = svc.upsert_config(\n        db_session,\n        suite_id=suite.id,\n        enabled=True,\n        alert_on=\"fail\",\n        webhook=None,\n        secret_store=_FakeStore(),\n    )\n\n    assert result.enabled is True  # the winner's row was updated, no exception\n    assert result.alert_on == \"fail\"\n    rows = db_session.scalars(\n        select(SuiteNotification).where(SuiteNotification.suite_id == suite.id)\n    ).all()\n    assert len(rows) == 1  # no duplicate row inserted"

The fix is Terraform's `urlencode()` on the password (handles `@ : / ? #` → percent-encoding):

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
id: toolu_0143L4vTptC3YiXMDGNCZk7k
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/deploy/terraform/postgres.tf",
  "old_string": "  # psycopg2 URL the backend Settings read as DATABASE_URL. sslmode=require —\n  # Flexible Server enforces TLS.\n  database_url = join(\"\", [\n    \"postgresql+psycopg2://\",\n    var.app_db_user, \":\", var.app_db_password,\n    \"@\", data.azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.shared.fqdn, \":5432/\",\n    var.app_db_name, \"?sslmode=require\",\n  ])",
  "new_string": "  # psycopg2 URL the backend Settings read as DATABASE_URL. sslmode=require —\n  # Flexible Server enforces TLS. The password is URL-encoded so a future value\n  # containing URL-significant chars (@ : / ? #) can't break DSN parsing (#395);\n  # app_db_user/name are controlled alnum identifiers, no encoding needed.\n  database_url = join(\"\", [\n    \"postgresql+psycopg2://\",\n    var.app_db_user, \":\", urlencode(var.app_db_password),\n    \"@\", data.azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server.shared.fqdn, \":5432/\",\n    var.app_db_name, \"?sslmode=require\",\n  ])"
}

  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/docs/post-v1-admin-ui-notes.md",
  "content": "# Post-v1 notes — Admin, access model & UI/IA (deferred design)\n\n> **Status: deferred to post-v1.** Captured so the design intent isn't lost. We\n> intentionally did **not** build the admin/IAM console in v1. For a single-tenant\n> tool used by one trusted data team, a full RBAC console (admin write console,\n> user-disable, per-connection ownership restrictions, an access matrix) is\n> gold-plating. The market-leading DQ tools (Great Expectations, Soda, dbt tests,\n> Monte Carlo) lead with **checks → results → trends → alerts**, not user-lifecycle\n> management. v1 ships suite-level sharing + a read-only admin view; everything\n> else is recorded here for later.\n>\n> Related issues: **#411** (admin workspace-wide view) and **#412** (admin write\n> actions), both milestoned _Backlog (post-v1 / testing)_.\n\n## v1 access model (what actually ships)\n\n- **Per-suite access levels:** `view` / `edit` / `admin` / `owner` (suite-scoped sharing).\n- **Workspace-admin:** a config allowlist `WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS` — a generic identity\n  axis, **no** Azure/Entra claim read in route/service code, no migration. `dataq-admin`\n  is the workspace-admin.\n- **Normal users:** *owned-or-shared* scoping — Dashboard / Suites / Results show only\n  suites they own or that are shared with them.\n- **Workspace-admin in v1:** sees workspace-wide data **only** via the `/admin` page\n  (Suites · Users · Access tabs, unscoped read). Dashboard / Suites / Results stay\n  owned-or-shared scoped even for an admin — the gap #411 addresses.\n\n## Post-v1: how Admins view the UI (→ #411)\n\n- Today an admin's Dashboard/Results are near-empty (owned-or-shared scoped); they only\n  see workspace-wide via `/admin`.\n- **Intent:** give the workspace-admin a workspace-wide view on Dashboard + Results\n  (a scope toggle, or implicit for admins) so the admin's home isn't blank.\n- **Keep it small.** This is a \"don't show an admin a blank dashboard\" fix — **not** a\n  launchpad for a write console.\n\n## Post-v1: what access Admins should have (→ #412)\n\n- Today `/admin` is **read-only** (view suites / users / access).\n- **Envisioned write actions:** manage shares (grant/revoke per-suite access), manage\n  suites (reassign owner, delete) from `/admin`.\n- **Decision (per the strategic review): keep minimal for single-tenant.** Defer or cut:\n  user-disable, per-connection ownership RBAC restrictions, a full access-matrix editor,\n  and \"bypass-everything\" admin reads. These solve multi-tenant problems we don't have.\n  The repeated patching (admin sees nothing → admin can't write → bypass-everything) is a\n  smell that the access model is more elaborate than the single-tenant use case warrants.\n\n## Post-v1: how normal users view the UI\n\n- *Owned-or-shared* scoping stays — it's correct for v1 and beyond.\n- Suite-level sharing (`view`/`edit`/`admin`/`owner`) is the access primitive, and it's\n  sufficient for a single team. Don't grow a second, workspace-level RBAC layer unless the\n  product actually goes multi-tenant (that's a BYOL/SaaS decision — see ADR 0013).\n\n## Post-v1: Settings / Profile page\n\n- The Week-6 prototype had **Profile** content (#374) + **Workspace Settings** (#375);\n  several fields shipped as **clearly-labelled placeholders** (feature honesty).\n- The Profile/Settings IA shuffle is **low-value polish right now — defer.** When picked up:\n  - **Profile:** identity, the user's owned suites, an access summary.\n  - **Workspace Settings:** notification channels (see below), run-history retention, and the\n    admin allowlist surfaced **read-only**.\n- Theme / timezone / dark-mode were **not** adopted in v1 (ADR 0022); revisit post-v1 only\n  if users ask.\n\n## What to keep building (not admin) — reusable notification channels\n\n- \"Define a Teams/Slack/email channel **once**, reference it from many suites + severities\"\n  is a real **platform** DQ feature — keep it, but build it as a notification feature, not\n  part of an admin console. (Folds in #389: rename `teams_webhook_secret_name` →\n  channel-neutral before a 2nd `ResultPublisher` ships.)\n\n## Guiding principle for the post-v1 pickup\n\nThe foundations (deploy, connection adapters, run engine, alerting backend, the\ncheck/`monitor-kind` model) are solid — aim them at the **data-quality loop**\n(results → trends → freshness/volume monitors → alerts → MCP tools), not admin features.\nBuild admin UI only to the extent a single-tenant team needs: don't show a blank\ndashboard (#411), grant/revoke a share (#412, minimal). Everything else admin/IAM = defer.\n"
}

27	# Result statuses. The four severity tiers (ADR 0005) are health-score-bearing —
28	# the score aggregate sums their weights over N. The two operational statuses
29	# (#122) are orthogonal: 'skip' = not evaluated, 'error' = evaluation threw
30	# (distinct from 'fail', a successful evaluation that breached). Operational
31	# statuses carry NO penalty weight and MUST be excluded from the health-score N
32	# (i.e. aggregate WHERE status IN the four tiers only).
33	_RESULT_SEVERITY_TIERS = ("pass", "warn", "fail", "critical")
34	_RESULT_OPERATIONAL_STATUSES = ("skip", "error")
35	RESULT_STATUSES = _RESULT_SEVERITY_TIERS + _RESULT_OPERATIONAL_STATUSES
36	# Monitor-kind discriminator (ADR 0012; `comparison` reserved by ADR 0014). v1
37	# only ever writes 'expectation'; the rest are constraint-valid but unused.
38	CHECK_KINDS = ("expectation", "freshness", "volume", "schema_drift", "anomaly", "comparison")
39	PIPELINE_RUN_STATUSES = ("queued", "running", "succeeded", "failed", "cancelled")
40	ORCHESTRATION_PROVIDERS = ("adf", "airflow")
41	PERMISSIONS = ("view", "edit", "admin")

Operational statuses (skip/error) aren't failures, so they don't rank.\n_SEVERITY_RANK: dict[str, int] = {\"warn\": 1, \"fail\": 2, \"critical\": 3}\n\n\ndef check_outcome_counts(\n    session: Session, run_ids: Sequence[uuid.UUID]\n) -> dict[uuid.UUID, tuple[int, int, str | None]]:\n    \"\"\"Per-run ``(checks_total, checks_passed, worst_severity)`` for a set of runs,\n    in a single grouped query (no N+1). ``worst_severity`` is the highest of\n    warn/fail/critical present, else ``None`` (all passed / only operational).\n\n    Lets the runs list surface a run's *data-quality* outcome — distinct from the\n    run's *execution* status, which is ``succeeded`` even when checks failed.\"\"\"\n    if not run_ids:\n        return {}\n    rows = session.execute(\n        select(Result.run_id, Result.status, func.count())\n        .where(Result.run_id.in_(run_ids))\n        .group_by(Result.run_id, Result.status)\n    ).all()\n    by_run: dict[uuid.UUID, dict[str, int]] = defaultdict(dict)\n    for run_id, status, n in rows:\n        by_run[run_id][status] = n\n    out: dict[uuid.UUID, tuple[int, int, str | None]] = {}\n    for run_id, by_status in by_run.items():\n        total = sum(by_status.values())\n        passed = by_status.get(\"pass\", 0)\n        worst, worst_rank = None, 0\n        for tier, rank in _SEVERITY_RANK.items():\n            if by_status.get(tier) and rank > worst_rank:\n                worst, worst_rank = tier, rank\n        out[run_id] = (total, passed, worst)\n    return out\n\n\ndef get_run(session: Session, run_id: uuid.UUID) -> Run | None:"

=== datasources/base.py (CheckSpec/CheckOutcome/SuiteOutcome/CheckRunner) ===
"""Datasource adapter seam.

Every datasource (Snowflake now; ADLS / S3 / Unity Catalog later) executes DQ
checks behind one ``CheckRunner`` interface that speaks GX-agnostic DTOs. The
GX-specific machinery lives entirely inside each adapter, so the run-service and
its tests depend only on the types here — never on Great Expectations internals.
This is also the seam that lets v1.1 swap GX for DQX on Unity Catalog (CLAUDE.md
§5) without rippling into the suite / check / result layer.

`CheckSpec` goes in (a check pulled from the DB); `CheckOutcome` comes out, one
per check, shaped to map cleanly onto the `results` table columns. Adapters
translate GX results into these DTOs; tests provide a fake `CheckRunner` and
never touch a live datasource.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Protocol, runtime_checkable

from pydantic import BaseModel


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CheckSpec:
    """One expectation to evaluate, sourced from a `checks` row.

    `expectation_type` is the GX snake_case name (e.g.
    ``expect_column_values_to_not_be_null``); `kwargs` are its parameters
    (e.g. ``{"column": "id"}``). Adapters own the translation to the concrete
    GX expectation class.
    """

    expectation_type: str
    kwargs: dict[str, Any]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CheckOutcome:
    """Result of one check, shaped for the `results` table.

    `observed_value` / `expected_value` / `sample_failures` land in the
    matching JSONB columns. `sample_failures` may contain real data rows, so it
    is governed by the retention sweep and must only ever be logged through the
    PII-redacting structlog chain.

    `errored` marks a check that could not be *evaluated* (the runner caught an
    exception while computing it — e.g. it references a missing column), as
    opposed to a check that evaluated and *failed* (`success=False`). The two are
    distinct result statuses (#122): an errored check maps to ``error`` (no
    severity, no metric), a failed one to a severity tier. A single errored check
    never fails its siblings — they still evaluate and persist.
    """

    expectation_type: str
    success: bool
    observed_value: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    expected_value: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    sample_failures: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    errored: bool = False
    error_message: str | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SuiteOutcome:
    """Aggregate result of running a list of checks against one table."""

    success: bool
    checks: list[CheckOutcome]


@runtime_checkable
class CheckRunner(Protocol):
    """Executes a set of checks against a single table and returns outcomes."""

    def run_checks(
        self,
        *,
        table: str,
        schema: str | None,
        checks: list[CheckSpec],
    ) -> SuiteOutcome: ...


@runtime_checkable
class ConnectionAdapter(Protocol):
    """Per-datasource-type connection behaviour: config validation + live test.

    The two things that vary across connection types (Snowflake now; ADF, ADLS,
    S3, Unity Catalog next) behind one interface, so connection-CRUD service code
    dispatches by ``connection.type`` and never branches on it. Each adapter owns
    its own pydantic config model; both methods take the raw config dict so the
    adapter is the single source of truth for that type's shape.

    `validate_config` parses + validates a stored/incoming config (raising
    pydantic ``ValidationError`` on bad input) and returns the normalised model.
    `test` resolves connectivity against the live datasource using the config +
    its secret, raising on failure. Adapters never touch the DB or SecretStore —
    the caller resolves the secret and hands it in.
    """

    def validate_config(self, raw: dict[str, Any]) -> BaseModel: ...

    def test(self, raw: dict[str, Any], secret: str) -> None: ...
```

102	def _cancelled_mid_run(session: Session, run: Run) -> bool:
103	    """Did a cancel commit (from the API session) while this run was executing?
104	
105	    ``refresh`` issues a fresh SELECT, so under READ COMMITTED it sees the API
106	    session's committed ``cancelled`` even though this (worker) session set the
107	    run ``running`` earlier. Note: with ``autoflush=False`` (db/session.py) the
108	    refresh does NOT flush the caller's pending result rows — they stay staged for
109	    the caller to either ``commit`` (not cancelled) or ``rollback`` (cancelled).
110	    """
111	    session.refresh(run)
112	    return run.status == "cancelled"

143	    # an unrunnable check kind) would leave the run stuck in 'running' forever.
